new_result.comment: STEP 3 (WSLIVE) helper: inspect a correlated Direction-A reply and, if it carries the unified endpoint-liveness ghost code 'unknown_endpoint' (emitted by the broker on a targeted resolve-miss / dead forward, or by the SW on a targeted-frame map-miss/purge -- AMENDMENT A), raise a distinct actionable NetworkError naming the ghost + the remedy (the tab was asked to re-register; retry). No auto-retry here (REV3): the broker's detection-site re-register broadcast is the heal and the next identical call is the retry. A non-ghost reply passes through untouched.

Generic MCP-initiated WS request/response over the broker: stamps a unique request_id, sends the frame (optionally target_tab OR target_endpoint_id), and consumes ONLY the matching reply off the shared queue (dropping foreign frames). Extracted from workflowy_glimpse so every Direction-A call (GLIMPSE, get_extension_settings, ...) shares one correlation impl. STEP 3 (WSLIVE): a correlated reply carrying code:'unknown_endpoint' is raised as a distinct actionable NetworkError via _raise_if_unknown_endpoint (never returned as data). WSLIVE2 (caller-intent routing): a caller holding a REAL endpoint_id passes target_endpoint_id (NOT laundered through target_tab), so the broker routes via resolve_target_endpoint and a miss is the unknown_browser_endpoint liveness ghost (heal + re-register) rather than an unknown_target_tab routing error; target_endpoint_id wins over target_tab if both are passed.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS call: ask the target Workflowy tab for its LIVE extension settings (note-session tags, global tags, default note-sessions parent UUID). Fails loudly if no tab. The second-ever MCP->browser request after GLIMPSE.

Gather ALL trailing #tags found by walking a session node's descendants, using the canonical emoji-aware split_name_and_tags parser (NEVER reads the note field). Returns a de-duped, first-seen-ordered list including the note-session tag(s) themselves.

Pure root->node Show-Path renderer reusing the same cache parent-chain walk as _resolve_uuid_path_and_respond (server), returning a list of name lines (HTML-unescaped) instead of sending a WS frame. Shared by list_note_sessions output.

Return anchors in Workflowy VISUAL order via a nested-priority DFS of the cache. Default/public mode enumerates GLOBAL anchors only (local anchors are recognized but hidden); private widget flags can include local anchors and add an anchor-only tree + raw-text inventory. Anchor-hood + attributes (local/favorite) are decided by the ONE shared classify_anchor_tags matcher over the FULL family vocabulary (local/favorite/deprecated word lists; --deprecated never confers Dock identity), so listing and boundary can never drift. favorites_only=True switches membership to the ⭐ shortlist: every favorite (global OR local, regardless of show_local), PLUS -- with show_local -- locals reachable from a favorite through an UNBROKEN chain of local Docks (an intervening non-favorite GLOBAL Dock cuts the chain and is connective; non-local non-favorite descendants of a favorite are hidden). Zero favorites in the vault -> favorites_fallback: the full list, flagged, with a composed favorite_tag_hint + favorites_notice. Rows/tree nodes carry is_favorite; the result echoes favorite_count / total_dock_count / shown counts. This is anchor inventory, NOT a Stage-1/Stage-2 render.

Create one plain note-session node (name = description + trailing union of session tag(s) + extra_tags; note = detail) under parent_uuid via ETCH. No metadata block, no children. Attribute tags are ONE per attribute (family encoding): when local_postfix / favorite_postfix WORDS are given, _attribute_tags emits <SEP><word> variants as SEPARATE tags appended to EACH anchor/session tag only (NOT extra_tags) -- #wfy-ns--local and/or #wfy-ns--fav -- producing a LOCAL anchor (hidden from list_anchors, still a descendants boundary) and/or a FAVORITE anchor (the dock.list ⭐ shortlist); neither word -> the bare tag, byte-for-byte the prior behavior. Guards the PARENT via _classify_node_map_state: a FOLDER parent is REJECTED with an actionable message (map to a FILE first); FILE/INSIDE_FILE parents are allowed but carry a mapped_subtree_warning (F12+3 to persist); UNMAPPED (the normal case for a plain note-sessions parent) is allowed silently. Returns whatever ETCH returns.

new_result.role: ⚡ add_to_anchor(self, parent_uuid: str, nodes, tags, note_file, content, name)
new_result.comment: Guarded capture wrapper around workflowy_etch: etch one or many nodes under an anchor (parent_uuid) AFTER the shared placement guard (_anchor_target_guard_error) confirms the target is not a FOLDER and not a NON-Markdown mapped file. Fails CLOSED on an uncached parent. Surfaces a mapped_subtree F12+3 advisory when the parent is a Markdown file / inside Markdown. This is the ONLY value-add over calling workflowy_etch directly (the guard); dialect-neutral by design (the anchor's dialect -- todo/note/brainstorm/etc -- is unknown at call time). THREE payload forms, EXACTLY ONE required (loud on both/neither -- deliberately unlike workflowy_etch's nodes_file, which silently WINS over inline nodes): `nodes` (an ETCH forest) XOR `note_file` (an absolute-path UTF-8 text file -> exactly ONE node: file STEM = NAME, raw text = NOTE, normalized at the edge via _node_payload_from_note_file so the funnel is untouched; filename-embedded #tags REJECTED -- tags must go through tags=; a leading '[ap_CORE]' filename handle is canonicalized to '[ap:CORE]') XOR `content` (a raw string -- write_file-parity -- with REQUIRED `name`; normalized at the edge via _node_payload_from_content into ONE node: name = NAME verbatim, content = NOTE verbatim; a trailing #tag in name is ALLOWED since it is directly authored). OPTIONAL `name` with note_file: overrides the stem as the node name (stem-derived tag-region check + AP-ID transform SKIPPED).

Edit an existing anchor: rename its TOPIC and/or replace its DESCRIPTION (note). The rename runs the ONE protected-name composer on ONE live snapshot (never a stale cache name): supplied trailing #tags or an added/changed leading [ap:] handle are loud errors; existing tags + AP-ID are preserved automatically. Refuses non-anchor nodes via the ONE shared classify_anchor_tags matcher on is_anchor -- so a LOCAL anchor (#wfy-ns--local) is editable exactly like a global one (locality only hides it from list_anchors, never from editing). Leaves any Cartographer metadata untouched and flags when the node lives in a mapped subtree (advise F12+3) -- never reconciles disk.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS read: ask the target tab for its LIVE slice-group config (expand_groups [each {id,name,prefixes,root_uuid,description}], active_group, the three F8 postfix words, the global-never-expand list, and the tiny Anchor Dock tag/local-postfix vocabulary needed by one-read LensSpec Stage 0). Same page-side handler the F8 copy button's nested read uses; the server is the single settings reader for the slice-group MCP tools.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS read answered by the BROKER ITSELF (not a tab): stamps a request_id and sends action=broker_status; the broker replies broker_status_result with its live registry snapshot (browser connections, endpoints incl. seconds_since_seen + is_default, default endpoint, MCP clients incl. is_primary, primary id). Rides the same request_id correlation rail as GLIMPSE. NOT tab-specific -- there is no target_tab and no tab_optional; the broker answers directly (like ping->pong), so it works even with zero browser tabs connected. Backs the workflowy_broker_status observability tool.

MCP-initiated Direction-A WS write: hand the target tab the FULL canonical expand_groups array + active_group id to persist (the server did all policy/normalization). The tab persists via its own persistExpandGroups path (atomic storage write + broadcast) and ACKs with the re-normalized groups. The ONLY server->tab write path for slice groups.

new_result.role: ⚡ workflowy_scry(self, node_id: str, use_efficient_traversal: bool, depth, size_limit: int, output_file)
new_result.comment: SCRY includes the requested root and its note. Size truncation explicitly reserves the root before retaining descendants (flat export order is not traversal order); file output delegates to the existing bulk exporter, which retains the root note alongside root identity. No second root fetch or cache path. Chain-1 W4 (F5): in a SINK operation (output_file) whose root names a visible archived node, the total-miss fall-through RAISES the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal before the exporter — never the historical zero-node file-mode success with no file; non-sink reads keep today's flow (the fallback re-run serves archived roots).

LAYER-4 snippet EXTRACTION -- the back half split out of beacon_get_code_snippet (Commit 2). Given an ALREADY-RESOLVED node (resolved via Layer 1 by the caller), it owns everything downstream of handle resolution: parse the node's BEACON/AST_QUALNAME/MD_PATH note, walk ancestors over nodes_by_id to the enclosing FILE (Path:) node, resolve the on-disk absolute path, and delegate to beacon_obtain_code_snippet for language-specific (AST/span/MD_PATH/text) snippet extraction. Holds NO handle-resolution logic (that is Layer 1). beacon_node_id is passed through purely for provenance/error framing; beacon_node is the resolved node dict; nodes_by_id is the SAME map used to resolve (no reload). This is the shape the step-7 site inside read_text_snippet_by_symbol already needed: extraction from an already-resolved UUID. A FILE node ALWAYS spans the whole file: when the resolved node IS the enclosing FILE node, or its derived name token equals the file's basename, the anchored name search is skipped and the whole-file file_top path runs ([ap:803VZI]) -- a file that names itself (module docstring) can no longer collapse the span to one line.
JS/TS AST_QUALNAME resolution - mirrors Python AST_QUALNAME handling for JS/TS files

new_result.role: ⚡ read_text_snippet_by_symbol(self, file_path, symbol: str, symbol_kind: str, context: int, *, return_candidates_only, suppress_tags, scope_root_ids)
⚡ read_uuid_from_symbol(self, file_path, symbol: str, symbol_kind: str, *, suppress_tags, scope_root_ids)

new_result.comment: Thin client method for the AP-ID resolver ([ap:APRSLV3]). The pure-Workflowy twin of read_uuid_from_symbol: resolves an [ap:XXXXXX] anchor-point handle to its Workflowy UUID(s) for plain (non-disk-backed) nodes that the symbol resolver correctly cannot match. Delegates VERBATIM to the shared module-level resolve_uuid_from_anchor_point(client=self) so the single resolution pipeline is reused everywhere (MCP tool + forthcoming [ap:APFAMILY2] anchor-point family + [ap:APCHILD] add_to_anchor-by-AP-ID). Cache-only, read-only.

LAYER-3 UNIVERSAL BOUNDARY RESOLVER -- THE single arbitration loop for UUID / AP-ID / symbol handles, shared by tag/mutator callers and resolve_node_identity_record (all three resolve verbs). Delegates mechanics to Layer 1 / the AP primitive / Layer 2 or the injectable async symbol_runner (beacon's scoped/suppressed leg). The DEFAULT symbol leg honours the global suppression list too ([ap:7ORCPL]): when the caller passes suppress_tags_provider (the tag and mutator fronts do), the leg awaits it ONLY when it actually runs -- after the UUID and AP-ID legs came back unresolved -- and drops suppressed candidates before the 0/1/N decision; without a provider the leg stays unfiltered (the established tri-state, other callers unchanged). Default order remains [prefer] + RESOLUTION_DOMAIN_ORDER; domain_order can supply the ruled beacon orders as data. Unique or ambiguous STOPS, only unresolved falls through; self-load failure is unresolved. Existing prefer/allow_* callers retain byte-identical tri-state results. The internal _with_leg_details posture exposes the raw leg extras (AP core, prefix, truncation, symbol/scope fields) and the reused map to the record builder, which never resolves again. No domain loop or primitive calls remain in the record builder. ARCHIVE READS TWO-PHASE (U1): the UUID and AP legs run at universe='live' in the family's order, and ONLY after every allowed domain missed live do they run again at universe='archive' in the same relative order -- the symbol leg NEVER runs on the archive phase (Axiom 12: symbols are live-only). U2 (Axiom 12, §U2.4): the whole archive phase is SKIPPED when prefer='symbol' -- the beacon family's marker (beacon.resolve is the only such caller) -- so beacon.resolve of an archived handle keeps today's 0-match record plus the beacon hint.

Per-file F12+1 refresh implementation (both processes run THIS code). FAIL-CLOSED GUARDS (U5, spec [ap:HFYAG2]): (1) root-validity — raises NetworkError when the resolved source path does not exist, regardless of dry_run, including the unmounted case; a directory Path reroutes to refresh_folder_cartographer_sync which refuses on the same terms. (2b) delete threshold — its one live reconcile_tree call is armed with max_delete_threshold=governance.carto_reconcile_delete_threshold and the per-run force flag, so an emptied/truncated source file cannot delete the FILE node's whole symbol subtree without an explicit override. force is explicit per-run and never defaults True. FILE-NOTE HEADER FRESHNESS (Dan 2026): after a successful map_codebase, an ordinary eligible FILE root receives exactly ONE note-only header update BEFORE the child reconcile — the fresh LINE COUNT merged into the existing note by _merge_file_note_header (owned header only, suffix preserved, legacy Source-SHA1 dropped, deferred portability Path-segment migration rides the same merged write); source_path_override splits, saved MD_PATH dummy blocks, Root:/directory targets and dry runs never touch the note, and a missing/invalid fresh count fails the refresh loudly.
Atomically merge apply-phase progress through the config status authority; retain buffered counters until acknowledged (best-effort).

Per-node F12 journal entry writer. Appends timestamped entries to <source_json>.weave_journal.json under cartographer_file_refresh/. PRIMARY DIAGNOSTIC TARGET for F12+3 timeout investigation: first-entry vs last-entry timestamp delta tells you whether the per-node reconcile loop itself was slow or finished fast (and the timeout is downstream WebSocket/quiescence).

new_result.role: ⚡ update_beacon_from_node(self, node_id: str, name: str, note: str)

new_result.comment: Folder-subtree F12+1 sync implementation (both processes run THIS code). FAIL-CLOSED GUARDS (U5, spec [ap:HFYAG2]): (1) root-validity — raises NetworkError before any write when no Root:/Path: resolved or the resolved root is missing/not a directory/unmounted; fires on dry_run too; there is NO force bypass for an invalid root. (2a) FILE-node delete threshold — after the FILE-scan collection loop and before the per-file refresh loop and the deletion sweep, a missing_count above governance.carto_folder_file_delete_threshold refuses with zero writes unless the run carries an explicit per-run force. The per-file refreshes inside the 2a loop pass force through to refresh_file_node_beacons. force is explicit per-run and never defaults True.

old_result.comment: Local MCP-server request_id demultiplexer for the single server<->broker WebSocket. The BROKER already routes correlated replies to the correct MCP server process; this object performs the SECOND demux layer INSIDE that process: _ws_request_response registers request_id->Future before sending, and websocket_handler.put(...) resolves the exact Future instead of dropping frames through a shared FIFO. Non-correlated / unmatched frames still fall through to the legacy queue for existing consumers. This is what makes nested/concurrent Direction-A calls safe (server->tab command triggers tab->server handler triggers server->tab config read, etc.) without waiters cannibalizing each other's replies.

old_result.role: in-memory job registry for ETCH/NEXUS/CARTO async jobs
old_result.comment: Module-level dict tracking in-memory asyncio jobs (ETCH, NEXUS, CARTO_BULK_APPLY). Populated by _start_background_job, scanned by mcp_job_status. RELEVANT TO F12+3 TIMEOUT INVESTIGATION: when 'MCP died' is observed, one diagnostic question is whether the foreground asyncio task representing _run_carto_bulk_visible_apply_job is still alive in this dict but stuck awaiting a downstream call — inspect via mcp_job_status. Detached CARTO_REFRESH workers do NOT live here; they're tracked via JSON files under cartographer_jobs/.

S03 §7.2 WS-front classification decorator: a browser-initiated WS handler carrying @_ws_cache_boundary(label) is a cache-backed operation front — its whole body runs inside ONE journal-adoption operation boundary (one manifest head end-to-end). Cache-free WS actions carry no decorator and are recorded in tests/coherence_s03b_registry.json.

accessor for last distinctive WebSocket close reason (PayloadTooBig etc)
async grace-wait helper that polls for a live WebSocket peer
old_result.comment: Belt-and-suspenders against MV3 SW idle race. If GLIMPSE arrives while the Chrome service worker is between idle-death and chrome.alarms rescue (~30s cycle), wait up to ~6s for the SW to reconnect rather than fail immediately. Reduces user-perceived dead-window from ~30s worst-case to ~0s.

Path to the shared cross-process cache-refresh skip-toggle state file (wall-clock epoch deadline) in the runtime base dir. Shared by all MCP servers so the toggle is global under multi-server broker routing.
Read the shared skip-toggle wall-clock epoch deadline from disk (0.0 if absent/empty/unreadable). Best-effort; fail-open to 0.0 (toggle OFF).

Return True iff the user-controlled cache-refresh skip toggle is currently active. Reads the SHARED on-disk wall-clock deadline so the toggle is honored regardless of which MCP server (primary) does the work. Best-effort cleanup of the file once expired.
Seconds remaining on the skip toggle, or 0.0 if inactive/expired. Derived from the SHARED on-disk wall-clock deadline.
Enable/disable the shared cross-process cache-refresh skip toggle by writing/removing the wall-clock deadline file. Used by the set_cache_refresh_skip WebSocket handler.
Recover queued final responsibilities when a coordinator task ends before entering its worker; token-guarded receipts remain pending.
Coalesce reasons, fresh-fetch demand and fixed final obligations at one iteration cutoff; return scheduling/skip acknowledgment, never publication success.

Read-only heartbeat artifact merge for scanner/widget triage. Reports fresh/stale/missing/invalid identity and clamped mtime age without influencing persisted status, PID liveness, cancellation, reap, kill, admission, or claim repair.
One admission-mutex serialized inventory; public readable rows remain a list, internal observations retain uncertainty and incarnation provenance.
Admission-mutex cleanup of discharged orphan final-obligation records only; unfinished and retained-row receipts stay pinned for recovery/deduplication.

old_result.role: delete CARTO job JSON/log/folder artifacts for a terminal job
old_result.comment: Shared deletion primitive used by manual job-history clearing. Deletes job JSON, logs_path, and the per-job folder named <YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>_<job-id> when present. Best-effort and never raises to callers.

old_result.role: clear terminal CARTO job history including failed/warning jobs
old_result.comment: Manual known-terminal history cleanup, additionally pinned by unfinished final-publication responsibility and live region claims. Only valid published/skipped exact-incarnation records permit removal; marker deletion uses the same admission mutex.

Directory holding per-job 'final nodes-export refresh' claim files (.refresh_claims/ under the CARTO jobs dir). Co-located with the jobs for config/portability. NOTE: claim files are NOT caught by Phase 1 of _gc_carto_jobs (a non-recursive *.json glob + CARTO_ type filter that a subdir claim file with no type key never matches); they are reaped two ways — age-based by _gc_carto_jobs Phase 3 (mtime sweep of .refresh_claims/*.claim.json), and on-demand by _clear_carto_job_history's manual 'Clear job history' sweep (which deletes every claim whose owning job is not currently active). Claims are tiny idempotency markers, not leases.
Reserve positively terminal exact incarnations in versioned final-obligation records under admission.mutex. Reservation is recoverable responsibility, never publication success.
Persist latched relevance and positive terminal evidence; reconcile restart reservations via existing identity authority, never omission or age.
Serialize before off-loop scan through conservative durable observation and exact final-batch extraction; only positive stop proofs reserve work, execution receipts discharge it.

Exact token/incarnation final obligation transition under admission.mutex; unmatched callbacks release neither durable responsibility nor the live attempt; publication requires new-fetch receipt and adoption.

Watcher and startup trigger adapter for the single A1 governance sweep; supplies configured grace/cooldown values, loud diagnostics, and claim-aware terminal/orphan auxiliary cleanup without introducing a parallel lifecycle loop.

Primary server logger: writes each line to stderr (visible under TypingMind, swallowed under Claude Code) AND appends to a per-PID file under the shared per-user log dir (broker_protocol.server_log_file), so any single MCP server stays observable regardless of host. File sink is on by default, best-effort, never raises; disable via WORKFLOWY_FILE_LOGGING=0.

F3/F2 ancestor-chain WS handler: virtual-UUID (mirror) parsing, /nodes-export cache fetch + dirty-ID advisory, shaped error frames — but the walk and the WHOLE Markdown grammar are delegated to ancestor_path.build_ancestor_path_document, the ONE shared core the node.ancestors MCP verb also calls, so the hotkey and the verb can never drift. The document carries dock.peek-vocabulary right-side markers (⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓ + ▸N/desc/self/tree metrics) plus the 🗺️ mapped-folder / 📄 mapped-file markers with the key at the top, so this handler reads the configured Dock vocabulary via a nested get_extension_settings Direction-A read — which is why websocket_handler TASK-dispatches it (an inline await would deadlock the pump, the list_anchors_for_widget reason).

Derive a safe .md filename from a Workflowy node name for F12+4 materialize. Strips leading decoration/emoji, trailing #tags, illegal filename chars; collapses whitespace to underscores; guarantees a non-empty stem and a .md extension.

F12+4 leading-text fix: if the note's body (after optional YAML frontmatter) starts with prose BEFORE the first Markdown heading, synthesize a leading '# Leading text' H1 above that prose so the pre-heading text is not lost when the note is split into a heading subtree. No-op when the body already opens with a heading or is empty.

F12+4 hygiene: strip a LEADING Cartographer metadata block (MD_PATH: … --- or BEACON (…) … ---) from a node's note before materializing it to a .md. Needed because a Dump-Bay child that was already written back to the primary file via F12+3 carries such a block at the top of its note; without stripping it, that metadata would be written into the new .md as body content (and then split into bogus child nodes). Mirrors markdown_roundtrip._strip_md_path_block / _strip_md_ast_beacon_block but kept local to avoid importing module privates.

Bulk F12+4 helper: classify a node's note as a Cartographer FILE/FOLDER header. Returns ('Root'|'Path', value) or None using the strict first-line-only _extract_path_header_from_note. A folder/path node has a header whose value has no recognized file extension; a file node's value has one (e.g. .md/.py).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a Markdown file (.md/.markdown)? Used by the bulk walk + eligibility classifier to decide whether to recurse INTO a file node (markdown -> yes; any other extension -> skip+prune).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a FILE (has a filename extension) rather than a FOLDER segment? A folder node's Path: is a bare segment (no dot-extension); a file node's Path: ends in an extension. Used to distinguish path/folder nodes (recurse through) from file nodes (skip unless .md). Thin wrapper: the canonical implementation now lives in api_client_nexus (single source of truth, co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note + _classify_node_map_state); imported here via a function-scoped local import to avoid the api_client_nexus->server cycle, mirroring the other unguarded server->client local imports. NO inline fallback copy on purpose: a bool predicate has no safe 'unknown' value (returning False would mislabel a real file node as a folder and misroute the F12 menus), and if api_client_nexus is unimportable the whole server is non-functional anyway -- so we let the import raise loudly rather than keep a divergent second copy of the logic.

FIRST server-queried F12 menu-visibility check. Walks UP the nodes-export cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof, unlike the DOM) to classify the hovered node, then combines that with the client-reported visible/hidden child booleans to decide whether the F12+4 entry appears and which bulk sub-options enable. Returns {show, mode, visible_option_enabled, all_option_enabled, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+4 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_materialize). Reads node_id + has_visible_children/has_hidden_children from the payload, runs _classify_bulk_materialize_eligibility, and echoes the verdict back (with node_id for client-side correlation).

Zoom-proof resolver for F12+3: given ANY node_id, walk UP the /nodes-export cache ancestor chain (which never hides anything, unlike the zoomed-in DOM) to find the enclosing Markdown FILE node. If the node itself IS a markdown FILE node, returns it. Crucially IGNORES the md-in-md temp node's SECOND-line Path: (that node is never a reverse-Markdown target); the true primary file is the enclosing markdown FILE ancestor. Returns the FILE node's UUID, or None when no enclosing markdown file exists (e.g. inside a non-markdown file, or no file at all).

Cache-backed (zoom-proof) eligibility classifier for the BULK F12+3 menu entry. Decision tree is SIMPLER than F12+4 (no submenu for availability, no child-visibility input needed to decide SHOW): a markdown FILE node -> single F12+3 (mode='single', no bulk entry); a node INSIDE a mapped file -> no bulk entry (degenerates to standard single F12+3 on the enclosing file, which the server resolves zoom-safely); any node that is NOT a file node and NOT inside a file (a folder/Root: node OR a plain unmapped Workflowy node) -> bulk. Returns {show, mode, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+3 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_f12p3). Reads node_id, runs _classify_bulk_f12p3_eligibility, echoes the verdict {show,mode,reason,classification} back (with node_id for client-side correlation). No child-visibility input is needed (F12+3 bulk has no availability submenu).

Bulk F12+3 collection walk (source-agnostic, mirrors _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves plumbing). DFS over a tree (client visible-DOM payload OR nodes-export cache subtree) gathering MARKDOWN FILE nodes only. Per-node rules: a markdown FILE node QUALIFIES and we do NOT descend into it (F12+3 regenerates the whole file from its Workflowy subtree); a non-markdown FILE node is skipped+pruned; folder/Root: nodes and plain nodes are recursed THROUGH. Uses the universal first-line-only header classifier, so a md-in-md temp node (Path on line 2) is never mistaken for a file node. Returns ordered list of {id,name} file-node descriptors.

Bulk F12+3 execution handler (action=bulk_generate_markdown). Performs ONE gesture-level /nodes-export freshness read (L9 GESTURE) before any cache walk or child launch, builds the tree (walk_mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; 'all' -> cache subtree via _build_cache_subtree_for_bulk_materialize), runs _collect_bulk_f12p3_markdown_file_nodes to gather every Markdown FILE node, then fires ONE INDEPENDENT detached _start_carto_markdown_generate_job per file (N widget status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan). Every child consumes the one shared gesture snapshot and admits/claims its own region independently; this handler does not block.

WebSocket handler for the docked-modal SERVER render (action=render_markdown_modal). Direction-A request_id rail: composes Markdown STRING(s) on the server from a DOM/captured-tree payload: snapshot -> all row option-Y views, rows_only -> server-authored row list only, single -> one focus_leaf row, rows -> frozen-DOM multi-select minimal covering subtree via _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture. Echoes request_id. Never forces a /nodes-export refresh (detect+warn staleness). TASK-DISPATCHED from the reader loop (U4), and the three SYNCHRONOUS compose_markdown_modal_* calls run via asyncio.to_thread so a large compose cannot monopolize the event loop -- the task's S03 operation-boundary snapshot propagates into the thread (contextvars).

WebSocket handler for the slice-group copy button (action=compile_slice_search). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id). TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) so it can do a NESTED Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the ORIGINATING tab without deadlocking the single websocket_handler pump. Reads the live slice-group config from that tab, resolves the requested group_id (or active group), and compiles the Workflowy membership search string via the single Python compiler compile_slice_search_expression (#P -#P--deprecated OR ...). Replies compile_slice_search_result with request_id + expression.

WebSocket handler for the live F8 keypress (action=f8_expansion_plan). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id) carrying the visible DOM subtree. TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab to read the active slice group's prefixes + the live postfix config (one settings reader, no client-side policy). Then runs Phase 0 (validate_subtree_against_cache, fail-closed) and Phase 2 (build_expansion_plan) over the validated visible tree and replies f8_expansion_plan_result (echoing request_id) with {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand, warnings} for the client to execute mechanically. No fallback: on validation failure or no live tab it replies with an error the client surfaces loudly.

Apply-slice Tier-1 handler (action=render_slice_modal): the docked Markdown modal sourced from the CACHE-PROJECTED slice group instead of the live virtualized DOM. Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id); TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_f8_expansion_plan / _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab, which would deadlock the single websocket_handler pump if awaited inline. Byte-exact on the semantic domain; no diff (the point is size); AP-ID, title and trailing tags are untouched (a note-only request composes no name). Empty text is a loud ValueError, never a silent no-op. No mapped-node refusal: parity with node.edit, which refuses none (checked at e5a86ce). The two thin verb delegates below stay one-line re-fronts (curate, don't carpet-bomb).

old_result.comment: GLIMPSE `since` Form-A window PARSER. Parses a time-window token into a duration in SECONDS (timestamps are epoch-seconds). Accepts a unit-suffixed integer/float -- s(econds) m(inutes) h(ours) d(ays) w(eeks) -- e.g. '3d','1w','12h','90m','45s'; a BARE number is interpreted as DAYS ('7' == '7d'), the common case. Whitespace-tolerant, case-insensitive. Returns None for a blank/None/garbage/non-positive token so the caller can raise an actionable error. Pure. | GLIMPSE `since` PRUNE -- the shared leaf-branch filter run LAST (after Phase1/2/3 AND after the timestamp reorder), on the already-final sorted forest. Decomposes the forest into root->leaf branches (same DFS the sort uses), keeps a branch iff its branch-date (via the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static -- created=leaf createdAt, modified=branch-max modifiedAt, IDENTICAL to the sort) is beyond the pivot: ascending -> STRICTLY GREATER than pivot (most-recent tail; the pivot node itself excluded, everything newer kept); descending -> STRICTLY LESS than pivot (the commensurate 'oldest tail', a don't-care corner but done right). A branch with no resolvable date is DROPPED (can't prove it's in the window). Then trie-merges the surviving branches back into a tree via the SAME _reorder pass with sort_by carried through, so straddled ancestors re-emit exactly as in the unfiltered render. Returns a NEW forest (inputs untouched); empty list when nothing survives.

GLIMPSE `since` Form-A (time-window) PIVOT. Data-relative leading edge (Dan): the pivot is the branch-date of the MOST RECENT leaf branch in the ALREADY-FINAL forest (ascending) minus the window -- so 'last 1 week' on data whose newest branch is 2 years old means the week ENDING at that 2-year-old edge, NOT wall-clock now. Descending flips to the OLDEST edge plus the window (the don't-care commensurate corner). Uses the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static for every branch date so it matches the sort. Returns the pivot epoch-seconds, or None if no branch has a resolvable date (caller then returns the tree unfiltered rather than erroring on empty data).

GLIMPSE `since="curated"` FORM-B PIVOT (the self-maintaining curation cursor). Walks the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, finds every node that has been CURATED = carries any tag matching an active slice prefix INCLUDING --deprecated variants but EXCLUDING the --suppress/--expand PRESENTATION variants (via node_is_curated_for_prefixes, threaded with the render caller's resolved match_scope -- the SAME SELECTION-stage scope knob Stage-1 membership uses, 'name' = title only so a note-body family tag never moves the cursor, 'name_and_note' = default NAME+NOTE -- deliberately looser than slice MEMBERSHIP on the triage axis, because deprecating a tag is itself a curation act the user must not re-encounter; suppressing/expanding one is a lens carve-out, NOT triage, and must not move the cursor -- Session-019 curated-cursor fix + match_scope plumbing). For each curated node it computes that node's branch-date using the SAME rule the sort uses (_branch_timestamp_key_static over the node's root->leaf cache path: created=the curated node's own createdAt; modified=branch-max modifiedAt down to it), and returns the MAX (ascending; MIN for descending) = the high-water mark. Everything strictly newer than this in the shared-tail prune is the UNCURATED tail. Returns None when NOTHING under root is curated yet (no group tag anywhere) so the tail shows the whole subtree (all of it is 'new since last curated'). Cache-only; pure aside from the cache read.
Count every node in a nested {children:[...]} subtree, inclusive of the root.
Maximum depth of a nested {children:[...]} subtree (a childless root is depth 1).

Resolves root_uuid prefix-tolerantly via the SHARED resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle (UUID exact -> unique prefix -> [ap:CORE] AP-ID; multi -> did-you-mean; none -> cache-miss error), builds ONE RenderProjectionSpec (kind raw_root) so STAGE-1 admission (exclude_completed) is read off the spec, projects the COMPLETE subtree via build_slice_subtree_from_cache(..., member_all=True) (every descendant is a member; no slice filtering; NO Phase 2/3/4), then hands the base tree + the SAME spec to the shared STAGE-2 tail render_stage2_filter_sort. old_result.comment: Shared per-input symbol resolution core for Lightning Rod. Resolves every requested UUID/symbol exactly once, preserves the original input item beside its resolved UUID, applies root scoping and optional suppression filtering, and returns ordered per-item records plus the classic render_symbols buckets. AP-ID ITEMS (ap:APSYMB): an '[ap:CORE]' / 'ap:CORE' item (any case; a BARE core is NOT accepted -- grammar guard _RENDER_SYMBOLS_AP_ID_ITEM_RE) resolves via the shared resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle BEFORE the UUID-shaped / symbol classification -- but ONLY when allow_anchor_points=True, which is passed ONLY by the render wrapper (_project_render_symbols_from_cache); the beacon-mutation modes call with the default False and are categorically unaffected (anchor points are ephemeral-read-only). Used by render_symbols and the beacon-mutation modes so mutation never re-resolves UUIDs or guesses which operation belongs to which resolved node. BRACKETED-UUID ITEMS (Dan, 2026): an item whose AP-ID-style brackets wrap a pure-hex >=8-char body ('[a2e552e3]' / '[full-uuid]') is unwrapped via the SAME pure normalizer the Layer-1 primitive consumes (unwrap_bracketed_uuid_handle) BEFORE the _uuid_shaped routing classification, so it ROUTES to the UUID leg instead of falling to the symbol leg; '[ap:CORE]' items (colon => non-hex) and bracketed non-hex cores ('[K7M2QF]') are never unwrapped and route exactly as before.

render_symbols PER-ITEM OBJECT ELEMENTS (ap:EXPSWP; D2 input shape Option B; D3 unwrap-only in v1): the ONE shared item normalizer for the render_symbols `symbols` list. An element is either a plain string handle (today's behavior, stripped) or a small object {'uuid': HANDLE | 'symbol': NAME, 'expand'?: bool} -- exactly one of uuid/symbol, non-empty string handle, expand bool if present (absent/false = plain member). Returns {ok, handles (resolution input, strings only), expand_handles (flagged handles, expand-wins on a plain+flagged duplicate per the locked semantics contract), raw (the canonical VERBATIM echo list: stripped strings + shallow-copied objects -- what the spec / wire blob / render_scope selection carries so every re-projection re-runs normalize->resolve->sweep deterministically, D5)}. LOUD structured rejection (success:False-shaped): both keys, neither key, empty/non-string handle, non-bool expand, unrecognized keys, or any element that is neither string nor dict. The uuid/symbol KEY is NOT honored as an explicit-kind resolution hint in v1 (unwrap-only; the handle flows through the existing favor classification) -- a v1.1 nicety. Used by ALL THREE entry surfaces (_lightning_rod_render_symbols, the _handle_render_slice_modal render_symbols branch, and the _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal render_symbols branch), replacing the three hand-rolled [str(s).strip() ...] coercions (a net de-duplication).

DYNAMIC TAG-FREE BEACON SLICE (Lightning Rod mode='render_symbols'). Resolves a mixed list of UUIDs and/or symbols (function/class/beacon names) per-item, UUID-first then symbol-fallback (favor flag), scopes to REQUIRED root_uuids (single or list), applies ABSOLUTE global-suppression filtering (option B) then buckets survivors resolved(1)/ambiguous(N)/unresolved(0)/out-of-scope. PER-ITEM EXPAND (ap:EXPSWP): a `symbols` element may be an object {uuid|symbol, expand:true} -- unwrapped/validated by the ONE shared _normalize_render_symbols_items on ALL THREE entry surfaces (MCP return / docked modal / push). A cleanly-resolved flagged item's whole cache subtree is swept into the Stage-1 member set (member_ids ⊇ resolved_ids) via collect_subtree_ids -- suppression-guarded at sweep time, completed-pruned by Phase 1 at admit time, boundary-free; a flagged-but-not-cleanly-resolved item is INERT (no partial expansion). Still NO Phase 2/3/4 machinery. Builds the render from the member set (resolved ∪ swept) + LCA connective root via build_selected_subtree_from_cache and the SHARED render_stage2_filter_sort tail (Phase-1 SELECTION only; no Phase 2/3/4). Markdown-only (no bracketed mode). Non-fatal: problem items are reported BOTH in-band (appended '## WARNING Unresolved/ambiguous symbols' section) AND out-of-band (resolution_report + warning). ONE WebSocket touch (unlike other Lightning Rod modes): the tab-agnostic get_slice_group_config read to obtain f8_global_never_expand_tags (the wfy-suppress list). Resolution uses ONLY the shared resolvers (resolve_uuid_like_node_handle + client.read_uuid_from_symbol + resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle for GATED [ap:CORE] anchor-point items, ap:APSYMB) -- no bespoke resolution logic. Where the symbol list comes from: a phase-1 architect agent that read a larger slice and passes forward exactly the symbols/UUIDs the phase-2 session should see. | SHARED render-symbols projection core (the anti-seam extraction). The SINGLE resolve->scope->suppress->bucket->LCA implementation, called by BOTH the MCP-return path (_lightning_rod_render_symbols) AND the docked-modal push cell (_handle_render_slice_modal's render_symbols branch), so the two can NEVER drift on resolution semantics. PURE of transport: it takes an already-loaded cache_by_id + an already-resolved suppress_tags list (each caller reads those in its own way -- the MCP path via _resolve_slice_group_config(None), the modal path via its own nested get_slice_group_config read) and returns {ok, error?, lca_root, resolved_ids (explicit-only; NEVER polluted by the sweep), member_ids (resolved ∪ swept -- the Stage-1 member set the callers' predicate tests), expand_ids, resolution_report (+ expand_ids/swept_count), report_markdown, warning}. Uses ONLY the shared resolvers (resolve_uuid_like_node_handle + client.read_uuid_from_symbol + resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle for GATED [ap:CORE] anchor-point items, ap:APSYMB) -- no bespoke resolution logic -- and the shared _symbol_report_row for rich ambiguity rows. No render, no WebSocket, no disk here; the callers own the render tail + reporting placement. NBBW follow-up: the per-item resolution runs in a worker thread on a private loop (cache-only; the pinned snapshot rides the copied context), so a large render never blocks the daemon.

The MCP-return render_symbols cell over the SHARED _project_render_symbols_from_cache resolve->scope->suppress->bucket->LCA core and the ONE render tail. tier (54e8356f(ii), MCP-return ONLY) swaps each rendered member's note for a fenced body via _apply_render_symbols_tier + snippet_view.render_symbol_tier_note: 'slice' (default) unchanged; 'metadata' exactly the snippet size header (the ONE format_snippet_header format); 'context' comment + def + first context_lines lines + a trailer pointing at the rest. The parameter never enters the lightning selection / spec blob, so the docked-modal and push paths cannot see it; headings_only/output_file are refused with a non-slice tier, and a failed disk read keeps the member's original note plus a WARNING section.

render-symbols ambiguity/unresolved REPORT ROW builder -- the anti-seam. It REUSES the rich descriptor the ONE symbol resolver already produced (uuid/name/file_path/ast_qualname/line/via via read_uuid_from_symbol -> _build_candidate_descriptor), looked up from descriptors_by_uuid, rather than rebuilding a poorer row (which was the 5th ambiguity dialect). For a UUID-path candidate (whose descriptor carries no path), it BEST-EFFORT enriches file_path via the EXISTING resolve_cartographer_path_from_node ancestor walk (the same Root:/Path: header logic used everywhere), and fills name from the cache -- tolerating the documented 'no resolvable path' case (a candidate under an unmapped region, or a multi-root call where a given candidate's chain has no Root:/Path: header) by leaving file_path None. Name is DOM-markup-stripped for readability. This is the closest we get to ONE ambiguity descriptor without a broader refactor of the four existing reporters (out of scope now).

render-symbols IN-BAND report: compose the '## WARNING Unresolved / ambiguous symbols' Markdown section appended to the bottom of the render. Lists each problem item (ambiguous / unresolved / out-of-scope / all-suppressed) with its candidate rows. Candidate uuids print SHORT ([ap:0M6VP8]: the paste-backable short form via unique_short_uuid_prefix over uuid_prefix_collisions, lengthened just enough to be unique; the structured resolution_report keeps the full UUIDs). Returns '' when there are no problem items (nothing appended). Deliberately plain Markdown so it renders cleanly in the same pseudo-document.

Phase-C DISK-TARGET UNIQUENESS check (SPEC v5 §5 step 11): no two preflighted items with a RESOLVED TARGET KEY -- actionable OR noop -- may claim the same disk target key. A noop row still asserts an intended end-state for its target; letting it collide with another row's mutation would make its ledger row dishonest. Returns a collisions list (batch preflight failure) or None.

Shared Q3 beacon batch orchestrator for ensure/remove. Ordinary per-item resolution and returned preflight failures are ledger rows, not batch vetoes; valid items continue through the existing JIT/CAS writer. Scope/cache/infrastructure failures and duplicate/disk-target collisions still abort. The ONE all-target lease acquisition, ownership, cancellation, and cleanup paths are unchanged; any lease refusal still blocks all eligible writes. Disk-only with complete partial-success ledger. Policy addendum: docs/BEACON-BATCH-PARTIAL-SUCCESS.md. NON-BLOCKING (NBBW): Phase B resolution runs in a worker thread (private loop, cache-only) and the client preflight/plan/commit bodies run in worker threads -- the commit thread is never abandoned on cancellation, so the lease release in finally still follows the last disk write. GLOBAL SUPPRESSION: symbol resolution honours #wfy-suppress via _beacon_symbol_suppress_tags (fail-loud read); a suppressed-only item is an item-local all_suppressed row, never written. COMMENT CONFLICTS (2R4E1P): a fill-mode conflict is KEPT, never an error -- the labels are still ensured, comment_outcome='kept_existing_conflict' rides every row status (committed/noop alike) with a warning carrying BOTH texts; the batch result gains a top-level warnings list and a summary.comment_conflicts_kept count, which make_mutation_ack lifts to the ack's warnings. ATOMIC OPT-IN ([ap:LPC157] residue): spec.atomic=true (default false) restores the strict preflight veto AFTER Phase C and BEFORE lease acquisition -- any item failure leaves every other row not_run with zero writes and no lease (the failing item keeps its error row); a mid-batch commit failure is still per item (writes are individually CAS-atomic, no rollback exists). ONE-LINE SUMMARY: the result carries a top-level summary_line ('N committed · M noop · K failed (...)' -- the single failure's symbol/kind/reason, else the distinct failure kinds) so an agent can act without reading the ledger.

Q4 Lightning Rod: batch Workflowy #tag mutation (add/remove/rename) on NODES by UUID/[ap:CORE] handle -- the Workflowy-nodes mutation cell of the 2x2 (Q3 = disk beacons). THIN LEDGER WRAPPER over the three client tag primitives (workflowy_add_tag/remove_tag/rename_tag) -- ZERO tag-region surgery of its own (the no-cracks core). Preflight-all-then-commit, mirroring _lightning_rod_mutate_beacons: resolve EVERY handle ONCE via the Layer-3 universal resolver (client.resolve_node_handle; allow_uuid + allow_anchor_point, NO symbols -- symbols are Q3's quadrant) -> ANY unresolved/ambiguous handle ABORTS the batch (complete ledger, zero mutations) -> duplicate-resolved-UUID preflight (batch abort, Q3 parity -- also makes intra-batch substrate drift impossible: each node is read-modify-written exactly once) -> sequential commit in input order delegating to the primitives (per-item failure recorded, batch CONTINUES). Complete ledger: exactly one row per normalized operation, in input order, under EVERY outcome, carrying the primitives' per-op detail (tags_added/tags_already_present, tags_removed/tags_not_present, renamed/old_occurrences_removed/new_tag_already_present, old_name/new_name). Render knobs (exclude_completed et al.) do NOT apply: mutation may reach suppressed/completed nodes -- Q4 targets NODES by handle (UUID/AP-ID), never by symbol, so global #wfy-suppress (which filters SYMBOL resolution, incl. Q3) does not apply here.

Q4 batch Workflowy tag mutation over the section-9 client wire (action=mutate_node_tags). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id). Deserializes the versioned wire frame {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, operations:[...]} via WorkflowyTagMutationSpec.from_wire -- the SAME _normalize_operations core the MCP tool boundary uses, so the two transports can never drift (STAGE-0 DOCTRINE) -- then runs the SAME _lightning_rod_mutate_tags orchestrator and replies mutate_node_tags_result (echoing request_id) with the full ledger. MergeSliceGroups ORCHESTRATOR (Phases A-G of the goal spec + the MRGAMD amendment layer). Mirrors _lightning_rod_mutate_tags in shape (phases, structured returns, complete reporting). MCP tool: merge two or more slice groups into ONE new slice lens via tags applied to Workflowy nodes. Inputs: groups (2+ named or dynamic refs), mode (union|intersection), tag (one base tag). Normalizes via MergeSliceGroupsSpec.normalize_from_tool_args (the ONE MCP-ingress core), then runs the _merge_slice_groups orchestrator. Returns the full report (root, tag counts, Q4 mutation ledger, verification block, persistence record).

MergeSliceGroups over the section-9 client wire (action=merge_slice_groups). Browser-initiated correlated request. Deserializes the versioned wire frame via MergeSliceGroupsSpec.from_wire (the SAME _normalize_group_refs core as the MCP boundary -- the two transports cannot drift, STAGE-0 DOCTRINE), injects config via _read_slice_group_config_nested (browser-initiated nested read, CFGOP1), runs the SAME _merge_slice_groups orchestrator, persists server-side via create_slice_group (A9: the wire handler persists via the SAME server-side path as the MCP origin -- no client-side fire-and-forget), and replies merge_slice_groups_result echoing request_id. TASK-DISPATCHED (see websocket_handler) because a merge runs tens of seconds of ~1 op/sec mutations and must not block the pump.

The FIRST semantic concern on the section-9 client->server mutation channel (action=anchor_dock_update). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id) from the Anchors modal's per-row star toggle. Deserializes the versioned wire frame via AnchorDockUpdateSpec.from_wire (TRANSPORT SHELL ONLY -- K3: it validates object/fields/version/JSON types and "at least one attribute present", and never re-implements the impl's families/attribute semantics) and routes to the ONE canonical seam _anchor_dock_update_impl (K1: target_tab=str(endpoint_id) so the impl's nested Direction-A config read targets the asking tab), whose _attribute_transform -> _node_edit_core(_tag_transform=...) -> _compose_protected_name owns every semantic decision. Replies anchor_dock_update_result echoing request_id with the impl result. The client sends INTENT ONLY (dock_handle + favorite/local + optional families) and composes NO tag. TASK-DISPATCHED (see websocket_handler) because _anchor_dock_update_impl -> _resolve_note_session_config issues a nested Direction-A get_extension_settings read, so an inline await could deadlock the single websocket pump (the _handle_list_anchors_for_widget precedent). Domain errors (ProtectedNameViolation / _AnchorOperationError) reply STRUCTURED with error_code + extra (K2) so the client can render the family chooser from extra.families_present.

LIGHTNING ROD postfix_policy (ap:IMPPTX) -- the ONE shared boundary validator/normalizer for the opt-in postfix-policy knob on Lightning render requests. Returns (normalized, error): 'none' (default -- the original Phase-1-only family/search match, NO expand/suppress/deprecated operations) or 'slice' (render_tags ONLY: the full Stage-1 four-phase funnel via build_stage1_base_tree, with the requested tags as active_prefixes and the live postfix words + real f8_global_never_expand_tags from config). LOUD errors: an unrecognized value, or 'slice' requested for any mode other than render_tags (gather produces a tag set, render_search has no tag-family expansion operand, render_symbols has its own absolute-suppression + per-item expand semantics ap:EXPSWP). Used by EVERY ingress surface -- the lightning_rod tool boundary, _lightning_rod_from_cache, the _handle_render_slice_modal lightning cell, the push cell (_glimpse_push_slice_to_modal), and the Scoped frozen-DOM handler (which then additionally rejects 'slice' itself) -- so the five surfaces can never drift on the contract. Pure; no I/O.

old_result.role: async _lightning_rod_from_cache(mode, root_uuid, tags, query, query_mode, tag_match, postfix_policy, as_markdown, output_file, sort_by, sort_direction, headings_only, since, match_scope)
old_result.comment: LIGHTNING ROD internal orchestrator -- the temporary/in-memory counterpart to _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache, but PURELY cache-only BY DEFAULT (NO WebSocket, NO slice-group config, NO Phase 2/3/4; render_tags postfix_policy='slice' is the ONE exception: ap:IMPPTX routes it through the FULL Stage-1 funnel build_stage1_base_tree with one _resolve_slice_group_config(None) read for the live postfix words + the real f8_global_never_expand_tags list, surfacing Phase-2 warnings / pruned-zombie count / body_suppressed_ids exactly like the persisted slice path). Resolves root_uuid prefix-tolerantly via the shared Layer-1 primitive resolve_uuid_like_node_handle, loads the /nodes-export cache, and dispatches on mode: 'gather' -> gather_tags_in_subtree (returns the sorted tag list; NO render); 'render_tags' -> build_tag_predicate (Option B prefix-family, NO postfix/deprecation semantics BY DEFAULT) -> build_selected_subtree_from_cache -> shared render tail; 'render_search' -> build_search_predicate (shlex 'smart' | 'regex') -> build_selected_subtree_from_cache -> shared render tail. match_scope (SELECTION-stage scope knob: 'name' = title only | 'name_and_note' = default title+body) is validated loudly at this boundary then threaded into ALL THREE modes' harvest/predicate (gather_tags_in_subtree / build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) and echoed in render_scope.lightning.match_scope. This is the THIRD cell of the Stage-1 SELECTION truth table (slice=is_slice_member, raw-dump=lambda True, lightning-rod=custom predicate), running Phase-1-only and skipping presentation policy BY DEFAULT. since='curated' is rejected here (no slice tag set defines 'curated'); live-GUI-sync is never supported. The traversal pair rides the shared selection fragment ([ap:EPR86W] 4b): descend_policy builds the anchor-boundary predicate for all three render modes, and recursive=False is refused LOUDLY here -- a Lightning Rod selection is defined by its predicate over the whole scope, so a depth cap would silently change membership (render_symbols and the mutation modes dispatch above and never carry the flag). Reuses render_stage2_filter_sort verbatim, so Lightning Rod output is structurally identical to every other cache-sourced GLIMPSE.

old_result.role: async _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache(slice_group, as_markdown, output_file, sort_by, sort_direction, target_tab)
old_result.comment: Cache-only GLIMPSE path for a slice group (no DOM/extract_dom): the content-return originator of a slice render. Reads the live slice-group config (tab-agnostic get_slice_group_config -- the ONLY WS touch, for OPTIONS not DOM), resolves the requested slice_group id-OR-name via the SHARED _resolve_slice_group_handle (exact id -> unique 'grp-' prefix -> case-insensitive name fallback -- the SAME resolver the push path uses, so the two can't drift), derives its root_uuid + active prefixes + effective sort, optionally resolves a root_uuid_override (the slice_override scope) or a stop-at-child-anchors boundary predicate, and builds ONE RenderProjectionSpec BEFORE projecting so STAGE-1 admission (exclude_completed/match_scope) is read off the spec. Runs STAGE 1 via the shared funnel build_stage1_base_tree (Phase 1 membership -> Phase 2 plan -> Phase 3 collapse/expand -> Phase 4 zombie prune), computes the curated pivot when since='curated', then hands the base tree + the SAME spec to the shared STAGE-2 tail render_stage2_filter_sort. active_prefixes / postfix words / global_never / cache_by_id are live-config OPERANDS, deliberately NOT spec fields. Output is structurally identical to a live-DOM GLIMPSE of the same expanded slice, so a session can be initialized with no human at the Workflowy GUI. Chain-1 r2 (F5): a sink aimed at a stored root that names a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal before any render/file work. Chain-2 r1 (F1): with NO override, the EFFECTIVE STORED root itself resolves through the SAME shared composite resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle the override root gets (live legs first, then the archive legs — the fallback gate and record_archive_served ride inside it), so an exported-and-deleted stored root is served by the automatic fallback re-run (banner + provenance via the finalizer) and an include-mode run records the archive answer; a live stored root resolves to itself unchanged, and an unknown one stays unresolved for the Stage-1 absent-root branch (today's error, sink refusal intact). Chain-2 r2 (R1): a SHAVED corrective match of the stored root is REJECTED, never adopted — the stored identity and the pre-r1 miss policy are preserved (uuid_resolution_was_shave classifies the outcome; the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded; the raw root falls to the absent-root branch) — while an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2) and keeps the archive repair. No second resolver and no per-carrier banner copy: the lens group atom's inherited root shares this exact seam via lens_engine._resolve_root.

PUSH-TO-MODAL path for glimpse(push_to_modal=True): instead of RETURNING the rendered content to the agent, it COMMANDS the target Workflowy tab to render the requested SERVER-SIDE SCOPE into its docked Markdown modal -- the server-push twin of a human clicking APPLY. Chain-1 W4 (F5): the funnel's resolve-HERE-before-the-round-trip doctrine now covers the render_lens cell's atom roots too -- a root naming a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal (the docked modal never serves archives), so a push can never ack success and then fail tab-side. Chain-1 r2 (R2-W2): the resolve-HERE doctrine now covers every indirect selection as well -- a render_lens GROUP atom pre-flights its group's STORED root (an explicit root_handle override is the target and wins; a bare group atom rides the stored default, so a recursive merged lens cannot hide an archived effective root), the render_symbols cell resolves its roots and runs its items through the SHARED _resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache router (live legs first; an archived root or item refuses before any command; items still ride verbatim per D5), and the direct slice-group cell resolves the chosen group's STORED root when no override root is present. Handles the full (slice_group, root_uuid) truth table: slice_group only (resolve id-or-name -> canonical group_id via the SHARED Layer-1 _resolve_slice_group_handle -- the SAME id/prefix/case-insensitive-name resolver _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache uses), root_uuid only (resolve prefix-tolerantly via the SHARED resolve_uuid_like_node_handle -> a RAW-DUMP push, the zero-token 'show me this anchor' command), or BOTH (slice lens scoped to an override root). All resolution happens HERE (before the round-trip) so a bad group name / missing UUID fails loudly early. Sends a Direction-A 'apply_slice_in_dock' frame carrying whichever of {group_id, root_uuid} are present + the AGENT-SUPPLIED sort/since as an EXPLICIT override (never the tab's global dock sort) via the generic _ws_request_response rail; returns the tab's ack. The tab-side dispatch invokes the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock (same fn the APPLY button uses), so the dock render + (for a slice) live-GUI-sync watcher are identical to a manual Apply; a raw-dump push installs NO watcher (no search/plan). The caller (glimpse) guards a bare live-DOM push (neither scope) as the only error.

UUID-hallucination HARDENING for a render_spec-driven GLIMPSE (the render_spec="modal"/blob path). Given a deserialized RenderProjectionSpec + the /nodes-export cache map, canonicalize EVERY UUID the spec carries -- root_uuid, focus.uuid, and EVERY focus.ancestor_path entry -- through the SHARED prefix-tolerant Layer-1 resolver resolve_uuid_like_node_handle (the exact machine SCRY / anchor / snippet callers use). Grace runs BEFORE the exact (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) focus match downstream, so it only CANONICALIZES a possibly-drifted string to its cache UUID; it NEVER loosens the occurrence-exact match itself (a canonicalized triple still resolves to exactly one occurrence via _resolve_focus_index_path). On the render_spec="modal" path the UUIDs are already server-canonical (near-no-op belt-and-suspenders); on the pasted-blob fallback path this is the real net against an agent-drifted UUID in the chain. A UUID that stays unresolved (no exact hit, no unique prefix) or is ambiguous is LEFT AS-IS (best-effort): a bad focus already fails safe to the whole document downstream, and a bad root_uuid surfaces its own cache-miss error in the dispatch that follows. Returns a NEW spec via with_overrides; the input spec (frozen) is never mutated. Pure; no I/O beyond reading the passed cache map.

Dispatch a resolved RenderProjectionSpec to the right cache-render helper by spec.kind -- the shared tail for BOTH render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (the "modal" WS query and the pasted-blob fallback). It routes the (slice|slice_override) cells to _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache (passing spec.group_id as slice_group, the resolved root as root_uuid_override for slice_override, and spec.focus) and the raw_root cell to _glimpse_root_uuid_from_cache (passing spec.root_uuid + spec.focus). The lightning_rod cell (ap:GLMPMODAL) re-projects the FOURTH scope by reading spec.lightning['mode'] and calling the SAME projector a fresh lightning_rod() call uses (_lightning_rod_from_cache for gather/render_tags/render_search; _lightning_rod_render_symbols for render_symbols): the opaque lightning selection is passed through verbatim, so no new render path is introduced. Each mode keeps its own constraints (render_symbols Markdown-only + roots via its own selection.root_uuids; gather raw-text/root_only; since='curated' rejected inside the projector). FOCUS on a lightning modal read is now SUPPORTED for the node-tree modes (render_tags/render_search/render_symbols): spec.focus is threaded into the projector and resolved occurrence-exactly by the shared render_stage2_filter_sort focus authority -- the ONLY residual rejection is gather+focus (a gather is a tag outline with one synthetic root row, so a real row focus is a category error). Every view knob (as_markdown / sort / since / headings_only / match_scope / descend_policy) is read off the spec, so the render is byte-identical to the equivalent explicit-arg GLIMPSE -- the whole point of routing through the ONE spec object. descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' is honored for the raw_root cell by building the anchor-boundary predicate here (the one config-read WS touch), exactly as the explicit-arg root_uuid path does.

The AGENT-OVERRIDE seam for the render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (render_spec="modal" AND the pasted-blob fallback). Given the RESOLVED, tab-sourced (or pasted) RenderProjectionSpec and the agent's TRI-STATE view overrides (as_markdown / headings_only / sort_by / sort_direction / since; None = inherit what the modal is showing, a value = explicit override), it (1) merges the non-None overrides onto the spec via the SINGLE normalized mutator spec.with_view_overrides (which re-runs the ONE normalizer and preserves the resolved kind via kind_hint -- NOT raw with_overrides), then (2) runs the LOUD combination guards ONCE on the FINAL merged spec, where spec.focus and spec.kind are known. The two guards (Dan-decided): (A) a sort override (sort_by/sort_direction supplied) is REJECTED when spec.focus is present -- sorting a single focused option-Y row is ill-defined; the user re-roots the modal at that subtree instead; (B) a since override is REJECTED when spec.focus is present (a tail/window over the whole underlying scope intersected with a focused row is meaningless). Beyond focus, the standard since preconditions are enforced by reading the FINAL SinceSpec object fields; curated requires a slice/slice_override scope. Returns (spec, None) on success or (spec, error_dict) on a rejected combination. This is the ONLY place agent view overrides are applied to a render_spec spec, so both render_spec sub-paths share ONE override+guard implementation.

Pure pre-order DFS that returns the FIRST node in a forest whose id/uuid matches -- the CANONICAL (unsorted) node lookup for the Scoped Lightning Rod occurrence-exact re-root pre-step in _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture. After the sorted forest is pruned to a clicked occurrence and that occurrence's LEAF UUIDs are collected, this locates the clicked node's canonical node in the UNSORTED captured forest so its subtree can be rebuilt DE-MIRRORED (filtered to those leaf UUIDs via build_selected_subtree_from_forest). Relies on the v1 invariant that a Workflowy UUID appears AT MOST ONCE in the raw (unsorted) tree -- Workflowy 'mirrors' are explicitly UNSUPPORTED in v1 -- so 'the first match' IS 'the only match'. Returns None if not found. The UUID (not object identity) is the ONLY valid bridge between the sorted shadow-copy tree and the canonical tree.

SLICE-BASE projection for a SLICE-FROZEN Scoped Lightning Rod. Deserializes the client's durable base_render_spec (RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob) and RE-PROJECTS that scope from the /nodes-export cache into a single render TREE, so _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture can then treat it EXACTLY like a DOM captured_tree (same re-root pre-step, same build_selected_subtree_from_forest filter, same _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture compose). It REUSES the canonical funnels -- build_stage1_base_tree for a slice / slice_override scope (via the SAME nested get_slice_group_config Direction-A read the sibling _handle_render_slice_modal uses), and build_slice_subtree_from_cache(member_all=True) for a raw_root scope -- and NEVER inlines a new projection. Returns (tree, None) on success or (None, error_dict) on any failure (no tab, no group, empty group, cache miss), so the caller replies verbatim. A lightning_rod base is rejected (a prior Lightning render is already ephemeral and arrives as captured_tree, never as a durable base spec). The projected tree is a first-class EPHEMERAL dom_capture from the caller onward -- the one-way collapse of the slice, NEVER re-laundered into a durable spec. STAGE-1 POLICY THREADING (post-Sol-audit Finding 3): spec.exclude_completed and spec.descend_policy's shared anchor boundary now reach the projection -- they were silently dropped before, so a frozen scope's Scoped re-projection could surface completed nodes and descend through child anchors the original render excluded.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD over a FROZEN DOM view (action=render_lightning_dom_capture). The DOM-frozen half of the Scoped toggle: the dock is showing an EPHEMERAL captured DOM forest and the user fired a Lightning Rod with [Scoped] ON, so the search is confined to that on-screen forest rather than walking the whole cache root. Reads the frame's captured_tree + opaque lightning selection {mode, tags?, query?, query_mode?, match_scope, postfix_policy?}; builds the SAME singular predicate the cache path uses (build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) and filters the forest via build_selected_subtree_from_forest; then composes through the EXISTING _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture machinery via its pre_filter seam, so the artifact stays a first-class kind='dom_capture' (EPHEMERAL -- the client provenance adapter must never launder it into a durable RenderProjectionSpec). gather short-circuits to gather_tags_in_forest -> render_tags_outline (raw_text/root_only), the forest sibling of the cache gather seam. No cache walk, no slice config; render_symbols is NOT supported here (it is inherently a cache-resolution mode). postfix_policy='slice' is LOUD-REJECTED in v1 (ap:IMPPTX): the full Stage-1 funnel hydrates expansions from the raw /nodes-export cache, which would silently graft nodes from OUTSIDE the ephemeral frozen domain (a source-correct forest hydrator is a separate future feature). The rejection now runs BEFORE any source-fork projection (post-Sol-audit Finding 4), so an unsupported request fails with its own actionable error -- never masked by a config/projection failure and never after wasted projection work. Task-dispatched like the sibling modal handlers. A malformed query fails LOUD (lightning_rod_query_error); an empty match renders an empty dom_capture document (valid 'no matches'), never an error.

The DOM-FROZEN sibling of _glimpse_dispatch_spec for render_spec="modal". It does NOT use the cache-projection path, because a frozen DOM view is a DIFFERENT SOURCE AXIS: an EPHEMERAL captured tree the tab pinned at freeze, not a durable /nodes-export scope. It composes that captured tree through the SAME composer + row-identity + focus primitives the cache path uses: normalize the {root,children} payload to one forest; prepare_stage2_render_forest for sort/since/counts (curated since is rejected -- no slice tags); then the shared materializer. TWO deliberate departures from the cache tail: (1) focus is EXACT-OR-ERROR -- an unresolvable focus triple returns a loud stale error, not the lenient whole-document fallback; (2) full/UUID mode is supported ONLY with headings_only=True (the {UUID<->title} harvest; a full body dump is rejected). The render_scope echo is honest kind='dom_capture' (durable_scope=False, live_gui_sync_supported=False) -- it never masquerades as raw_root/slice. GUARDRAIL: the captured tree is never folded into a RenderProjectionSpec. ADVISORY PROVENANCE (S04 Remediation Chain 4): the hard-barrier read advisory is a cache-provenance claim applied ONLY when the composed content is /nodes-export-derived -- the cache_sourced kwarg (default False, this function composes browser-captured trees) is carried explicitly to the ONE advisory authority; the render_spec="modal" dom_captured_tree read and genuinely DOM-frozen Scoped Lightning are unadvised, while a slice-frozen Scoped run passes cache_sourced=True and stays advised.

THE render_spec="modal" path -- the primary 'GLIMPSE what I'm looking at in the docked modal' capability. Issues ONE Direction-A get_current_modal_render_spec WS query to the target tab via the generic _ws_request_response rail (request_id correlation; the tab answers from its OWN dockedSliceContext.render_spec + selected-row triple -- a LEAF query, NO nested back-to-tab round trip, so NO deadlock-note applies). Deserializes the reply's render_spec blob into a RenderProjectionSpec via from_render_spec_blob (the SAME normalizer every entry point uses), applies UUID prefix-grace to every UUID in the spec (root + focus triple) via _grace_resolve_spec_uuids against the /nodes-export cache, then dispatches by kind through _glimpse_dispatch_spec -> the existing focused-projection helpers. DETERMINISTIC end-to-end: the agent types ZERO UUIDs (the blob comes from the tab's own server-adopted scope), and SERVER code (not the agent) deserializes + re-projects, so this is the (b)-variant architecture Dan chose -- the Python composer stays the sole renderer, no client-string round-trips through the server. Fails loudly if the tab has no cache-sourced render to report (success:false + a clear message telling the human to Apply a slice / push a scope first).

THE ONE agent-facing output-contract finalizer for the GLIMPSE FAMILY of MCP tools -- its consumers are the glimpse family (workflowy_glimpse), lightning_rod, anchor.dock.render, and slice_group render/sift/merge.render. Given the rich internal result dict every render helper builds, it delivers to the AGENT exactly what the human wants to see -- and nothing redundant. Rule: (1) output_file set -> pass the file-write summary through unchanged (the disk write is the deliverable, not the string). (2) result is not a dict -> already a bare value, pass through. (3) MARKDOWN / RAW-TEXT mode -- a RENDERED TEXT STRING is present -> return it RAW (real newlines, like read_text_file), NOTHING ELSE: preview_markdown (every Markdown-mode render across GLIMPSE live-DOM / slice_group / raw root_uuid / render_spec modal+blob / dom_capture, AND Lightning Rod render_tags/render_search/render_symbols) OR preview_text (the Lightning Rod gather raw-text tag outline, byte-identical to the modal's Gather). The rendered string IS the whole semantic payload in this mode, so no envelope is wanted. This is the single future-proof seam: ANY future raw-text mode just fills preview_text (or preview_markdown) and is delivered raw with ZERO further change here. (4) FULL / UUID mode -- a preview_tree is present -> return the STRUCTURED DICT, preserving preview_tree AND all the genuinely-useful metadata (node_count, depth, _source, render_scope, since_applied, ...), but STRIPPING ONLY the redundant CONTENT twins: `rows` (modal tree-view metadata that duplicates preview_tree) and any stray preview_markdown/preview_text; additionally, when headings_only=True (the compact UUID-harvest pass), strip bulky live-DOM raw `root`/`children` to keep the payload small. Full mode is for structural / UUID work, so the stats ARE wanted here -- only the duplicative rows/markdown clutter is dropped. (5) everything else (errors success:false, push_to_modal acks, gather's structured tag list when preview_text is somehow absent, empty payloads with neither field) -> pass the structured dict through unchanged so failures/acks still signal correctly. The rich internal payloads (rows, render_scope, since_applied, node_count) are LEFT INTACT on the helper returns -- they still flow to the browser/modal WS reply handlers that need them; this finalizer only shapes the AGENT-facing tool return. preview_markdown is checked before preview_text before preview_tree: at most one is ever populated on a given result, so order is belt-and-suspenders. STALE-FOCUS GUARD [ap:XDVDRG]: a Markdown/raw-text result that carries focus_unresolved is NEVER delivered raw -- its always-empty string would read as a legitimately empty view; the structured stale payload is returned instead (success flipped to false, the empty preview twins and modal rows dropped, error + focus_unresolved kept) so the shared family error boundary surfaces the loud stale-focus error. A legitimate empty (empty since-window, no focus_unresolved) still returns its raw '' when NO recency selection is active -- the (empty) stub then fires at the public funnel (9a); when a recency selection IS active ([ap:TVIIBN] 4e), the Markdown body is passed through the ONE empty-output stub (stub_empty_text_result, caveat C1) and the result opens with ONE '> Recency selection: ...' rule line naming what was chosen and teaching that sort_direction only orders (the structured full/UUID twin carries the same sentence as a top-level recency_header key, no quote marker). The header text is composed ONLY by _recency_header_sentence -- one composer, no second header writer; the browser modal / push / file paths never pass through here and are untouched by construction.

Pure simple-form identity interpretation over caller-injected cache/config operands. Reuses the existing node/group resolvers and Dock classifier, and the two pure decisions; returns a lowering or read_note intent, never acquires state or renders. Transport and note-read control flow stay per origin.

ONE estate entry through the EXISTING server render funnel (no new render path): a named-group entry normalizes via normalize_from_glimpse_args(group_id=<handle>, match_scope='name') — a slice spec at the group's stored root with its saved default sort/policy, resolved by the SAME _resolve_slice_group_handle glimpse(group_handle=…) uses; a spec entry deserializes via RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob (spec VERBATIM, focus included), rides the UUID prefix-grace, then the loud focus-intent-loss check (a saved selection that collapses to None aborts the entry rather than dumping the whole scope). Both go through the ONE override+guard seam (_apply_modal_view_overrides_and_guard → with_view_overrides) and _glimpse_dispatch_spec — which honors single-row AND mode='rows' covering-subtree focus via the shared Stage-2 tail, and NEVER runs the in-band Anchor-Dock raw-dump guard (every estate entry passes as allow_anchor_dock=true by construction). Returns a flat per-entry record; every failure shape (invalid entry, unresolvable group, root_not_in_cache, stale focus, guard rejection, funnel error, unexpected exception) is a LOUD record — the caller keeps rendering the others. Chain-1 r2 (F5/R2-W1): ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError is the one re-raised exception — an entry whose root names a visible archived node refuses the WHOLE sink call with the universal envelope, never an isolated failed row an assembly could write into a delivery-success file.

Estate OUTPUT origin: simple forms/full JSON directly or a Dock/estate handle, interpreted by the pure grammar and injected-snapshot resolver. Dock first (no note read), else ONE live _node_read_impl; entries never nest. Lowered entries use the same TWO-branch _glimpse_estate_render_entry and _glimpse_dispatch_spec. Existing alias/title headings, scope echoes, per-entry isolation, view overrides, output_file and reserved tabs semantics remain; no renderer, wire, cache writer or transport fork. Chain 1 r2 (WO [ap:4Q3LQV] W1): under repository_view the estate delivers the ONE coherence advisory authority's warning on its own reply -- the canonical line on the screen (text adapter on the document part, below the composed '> ' lines) and the structured key on the successful file acknowledgement -- while every file byte and assembled D stays clean; applicability rides the operation's captured status and is byte-identical when clean or with the flag off.

old_result.role: glimpse(output_file, as_markdown: bool, target_tab, sort_by, sort_direction, slice_group, root_uuid, headings_only, render_spec, allow_anchor_dock)
old_result.comment: GLIMPSE ingress: modal sentinel first; simple forms use the pure grammar and snapshot resolver before the existing spec/grace/view-override/push/render path. Explicit scope truth table and low-level defaults remain unchanged. [ap:EPR86W] part a: the raw-root cell honours recursive=False (root + direct children only, via the ONE shared walker's max_depth gate) and threads it to the push funnel; recursive=False on a slice-group scope or a live-DOM GLIMPSE is refused loudly at the boundary (and, for blobs, at the ONE spec normalizer).

Server helper: acquire the live WS peer (grace wait) and fetch the target tab's extension settings, returning normalized (note_session_tags, global_tags, default_parent). Fails loudly if no tab is reachable. Shared by both note-session MCP tools.
