old_result.comment: Path to the shared cross-process cache-refresh skip-toggle state file (wall-clock epoch deadline) in the runtime base dir. Shared by all MCP servers so the toggle is global under multi-server broker routing.
Read the shared skip-toggle wall-clock epoch deadline from disk (0.0 if absent/empty/unreadable). Best-effort; fail-open to 0.0 (toggle OFF).

Return True iff the user-controlled cache-refresh skip toggle is currently active. Reads the SHARED on-disk wall-clock deadline so the toggle is honored regardless of which MCP server (primary) does the work. Best-effort cleanup of the file once expired.
Seconds remaining on the skip toggle, or 0.0 if inactive/expired. Derived from the SHARED on-disk wall-clock deadline.
Enable/disable the shared cross-process cache-refresh skip toggle by writing/removing the wall-clock deadline file. Used by the set_cache_refresh_skip WebSocket handler.
Recover queued final responsibilities when a coordinator task ends before entering its worker; token-guarded receipts remain pending.
Coalesce reasons, fresh-fetch demand and fixed final obligations at one iteration cutoff; return scheduling/skip acknowledgment, never publication success.

Read-only heartbeat artifact merge for scanner/widget triage. Reports fresh/stale/missing/invalid identity and clamped mtime age without influencing persisted status, PID liveness, cancellation, reap, kill, admission, or claim repair.
One admission-mutex serialized inventory; public readable rows remain a list, internal observations retain uncertainty and incarnation provenance.
Admission-mutex cleanup of discharged orphan final-obligation records only; unfinished and retained-row receipts stay pinned for recovery/deduplication.

Shared deletion primitive used by manual job-history clearing. Deletes job JSON, logs_path, and the per-job folder named <YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>_<job-id> when present. Best-effort and never raises to callers.
old_result.role: delete CARTO job JSON/log/folder artifacts for a terminal job

old_result.comment: Manual known-terminal history cleanup, additionally pinned by unfinished final-publication responsibility and live region claims. Only valid published/skipped exact-incarnation records permit removal; marker deletion uses the same admission mutex.
old_result.role: clear terminal CARTO job history including failed/warning jobs

old_result.comment: Directory holding per-job 'final nodes-export refresh' claim files (.refresh_claims/ under the CARTO jobs dir). Co-located with the jobs for config/portability. NOTE: claim files are NOT caught by Phase 1 of _gc_carto_jobs (a non-recursive *.json glob + CARTO_ type filter that a subdir claim file with no type key never matches); they are reaped two ways — age-based by _gc_carto_jobs Phase 3 (mtime sweep of .refresh_claims/*.claim.json), and on-demand by _clear_carto_job_history's manual 'Clear job history' sweep (which deletes every claim whose owning job is not currently active). Claims are tiny idempotency markers, not leases.
Reserve positively terminal exact incarnations in versioned final-obligation records under admission.mutex. Reservation is recoverable responsibility, never publication success.
Persist latched relevance and positive terminal evidence; reconcile restart reservations via existing identity authority, never omission or age.
Serialize before off-loop scan through conservative durable observation and exact final-batch extraction; only positive stop proofs reserve work, execution receipts discharge it.

Exact token/incarnation final obligation transition under admission.mutex; unmatched callbacks release neither durable responsibility nor the live attempt; publication requires new-fetch receipt and adoption.

Watcher and startup trigger adapter for the single A1 governance sweep; supplies configured grace/cooldown values, loud diagnostics, and claim-aware terminal/orphan auxiliary cleanup without introducing a parallel lifecycle loop.

Primary server logger: writes each line to stderr (visible under TypingMind, swallowed under Claude Code) AND appends to a per-PID file under the shared per-user log dir (broker_protocol.server_log_file), so any single MCP server stays observable regardless of host. File sink is on by default, best-effort, never raises; disable via WORKFLOWY_FILE_LOGGING=0.

F3/F2 ancestor-chain WS handler: virtual-UUID (mirror) parsing, /nodes-export cache fetch + dirty-ID advisory, shaped error frames — but the walk and the WHOLE Markdown grammar are delegated to ancestor_path.build_ancestor_path_document, the ONE shared core the node.ancestors MCP verb also calls, so the hotkey and the verb can never drift. The document carries dock.peek-vocabulary right-side markers (⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓ + ▸N/desc/self/tree metrics) plus the 🗺️ mapped-folder / 📄 mapped-file markers with the key at the top, so this handler reads the configured Dock vocabulary via a nested get_extension_settings Direction-A read — which is why websocket_handler TASK-dispatches it (an inline await would deadlock the pump, the list_anchors_for_widget reason).

Derive a safe .md filename from a Workflowy node name for F12+4 materialize. Strips leading decoration/emoji, trailing #tags, illegal filename chars; collapses whitespace to underscores; guarantees a non-empty stem and a .md extension.

F12+4 leading-text fix: if the note's body (after optional YAML frontmatter) starts with prose BEFORE the first Markdown heading, synthesize a leading '# Leading text' H1 above that prose so the pre-heading text is not lost when the note is split into a heading subtree. No-op when the body already opens with a heading or is empty.

F12+4 hygiene: strip a LEADING Cartographer metadata block (MD_PATH: … --- or BEACON (…) … ---) from a node's note before materializing it to a .md. Needed because a Dump-Bay child that was already written back to the primary file via F12+3 carries such a block at the top of its note; without stripping it, that metadata would be written into the new .md as body content (and then split into bogus child nodes). Mirrors markdown_roundtrip._strip_md_path_block / _strip_md_ast_beacon_block but kept local to avoid importing module privates.

Bulk F12+4 helper: classify a node's note as a Cartographer FILE/FOLDER header. Returns ('Root'|'Path', value) or None using the strict first-line-only _extract_path_header_from_note. A folder/path node has a header whose value has no recognized file extension; a file node's value has one (e.g. .md/.py).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a Markdown file (.md/.markdown)? Used by the bulk walk + eligibility classifier to decide whether to recurse INTO a file node (markdown -> yes; any other extension -> skip+prune).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a FILE (has a filename extension) rather than a FOLDER segment? A folder node's Path: is a bare segment (no dot-extension); a file node's Path: ends in an extension. Used to distinguish path/folder nodes (recurse through) from file nodes (skip unless .md). Thin wrapper: the canonical implementation now lives in api_client_nexus (single source of truth, co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note + _classify_node_map_state); imported here via a function-scoped local import to avoid the api_client_nexus->server cycle, mirroring the other unguarded server->client local imports. NO inline fallback copy on purpose: a bool predicate has no safe 'unknown' value (returning False would mislabel a real file node as a folder and misroute the F12 menus), and if api_client_nexus is unimportable the whole server is non-functional anyway -- so we let the import raise loudly rather than keep a divergent second copy of the logic.

FIRST server-queried F12 menu-visibility check. Walks UP the nodes-export cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof, unlike the DOM) to classify the hovered node, then combines that with the client-reported visible/hidden child booleans to decide whether the F12+4 entry appears and which bulk sub-options enable. Returns {show, mode, visible_option_enabled, all_option_enabled, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+4 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_materialize). Reads node_id + has_visible_children/has_hidden_children from the payload, runs _classify_bulk_materialize_eligibility, and echoes the verdict back (with node_id for client-side correlation).

Zoom-proof resolver for F12+3: given ANY node_id, walk UP the /nodes-export cache ancestor chain (which never hides anything, unlike the zoomed-in DOM) to find the enclosing Markdown FILE node. If the node itself IS a markdown FILE node, returns it. Crucially IGNORES the md-in-md temp node's SECOND-line Path: (that node is never a reverse-Markdown target); the true primary file is the enclosing markdown FILE ancestor. Returns the FILE node's UUID, or None when no enclosing markdown file exists (e.g. inside a non-markdown file, or no file at all).

Cache-backed (zoom-proof) eligibility classifier for the BULK F12+3 menu entry. Decision tree is SIMPLER than F12+4 (no submenu for availability, no child-visibility input needed to decide SHOW): a markdown FILE node -> single F12+3 (mode='single', no bulk entry); a node INSIDE a mapped file -> no bulk entry (degenerates to standard single F12+3 on the enclosing file, which the server resolves zoom-safely); any node that is NOT a file node and NOT inside a file (a folder/Root: node OR a plain unmapped Workflowy node) -> bulk. Returns {show, mode, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+3 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_f12p3). Reads node_id, runs _classify_bulk_f12p3_eligibility, echoes the verdict {show,mode,reason,classification} back (with node_id for client-side correlation). No child-visibility input is needed (F12+3 bulk has no availability submenu).

Bulk F12+3 collection walk (source-agnostic, mirrors _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves plumbing). DFS over a tree (client visible-DOM payload OR nodes-export cache subtree) gathering MARKDOWN FILE nodes only. Per-node rules: a markdown FILE node QUALIFIES and we do NOT descend into it (F12+3 regenerates the whole file from its Workflowy subtree); a non-markdown FILE node is skipped+pruned; folder/Root: nodes and plain nodes are recursed THROUGH. Uses the universal first-line-only header classifier, so a md-in-md temp node (Path on line 2) is never mistaken for a file node. Returns ordered list of {id,name} file-node descriptors.

Bulk F12+3 execution handler (action=bulk_generate_markdown). Performs ONE gesture-level /nodes-export freshness read (L9 GESTURE) before any cache walk or child launch, builds the tree (walk_mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; 'all' -> cache subtree via _build_cache_subtree_for_bulk_materialize), runs _collect_bulk_f12p3_markdown_file_nodes to gather every Markdown FILE node, then fires ONE INDEPENDENT detached _start_carto_markdown_generate_job per file (N widget status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan). Every child consumes the one shared gesture snapshot and admits/claims its own region independently; this handler does not block.

WebSocket handler for the docked-modal SERVER render (action=render_markdown_modal). Direction-A request_id rail: composes Markdown STRING(s) on the server from a DOM/captured-tree payload: snapshot -> all row option-Y views, rows_only -> server-authored row list only, single -> one focus_leaf row, rows -> frozen-DOM multi-select minimal covering subtree via _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture. Echoes request_id. Never forces a /nodes-export refresh (detect+warn staleness). TASK-DISPATCHED from the reader loop (U4), and the three SYNCHRONOUS compose_markdown_modal_* calls run via asyncio.to_thread so a large compose cannot monopolize the event loop -- the task's S03 operation-boundary snapshot propagates into the thread (contextvars).

WebSocket handler for the slice-group copy button (action=compile_slice_search). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id). TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) so it can do a NESTED Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the ORIGINATING tab without deadlocking the single websocket_handler pump. Reads the live slice-group config from that tab, resolves the requested group_id (or active group), and compiles the Workflowy membership search string via the single Python compiler compile_slice_search_expression (#P -#P--deprecated OR ...). Replies compile_slice_search_result with request_id + expression.

WebSocket handler for the live F8 keypress (action=f8_expansion_plan). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id) carrying the visible DOM subtree. TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab to read the active slice group's prefixes + the live postfix config (one settings reader, no client-side policy). Then runs Phase 0 (validate_subtree_against_cache, fail-closed) and Phase 2 (build_expansion_plan) over the validated visible tree and replies f8_expansion_plan_result (echoing request_id) with {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand, warnings} for the client to execute mechanically. No fallback: on validation failure or no live tab it replies with an error the client surfaces loudly.

Apply-slice Tier-1 handler (action=render_slice_modal): the docked Markdown modal sourced from the CACHE-PROJECTED slice group instead of the live virtualized DOM. Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id); TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_f8_expansion_plan / _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab, which would deadlock the single websocket_handler pump if awaited inline. Resolves the requested slice group (by group_id, else active), then runs the SHARED cache-projection funnel build_stage1_base_tree (Phase 1 build_slice_subtree_from_cache -> Phase 2 build_expansion_plan -> Phase 3 apply_expansion_plan_to_subtree -> Phase 4 prune_collapsed_leaf_zombies) -- the EXACT SAME funnel _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache calls, so the Apply-slice modal and the slice-group GLIMPSE can never diverge on the projection (incl. the Phase-4 render-only zombie prune, the deliberate divergence from the live Workflowy expansion state) -- then _build_markdown_preview_from_tree (the SAME shared composer the live-DOM modal uses) with the _root_in_non_md_file_from_cache seed. Returns ONE Markdown STRING that is complete BY CONSTRUCTION (cache-sourced, not virtualized), so the dock can display it with no scroll/F8/refresh-dance and the client suppresses the scroll-to-bottom warning (cache_sourced=true). Replies render_slice_modal_result echoing request_id so the broker routes it to ONLY the originating tab. | Build the stable STRING key for a tree-view row's (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple, used both to key the Apply-slice SNAPSHOT map server-side and (echoed by the client on a row click) to select the exact occurrence in the SINGLE per-row path. NUL-joined ancestor_path so it cannot collide with a uuid; occurrence suffixed. Deterministic + pure -- the same row produces the same key on the original render and on any re-projection (MATCH = EMIT).

Build the SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE render_scope echo object for a cache-projected render. This is the ONE object every consumer (client adoptRenderScope -> per-tab render state + ribbon widgets + footer; and the MCP push tool output) treats as the normalized ground truth of what was ACTUALLY rendered, regardless of which SURFACE (ribbon click or MCP glimpse() call) triggered the render. Carries ONLY the normalized structured render-defining fields: scope identity (kind/group_id/group_name/root_uuid) + view params (sort_by/sort_direction/since object-or-null/headings_only). There is no pre-composed display string -- the status footer is the ONE consumer that renders a human string, composing it from THESE fields, so string-composition lives in exactly one place. kind is 'slice' (group at its own root), 'slice_override' (group tags scoped to an override root), 'raw_root' (bare root_uuid raw dump, no group -> the footer labels it 'raw dump of <root8>'), or 'lightning_rod' (a temporary Lightning Rod selection via the `lightning` param, which takes PRECEDENCE). LIGHTNING SELECTION: a lightning render carries ONE opaque `selection` object {mode:'gather'|'render_tags'|'render_search'|'render_symbols', + per-mode fields (tags+postfix_policy | query/query_mode | symbols/root_uuids/favor) + match_scope} that the client round-trips VERBATIM for BEHAVIOR (routing is by selection.mode, never selection_kind). selection_kind ('gather'|'tags'|'search'|'symbols') + workflowy_search_equivalent are DERIVED from selection.mode and are DISPLAY-ONLY (footer/status-bar label). UNMOORED SIGNAL: live_gui_sync_supported is a TOP-LEVEL bool emitted for EVERY kind (+ live_gui_sync_skipped_reason naming why when False) -- False for a raw dump (no membership search), a descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' render (inexpressible as a Workflowy search), a search_too_many_variants refusal, or any lightning selection; the client surfaces the unmoored state on the yellow bar. It is DISPLAY/observability only, never a behavior driver. EVERY kind also carries the explicit CONTENT/TREE CONTRACT fields content_format ('markdown'|'raw_text') + tree_mode ('render_tree'|'root_only') so the client never guesses how to paint the one rendered string or populate the top-half list (only a lightning GATHER is raw_text/root_only today). Pure + deterministic; no I/O.
old_result.role: _compose_render_scope(kind, group_id, group_name, root_uuid, sort_by, sort_direction, since, headings_only)

old_result.comment: Phase-E1 SPEC-AWARE BRIDGE to the ONE render_scope composer. Given a RESOLVED RenderProjectionSpec (kind/root/group already canonicalized by the caller's resolution step -- NOT the raw incoming spec), DELEGATE to _compose_render_scope by unpacking exactly the scalar params it already takes (Option A, Dan-decided: delegate, do NOT reimplement from spec.to_render_scope_fields(), so there stays ONE render_scope-assembly implementation and this never becomes a second scope factory / caller-side fabrication site). The is_raw_dump / root_overridden booleans the scalar composer wants are read straight off the spec's kind-derived properties (spec.is_raw_dump / spec.root_overridden), and sort_by is passed via spec.sort_by_internal() (the ONE wire-'none'<->internal-None translation). search_too_many_variants is a POST-RENDER fact (not a spec input field, per invariant 5) so it is threaded as an explicit kwarg here, exactly as the scalar composer already accepts it. This is the E1 seam that lets every downstream server call site (modal handler E3, content-return GLIMPSE paths E4, push frame E5) compose render_scope FROM the same spec it projected from, instead of from a parallel bag of locals -- the two-parallel-assembly-points seam Phase E removes. Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

The ONE inherited slice-group root policy seam shared by MCP/lens renders and every stored-root consumer (APPLY, copy-search, named merge, scoped reprojection, push and group purge). Delegates resolution to resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle with the caller's pinned map; exact UUIDs, clean prefixes including 8 hex, and AP-IDs are adopted with existing archive semantics. Corrective UUID shaves are rejected and only their speculative correction echo is discarded. Transport, scope notes and miss envelopes stay per-origin; explicit input roots keep the standard forgiving boundary.

PURE formatter for the ambiguous/missing error ENVELOPE returned by the cache-projection root_uuid resolution sites (the bare-root RAW-DUMP GLIMPSE, the slice-group override root, the push scope root, and Lightning Rod). Given a resolve_uuid_like_node_handle result that did NOT resolve (candidates present => ambiguous; else => missing), returns the standard {success:False, error, [candidates/matched_prefix_len/truncated], **extra} dict -- so the several sites can't DRIFT on the field set. Deliberately NOT a resolver wrapper: each caller keeps its own resolution and control flow (plain return vs await _reply) and its own error WORDING (via display/label); this only unifies the payload SHAPE. Chain-1 W4 (F5): in the MISSING branch, a refusal-reason operation (a sink, a write, an export, a purge preview) whose root names a visible archived node RAISES ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the exact §5.2/§5.3 text and provenance — before any file/modal/preview work; reads (reason None/flag) and no-context callers keep today's hint-only text. Returns None when the handle actually resolved (caller should not call it then). Pure; no I/O.

ONE handler for every cache-projected docked-modal render + per-row re-render (the 'Apply slice' feature). Resolves the four-cell scope truth table: slice (group_id), slice_override (group_id+root_uuid), raw_root (root_uuid only), lightning_rod (lightning{mode,...}; group-less, Phase-1-only via an injected member_predicate BY DEFAULT -- render_tags + postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) upgrades the cell to the shared build_stage1_base_tree funnel with one nested postfix config read). Lightning modes: gather (short-circuits to the raw-text tag outline), render_tags{tags} (DEFAULT: no config read; 'slice': one nested postfix config read), render_search{query,query_mode} (both scope via one frame root_uuid), and render_symbols{symbols,root_uuids,favor} (the tag-free beacon slice: roots via its own root_uuids -> their LCA, does one nested config read for the global-suppression filter, resolves via the shared _project_render_symbols_from_cache, and appends its unresolved/ambiguous report to the full-document reply), plus render_lens{lens,query?} (the recursive LensSpec cell: one nested config read, the shared immutable Stage-0 snapshot + transport-free _project_render_lens_from_cache, derived-LCA rooting, and explicit empty artifact). All five modes emit one opaque `selection` object into the render_scope. old_result.comment: GLIMPSE `since` Form-A window PARSER. Parses a time-window token into a duration in SECONDS (timestamps are epoch-seconds). Accepts a unit-suffixed integer/float -- s(econds) m(inutes) h(ours) d(ays) w(eeks) -- e.g. '3d','1w','12h','90m','45s'; a BARE number is interpreted as DAYS ('7' == '7d'), the common case. Whitespace-tolerant, case-insensitive. Returns None for a blank/None/garbage/non-positive token so the caller can raise an actionable error. Pure. | GLIMPSE `since` PRUNE -- the shared leaf-branch filter run LAST (after Phase1/2/3 AND after the timestamp reorder), on the already-final sorted forest. Decomposes the forest into root->leaf branches (same DFS the sort uses), keeps a branch iff its branch-date (via the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static -- created=leaf createdAt, modified=branch-max modifiedAt, IDENTICAL to the sort) is beyond the pivot: ascending -> STRICTLY GREATER than pivot (most-recent tail; the pivot node itself excluded, everything newer kept); descending -> STRICTLY LESS than pivot (the commensurate 'oldest tail', a don't-care corner but done right). A branch with no resolvable date is DROPPED (can't prove it's in the window). Then trie-merges the surviving branches back into a tree via the SAME _reorder pass with sort_by carried through, so straddled ancestors re-emit exactly as in the unfiltered render. Returns a NEW forest (inputs untouched); empty list when nothing survives.

GLIMPSE `since` Form-A (time-window) PIVOT. Data-relative leading edge (Dan): the pivot is the branch-date of the MOST RECENT leaf branch in the ALREADY-FINAL forest (ascending) minus the window -- so 'last 1 week' on data whose newest branch is 2 years old means the week ENDING at that 2-year-old edge, NOT wall-clock now. Descending flips to the OLDEST edge plus the window (the don't-care commensurate corner). Uses the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static for every branch date so it matches the sort. Returns the pivot epoch-seconds, or None if no branch has a resolvable date (caller then returns the tree unfiltered rather than erroring on empty data).

GLIMPSE `since="curated"` FORM-B PIVOT (the self-maintaining curation cursor). Walks the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, finds every node that has been CURATED = carries any tag matching an active slice prefix INCLUDING --deprecated variants but EXCLUDING the --suppress/--expand PRESENTATION variants (via node_is_curated_for_prefixes, threaded with the render caller's resolved match_scope -- the SAME SELECTION-stage scope knob Stage-1 membership uses, 'name' = title only so a note-body family tag never moves the cursor, 'name_and_note' = default NAME+NOTE -- deliberately looser than slice MEMBERSHIP on the triage axis, because deprecating a tag is itself a curation act the user must not re-encounter; suppressing/expanding one is a lens carve-out, NOT triage, and must not move the cursor -- Session-019 curated-cursor fix + match_scope plumbing). For each curated node it computes that node's branch-date using the SAME rule the sort uses (_branch_timestamp_key_static over the node's root->leaf cache path: created=the curated node's own createdAt; modified=branch-max modifiedAt down to it), and returns the MAX (ascending; MIN for descending) = the high-water mark. Everything strictly newer than this in the shared-tail prune is the UNCURATED tail. Returns None when NOTHING under root is curated yet (no group tag anywhere) so the tail shows the whole subtree (all of it is 'new since last curated'). Cache-only; pure aside from the cache read.

Phase-C DISK-TARGET UNIQUENESS check (SPEC v5 §5 step 11): no two preflighted items with a RESOLVED TARGET KEY -- actionable OR noop -- may claim the same disk target key. A noop row still asserts an intended end-state for its target; letting it collide with another row's mutation would make its ledger row dishonest. Returns a collisions list (batch preflight failure) or None.

Shared Q3 beacon batch orchestrator for ensure/remove. Ordinary per-item resolution and returned preflight failures are ledger rows, not batch vetoes; valid items continue through the existing JIT/CAS writer. Scope/cache/infrastructure failures and duplicate/disk-target collisions still abort. The ONE all-target lease acquisition, ownership, cancellation, and cleanup paths are unchanged; any lease refusal still blocks all eligible writes. Disk-only with complete partial-success ledger. Policy addendum: docs/BEACON-BATCH-PARTIAL-SUCCESS.md. NON-BLOCKING (NBBW): Phase B resolution runs in a worker thread (private loop, cache-only) and the client preflight/plan/commit bodies run in worker threads -- the commit thread is never abandoned on cancellation, so the lease release in finally still follows the last disk write. GLOBAL SUPPRESSION: symbol resolution honours #wfy-suppress via _beacon_symbol_suppress_tags (fail-loud read); a suppressed-only item is an item-local all_suppressed row, never written. COMMENT CONFLICTS (2R4E1P): a fill-mode conflict is KEPT, never an error -- the labels are still ensured, comment_outcome='kept_existing_conflict' rides every row status (committed/noop alike) with a warning carrying BOTH texts; the batch result gains a top-level warnings list and a summary.comment_conflicts_kept count, which make_mutation_ack lifts to the ack's warnings. ATOMIC OPT-IN ([ap:LPC157] residue): spec.atomic=true (default false) restores the strict preflight veto AFTER Phase C and BEFORE lease acquisition -- any item failure leaves every other row not_run with zero writes and no lease (the failing item keeps its error row); a mid-batch commit failure is still per item (writes are individually CAS-atomic, no rollback exists). ONE-LINE SUMMARY: the result carries a top-level summary_line ('N committed · M noop · K failed (...)' -- the single failure's symbol/kind/reason, else the distinct failure kinds) so an agent can act without reading the ledger.

old_result.comment: Cache-only GLIMPSE path for a slice group (no DOM/extract_dom): the content-return originator of a slice render. Reads the live slice-group config (tab-agnostic get_slice_group_config -- the ONLY WS touch, for OPTIONS not DOM), resolves the requested slice_group id-OR-name via the SHARED _resolve_slice_group_handle (exact id -> unique 'grp-' prefix -> case-insensitive name fallback -- the SAME resolver the push path uses, so the two can't drift), derives its root_uuid + active prefixes + effective sort, optionally resolves a root_uuid_override (the slice_override scope) or a stop-at-child-anchors boundary predicate, and builds ONE RenderProjectionSpec BEFORE projecting so STAGE-1 admission (exclude_completed/match_scope) is read off the spec. Output is structurally identical to a live-DOM GLIMPSE of the same expanded slice, so a session can be initialized with no human at the Workflowy GUI. Chain-1 r2 (F5): a sink aimed at a stored root that names a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal before any render/file work. Chain-2 r1 (F1): with NO override, the EFFECTIVE STORED root itself resolves through the SAME shared composite resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle the override root gets (live legs first, then the archive legs — the fallback gate and record_archive_served ride inside it), so an exported-and-deleted stored root is served by the automatic fallback re-run (banner + provenance via the finalizer) and an include-mode run records the archive answer; a live stored root resolves to itself unchanged, and an unknown one stays unresolved for the Stage-1 absent-root branch (today's error, sink refusal intact). Chain-2 r2 (R1): a SHAVED corrective match of the stored root is REJECTED, never adopted — the stored identity and the pre-r1 miss policy are preserved (uuid_resolution_was_shave classifies the outcome; the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded; the raw root falls to the absent-root branch) — while an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2) and keeps the archive repair. No second resolver and no per-carrier banner copy: the lens group atom's inherited root shares this exact seam via lens_engine._resolve_root.

old_result.comment: PUSH-TO-MODAL path for glimpse(push_to_modal=True): instead of RETURNING the rendered content to the agent, it COMMANDS the target Workflowy tab to render the requested SERVER-SIDE SCOPE into its docked Markdown modal -- the server-push twin of a human clicking APPLY. Chain-1 W4 (F5): the funnel's resolve-HERE-before-the-round-trip doctrine now covers the render_lens cell's atom roots too -- a root naming a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal (the docked modal never serves archives), so a push can never ack success and then fail tab-side. Chain-1 r2 (R2-W2): the resolve-HERE doctrine now covers every indirect selection as well -- a render_lens GROUP atom pre-flights its group's STORED root (an explicit root_handle override is the target and wins; a bare group atom rides the stored default, so a recursive merged lens cannot hide an archived effective root), the render_symbols cell resolves its roots and runs its items through the SHARED _resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache router (live legs first; an archived root or item refuses before any command; items still ride verbatim per D5), and the direct slice-group cell resolves the chosen group's STORED root when no override root is present. Handles the full (slice_group, root_uuid) truth table: slice_group only (resolve id-or-name -> canonical group_id via the SHARED Layer-1 _resolve_slice_group_handle -- the SAME id/prefix/case-insensitive-name resolver _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache uses), root_uuid only (resolve prefix-tolerantly via the SHARED resolve_uuid_like_node_handle -> a RAW-DUMP push, the zero-token 'show me this anchor' command), or BOTH (slice lens scoped to an override root). All resolution happens HERE (before the round-trip) so a bad group name / missing UUID fails loudly early. Sends a Direction-A 'apply_slice_in_dock' frame carrying whichever of {group_id, root_uuid} are present + the AGENT-SUPPLIED sort/since as an EXPLICIT override (never the tab's global dock sort) via the generic _ws_request_response rail; returns the tab's ack. The tab-side dispatch invokes the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock (same fn the APPLY button uses), so the dock render + (for a slice) live-GUI-sync watcher are identical to a manual Apply; a raw-dump push installs NO watcher (no search/plan). The caller (glimpse) guards a bare live-DOM push (neither scope) as the only error.

UUID-hallucination HARDENING for a render_spec-driven GLIMPSE (the render_spec="modal"/blob path). Given a deserialized RenderProjectionSpec + the /nodes-export cache map, canonicalize EVERY UUID the spec carries -- root_uuid, focus.uuid, and EVERY focus.ancestor_path entry -- through the SHARED prefix-tolerant Layer-1 resolver resolve_uuid_like_node_handle (the exact machine SCRY / anchor / snippet callers use). Grace runs BEFORE the exact (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) focus match downstream, so it only CANONICALIZES a possibly-drifted string to its cache UUID; it NEVER loosens the occurrence-exact match itself (a canonicalized triple still resolves to exactly one occurrence via _resolve_focus_index_path). On the render_spec="modal" path the UUIDs are already server-canonical (near-no-op belt-and-suspenders); on the pasted-blob fallback path this is the real net against an agent-drifted UUID in the chain. A UUID that stays unresolved (no exact hit, no unique prefix) or is ambiguous is LEFT AS-IS (best-effort): a bad focus already fails safe to the whole document downstream, and a bad root_uuid surfaces its own cache-miss error in the dispatch that follows. Returns a NEW spec via with_overrides; the input spec (frozen) is never mutated. Pure; no I/O beyond reading the passed cache map.

Dispatch a resolved RenderProjectionSpec to the right cache-render helper by spec.kind -- the shared tail for BOTH render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (the "modal" WS query and the pasted-blob fallback). It routes the (slice|slice_override) cells to _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache (passing spec.group_id as slice_group, the resolved root as root_uuid_override for slice_override, and spec.focus) and the raw_root cell to _glimpse_root_uuid_from_cache (passing spec.root_uuid + spec.focus). The lightning_rod cell (ap:GLMPMODAL) re-projects the FOURTH scope by reading spec.lightning['mode'] and calling the SAME projector a fresh lightning_rod() call uses (_lightning_rod_from_cache for gather/render_tags/render_search; _lightning_rod_render_symbols for render_symbols): the opaque lightning selection is passed through verbatim, so no new render path is introduced. Each mode keeps its own constraints (render_symbols Markdown-only + roots via its own selection.root_uuids; gather raw-text/root_only; since='curated' rejected inside the projector). FOCUS on a lightning modal read is now SUPPORTED for the node-tree modes (render_tags/render_search/render_symbols): spec.focus is threaded into the projector and resolved occurrence-exactly by the shared render_stage2_filter_sort focus authority -- the ONLY residual rejection is gather+focus (a gather is a tag outline with one synthetic root row, so a real row focus is a category error). Every view knob (as_markdown / sort / since / headings_only / match_scope / descend_policy) is read off the spec, so the render is byte-identical to the equivalent explicit-arg GLIMPSE -- the whole point of routing through the ONE spec object. descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' is honored for the raw_root cell by building the anchor-boundary predicate here (the one config-read WS touch), exactly as the explicit-arg root_uuid path does.

The AGENT-OVERRIDE seam for the render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (render_spec="modal" AND the pasted-blob fallback). Given the RESOLVED, tab-sourced (or pasted) RenderProjectionSpec and the agent's TRI-STATE view overrides (as_markdown / headings_only / sort_by / sort_direction / since; None = inherit what the modal is showing, a value = explicit override), it (1) merges the non-None overrides onto the spec via the SINGLE normalized mutator spec.with_view_overrides (which re-runs the ONE normalizer and preserves the resolved kind via kind_hint -- NOT raw with_overrides), then (2) runs the LOUD combination guards ONCE on the FINAL merged spec, where spec.focus and spec.kind are known. The two guards (Dan-decided): (A) a sort override (sort_by/sort_direction supplied) is REJECTED when spec.focus is present -- sorting a single focused option-Y row is ill-defined; the user re-roots the modal at that subtree instead; (B) a since override is REJECTED when spec.focus is present (a tail/window over the whole underlying scope intersected with a focused row is meaningless). Beyond focus, the standard since preconditions are enforced by reading the FINAL SinceSpec object fields; curated requires a slice/slice_override scope. Returns (spec, None) on success or (spec, error_dict) on a rejected combination. This is the ONLY place agent view overrides are applied to a render_spec spec, so both render_spec sub-paths share ONE override+guard implementation.

Pure pre-order DFS that returns the FIRST node in a forest whose id/uuid matches -- the CANONICAL (unsorted) node lookup for the Scoped Lightning Rod occurrence-exact re-root pre-step in _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture. After the sorted forest is pruned to a clicked occurrence and that occurrence's LEAF UUIDs are collected, this locates the clicked node's canonical node in the UNSORTED captured forest so its subtree can be rebuilt DE-MIRRORED (filtered to those leaf UUIDs via build_selected_subtree_from_forest). Relies on the v1 invariant that a Workflowy UUID appears AT MOST ONCE in the raw (unsorted) tree -- Workflowy 'mirrors' are explicitly UNSUPPORTED in v1 -- so 'the first match' IS 'the only match'. Returns None if not found. The UUID (not object identity) is the ONLY valid bridge between the sorted shadow-copy tree and the canonical tree.

SLICE-BASE projection for a SLICE-FROZEN Scoped Lightning Rod. Deserializes the client's durable base_render_spec (RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob) and RE-PROJECTS that scope from the /nodes-export cache into a single render TREE, so _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture can then treat it EXACTLY like a DOM captured_tree (same re-root pre-step, same build_selected_subtree_from_forest filter, same _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture compose). It REUSES the canonical funnels -- build_stage1_base_tree for a slice / slice_override scope (via the SAME nested get_slice_group_config Direction-A read the sibling _handle_render_slice_modal uses), and build_slice_subtree_from_cache(member_all=True) for a raw_root scope -- and NEVER inlines a new projection. Returns (tree, None) on success or (None, error_dict) on any failure (no tab, no group, empty group, cache miss), so the caller replies verbatim. A lightning_rod base is rejected (a prior Lightning render is already ephemeral and arrives as captured_tree, never as a durable base spec). The projected tree is a first-class EPHEMERAL dom_capture from the caller onward -- the one-way collapse of the slice, NEVER re-laundered into a durable spec. STAGE-1 POLICY THREADING (post-Sol-audit Finding 3): spec.exclude_completed and spec.descend_policy's shared anchor boundary now reach the projection -- they were silently dropped before, so a frozen scope's Scoped re-projection could surface completed nodes and descend through child anchors the original render excluded.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD over a FROZEN DOM view (action=render_lightning_dom_capture). The DOM-frozen half of the Scoped toggle: the dock is showing an EPHEMERAL captured DOM forest and the user fired a Lightning Rod with [Scoped] ON, so the search is confined to that on-screen forest rather than walking the whole cache root. Reads the frame's captured_tree + opaque lightning selection {mode, tags?, query?, query_mode?, match_scope, postfix_policy?}; builds the SAME singular predicate the cache path uses (build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) and filters the forest via build_selected_subtree_from_forest; then composes through the EXISTING _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture machinery via its pre_filter seam, so the artifact stays a first-class kind='dom_capture' (EPHEMERAL -- the client provenance adapter must never launder it into a durable RenderProjectionSpec). gather short-circuits to gather_tags_in_forest -> render_tags_outline (raw_text/root_only), the forest sibling of the cache gather seam. No cache walk, no slice config; render_symbols is NOT supported here (it is inherently a cache-resolution mode). postfix_policy='slice' is LOUD-REJECTED in v1 (ap:IMPPTX): the full Stage-1 funnel hydrates expansions from the raw /nodes-export cache, which would silently graft nodes from OUTSIDE the ephemeral frozen domain (a source-correct forest hydrator is a separate future feature). The rejection now runs BEFORE any source-fork projection (post-Sol-audit Finding 4), so an unsupported request fails with its own actionable error -- never masked by a config/projection failure and never after wasted projection work. Task-dispatched like the sibling modal handlers. A malformed query fails LOUD (lightning_rod_query_error); an empty match renders an empty dom_capture document (valid 'no matches'), never an error.

The DOM-FROZEN sibling of _glimpse_dispatch_spec for render_spec="modal". It does NOT use the cache-projection path, because a frozen DOM view is a DIFFERENT SOURCE AXIS: an EPHEMERAL captured tree the tab pinned at freeze, not a durable /nodes-export scope. It composes that captured tree through the SAME composer + row-identity + focus primitives the cache path uses: normalize the {root,children} payload to one forest; prepare_stage2_render_forest for sort/since/counts (curated since is rejected -- no slice tags); then the shared materializer. TWO deliberate departures from the cache tail: (1) focus is EXACT-OR-ERROR -- an unresolvable focus triple returns a loud stale error, not the lenient whole-document fallback; (2) full/UUID mode is supported ONLY with headings_only=True (the {UUID<->title} harvest; a full body dump is rejected). The render_scope echo is honest kind='dom_capture' (durable_scope=False, live_gui_sync_supported=False) -- it never masquerades as raw_root/slice. GUARDRAIL: the captured tree is never folded into a RenderProjectionSpec. ADVISORY PROVENANCE (S04 Remediation Chain 4): the hard-barrier read advisory is a cache-provenance claim applied ONLY when the composed content is /nodes-export-derived -- the cache_sourced kwarg (default False, this function composes browser-captured trees) is carried explicitly to the ONE advisory authority; the render_spec="modal" dom_captured_tree read and genuinely DOM-frozen Scoped Lightning are unadvised, while a slice-frozen Scoped run passes cache_sourced=True and stays advised.

THE render_spec="modal" path -- the primary 'GLIMPSE what I'm looking at in the docked modal' capability. Issues ONE Direction-A get_current_modal_render_spec WS query to the target tab via the generic _ws_request_response rail (request_id correlation; the tab answers from its OWN dockedSliceContext.render_spec + selected-row triple -- a LEAF query, NO nested back-to-tab round trip, so NO deadlock-note applies). Deserializes the reply's render_spec blob into a RenderProjectionSpec via from_render_spec_blob (the SAME normalizer every entry point uses), applies UUID prefix-grace to every UUID in the spec (root + focus triple) via _grace_resolve_spec_uuids against the /nodes-export cache, then dispatches by kind through _glimpse_dispatch_spec -> the existing focused-projection helpers. DETERMINISTIC end-to-end: the agent types ZERO UUIDs (the blob comes from the tab's own server-adopted scope), and SERVER code (not the agent) deserializes + re-projects, so this is the (b)-variant architecture Dan chose -- the Python composer stays the sole renderer, no client-string round-trips through the server. Fails loudly if the tab has no cache-sourced render to report (success:false + a clear message telling the human to Apply a slice / push a scope first).

THE ONE agent-facing output-contract finalizer for the GLIMPSE FAMILY of MCP tools -- its consumers are the glimpse family (workflowy_glimpse), lightning_rod, anchor.dock.render, and slice_group render/sift/merge.render. Given the rich internal result dict every render helper builds, it delivers to the AGENT exactly what the human wants to see -- and nothing redundant. Rule: (1) output_file set -> pass the file-write summary through unchanged (the disk write is the deliverable, not the string). (2) result is not a dict -> already a bare value, pass through. (3) MARKDOWN / RAW-TEXT mode -- a RENDERED TEXT STRING is present -> return it RAW (real newlines, like read_text_file), NOTHING ELSE: preview_markdown (every Markdown-mode render across GLIMPSE live-DOM / slice_group / raw root_uuid / render_spec modal+blob / dom_capture, AND Lightning Rod render_tags/render_search/render_symbols) OR preview_text (the Lightning Rod gather raw-text tag outline, byte-identical to the modal's Gather). The rendered string IS the whole semantic payload in this mode, so no envelope is wanted. This is the single future-proof seam: ANY future raw-text mode just fills preview_text (or preview_markdown) and is delivered raw with ZERO further change here. (4) FULL / UUID mode -- a preview_tree is present -> return the STRUCTURED DICT, preserving preview_tree AND all the genuinely-useful metadata (node_count, depth, _source, render_scope, since_applied, ...), but STRIPPING ONLY the redundant CONTENT twins: `rows` (modal tree-view metadata that duplicates preview_tree) and any stray preview_markdown/preview_text; additionally, when headings_only=True (the compact UUID-harvest pass), strip bulky live-DOM raw `root`/`children` to keep the payload small. Full mode is for structural / UUID work, so the stats ARE wanted here -- only the duplicative rows/markdown clutter is dropped. (5) everything else (errors success:false, push_to_modal acks, gather's structured tag list when preview_text is somehow absent, empty payloads with neither field) -> pass the structured dict through unchanged so failures/acks still signal correctly. The rich internal payloads (rows, render_scope, since_applied, node_count) are LEFT INTACT on the helper returns -- they still flow to the browser/modal WS reply handlers that need them; this finalizer only shapes the AGENT-facing tool return. preview_markdown is checked before preview_text before preview_tree: at most one is ever populated on a given result, so order is belt-and-suspenders. STALE-FOCUS GUARD [ap:XDVDRG]: a Markdown/raw-text result that carries focus_unresolved is NEVER delivered raw -- its always-empty string would read as a legitimately empty view; the structured stale payload is returned instead (success flipped to false, the empty preview twins and modal rows dropped, error + focus_unresolved kept) so the shared family error boundary surfaces the loud stale-focus error. A legitimate empty (empty since-window, no focus_unresolved) still returns its raw '' when NO recency selection is active -- the (empty) stub then fires at the public funnel (9a); when a recency selection IS active ([ap:TVIIBN] 4e), the Markdown body is passed through the ONE empty-output stub (stub_empty_text_result, caveat C1) and the result opens with ONE '> Recency selection: ...' rule line naming what was chosen and teaching that sort_direction only orders (the structured full/UUID twin carries the same sentence as a top-level recency_header key, no quote marker). The header text is composed ONLY by _recency_header_sentence -- one composer, no second header writer; the browser modal / push / file paths never pass through here and are untouched by construction.

Pure simple-form identity interpretation over caller-injected cache/config operands. Reuses the existing node/group resolvers and Dock classifier, and the two pure decisions; returns a lowering or read_note intent, never acquires state or renders. Transport and note-read control flow stay per origin.

ONE estate entry through the EXISTING server render funnel (no new render path): a named-group entry normalizes via normalize_from_glimpse_args(group_id=<handle>, match_scope='name') — a slice spec at the group's stored root with its saved default sort/policy, resolved by the SAME _resolve_slice_group_handle glimpse(group_handle=…) uses; a spec entry deserializes via RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob (spec VERBATIM, focus included), rides the UUID prefix-grace, then the loud focus-intent-loss check (a saved selection that collapses to None aborts the entry rather than dumping the whole scope). Both go through the ONE override+guard seam (_apply_modal_view_overrides_and_guard → with_view_overrides) and _glimpse_dispatch_spec — which honors single-row AND mode='rows' covering-subtree focus via the shared Stage-2 tail, and NEVER runs the in-band Anchor-Dock raw-dump guard (every estate entry passes as allow_anchor_dock=true by construction). Returns a flat per-entry record; every failure shape (invalid entry, unresolvable group, root_not_in_cache, stale focus, guard rejection, funnel error, unexpected exception) is a LOUD record — the caller keeps rendering the others. Chain-1 r2 (F5/R2-W1): ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError is the one re-raised exception — an entry whose root names a visible archived node refuses the WHOLE sink call with the universal envelope, never an isolated failed row an assembly could write into a delivery-success file.

Estate OUTPUT origin: simple forms/full JSON directly or a Dock/estate handle, interpreted by the pure grammar and injected-snapshot resolver. Dock first (no note read), else ONE live _node_read_impl; entries never nest. Lowered entries use the same TWO-branch _glimpse_estate_render_entry and _glimpse_dispatch_spec. Existing alias/title headings, scope echoes, per-entry isolation, view overrides, output_file and reserved tabs semantics remain; no renderer, wire, cache writer or transport fork. Chain 1 r2 (WO [ap:4Q3LQV] W1): under repository_view the estate delivers the ONE coherence advisory authority's warning on its own reply -- the canonical line on the screen (text adapter on the document part, below the composed '> ' lines) and the structured key on the successful file acknowledgement -- while every file byte and assembled D stays clean; applicability rides the operation's captured status and is byte-identical when clean or with the flag off.

GLIMPSE ingress: modal sentinel first; simple forms use the pure grammar and snapshot resolver before the existing spec/grace/view-override/push/render path. Explicit scope truth table and low-level defaults remain unchanged. [ap:EPR86W] part a: the raw-root cell honours recursive=False (root + direct children only, via the ONE shared walker's max_depth gate) and threads it to the push funnel; recursive=False on a slice-group scope or a live-DOM GLIMPSE is refused loudly at the boundary (and, for blobs, at the ONE spec normalizer).

old_result.comment: Server helper: acquire the live WS peer (grace wait) and fetch the target tab's extension settings, returning normalized (note_session_tags, global_tags, default_parent). Fails loudly if no tab is reachable. Shared by both note-session MCP tools. Archive Reads U3: the raw reply ALSO feeds remember_archive_folder_from_reply — the daemon's memory of the extension's archive_folder option, so archive reads never need a tab (the file write defers inside an augmented operation, Axiom 5/E36).

Extract the configured LOCAL-anchor postfix word list from a get_extension_settings raw reply, defaulting to [DEFAULT_LOCAL_ANCHOR_POSTFIX] ('local') when absent/empty/malformed. The ONE server-side place the local-postfix default lives -- the Dock-favorites unit added the exact siblings _favorite_anchor_postfixes_from_reply / _deprecated_anchor_postfixes_from_reply and the ONE aggregator _anchor_postfix_kwargs_from_reply, so list_anchors and every classify/boundary call site read the full family vocabulary identically (no per-site defaulting, no drift). Rides in the raw reply (note_session_local_postfixes) rather than a widened _resolve_note_session_config tuple, to avoid an arity change across every existing unpack site.

Extract the configured FAVORITE-anchor postfix word list from a get_extension_settings raw reply (note_session_favorite_postfixes), defaulting to [DEFAULT_FAVORITE_ANCHOR_POSTFIX] ('fav') when absent/empty/malformed -- the exact sibling of _local_anchor_postfixes_from_reply (trim, strip one leading '#', drop non-strings/empties, order-preserving de-dup). The ONE server-side place the favorite-postfix default lives, so an extension that never sends the new key keeps working unchanged (I8: no vocabulary hardcoded in behaviour; words come from the reply through this helper).

Server helper for the slice-group MCP tools: acquire the live WS peer (grace wait) and read the target tab's LIVE slice-group config via client.get_slice_group_config -> returns (groups, active_id, postfixes_dict, global_never_expand, raw). Fails loudly if no tab. The server is the single settings reader (one source of truth), exactly like _resolve_note_session_config for anchors.

CFGOP1: the ONE nested get_slice_group_config TRANSPORT for the SIX browser-facing handlers/helpers that read the live slice-group/postfix config (_handle_compile_slice_search, _handle_f8_expansion_plan, _handle_render_slice_modal's slice cell + Lightning render_tags postfix_policy='slice' branch + render_symbols suppression read, and _project_slice_base_tree_for_scoped_lightning). Consolidates the six hand-duplicated blocks (ws-acquire -> _ws_request_response('get_slice_group_config', target_endpoint_id=ORIGINATING tab, tab_optional for the endpoint-absent case, 15s) -> unknown_endpoint ghost catch -> per-site error envelope) into ONE Stage-0 transport helper. Per the STAGE-0 DOCTRINE: transport/interpretation envelopes consolidate, control flow NEVER does -- each caller keeps its own group resolution, operand parsing (parse_slice_policy_config), and reply shape. The WSLIVE2 ghost rail is PRESERVED exactly: route by the originating tab's real endpoint_id (never degraded to unknown_target_tab masking); a ghost surfaces as code='unknown_endpoint' so the client retries after the broker's re-register broadcast. context = the caller's verb-phrase (error wording stays per-site); error_type (site 6's scoped_lightning_config_read_failed) folds into BOTH envelopes. Returns (reply, None) on success or (None, envelope) on any failure.

SGSORT semantic resolve-point for a slice group's effective render sort. Preserves the inviolable None-vs-'none' distinction until the live chosen group dict is in hand: Python None / JSON null inherits the group's stored default_sort_by + default_sort_direction pair; the string 'none' is explicit document order and canonicalizes direction to asc; created/modified pass through with sanitized direction. Called only at the two slice config resolve-points (_glimpse_slice_group_from_cache and _handle_render_slice_modal), so downstream render_scope/render-tail code sees only resolved wire values and never re-decides inheritance.

Advisory short-name collision detector for slice-group WRITES (create / update-rename / merge.persist). Parses the candidate full name with the ONE grammar parser and lists every OTHER leaf group whose semantic short name collides (case-insensitive); expander/category rows and empty short names never participate (they are not short-name-resolvable), and an expander CANDIDATE yields no warnings (its short name is organizational, not a resolvable handle). Non-fatal by design: the report-only result rides in the write reply as short_name_collisions so an agent learns at WRITE time that the new name will be ambiguous as a short handle (the resolver still fails loudly with colliding_ids at USE time). Pure; no I/O.

Resolve an agent-supplied slice-group id against the in-hand groups list, with the SAME hallucinated-UUID prefix backtracking used everywhere else (anchor/snippet/SCRY) via the SHARED _resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback -- but with key_prefix='grp-' since group ids are 'grp-'+uuid4().hex (not in the /nodes-export cache; matched against the slice-group config instead). Returns (index, error_dict): exact id wins; else a UNIQUE prefix match is adopted silently; a MULTI prefix match returns an error with candidate ids; no match returns a not-found error. None error => index valid.

Layer-1 shared slice-group HANDLE resolver ([ap:9QK4MV] refactor; semantic short names added 2026). Resolve an agent-supplied slice_group handle against an in-hand groups list, returning (group_dict|None, error|None). Resolution order: (1) exact id; (2) unique 'grp-' prefix via _resolve_slice_group_id; (3) case-insensitive FULL stored-name match (pipe path + trailing [n] included); (4) case-insensitive semantic SHORT-name match -- the final pipe segment, index-stripped, via the ONE grammar parser parse_slice_group_name; LEAF groups only, the supplied handle participates only when it parses as a bare leaf (a trailing [n] ON THE HANDLE is tolerated), empty short names never match. At every name stage: 1 hit -> adopt; >1 -> colliding_ids error (never auto-pick); a stage-3 full-name hit outranks stage-4 short-name hits. Pure: no network/cache/I/O. This is the ONE home for 'resolve a slice-group handle' -- every render/CRUD/purge site AND the LensSpec group-atom resolver (via its raise-style adapter) route through here, so the handle grammar can never drift between surfaces.

MCP tool wrapper: resolve live config from the target tab, then delegate to client.list_note_sessions (cache walk + nested-priority DFS). Exposed publicly as 'list_anchors' (anchor = the user-facing name for what the internals still call note_session).

Internal anchor listing wrapper: public list_anchors calls it with default flags; the private widget endpoint passes tree/raw/local/favorites flags. Keeps live config resolution + client.list_note_sessions delegation in one place while preserving the public MCP tool signature. favorites_only defaults to FALSE here so the legacy list_anchors tool (all flags False) is unchanged; the public anchor.dock.list default (true) lives in _anchor_dock_list_impl alone.

MCP tool: return the user's canonical/global tag vocabulary (a routing HINT, not a constraint) read from SHARED cross-tab extension config via the tab-agnostic _resolve_note_session_config path. Tab-agnostic by design — never errors under multi-tab; only fails when no tab is reachable.

MCP tool wrapper: resolve default parent + anchor tag(s) from the target tab when not passed, then delegate to client.create_note_session (single ETCH). Fails loudly with no silent root fallback. local=True -> resolve the FIRST configured local postfix (via _local_anchor_postfixes_from_reply) and pass it as local_postfix so the anchor tag becomes base--local (a LOCAL anchor: hidden from list_anchors but still a descendants boundary). Exposed publicly as 'create_anchor' with exposed kwarg anchor_tag (internals still say note_session / session_tags).

MCP tool wrapper: resolve live anchor tags from the target tab, guard the 'note session' terminology rule, then delegate to client.update_note_session (rename base name preserving tags / replace note; mapped-subtree advisory surfaced for the agent to report). Exposed publicly as 'update_anchor' (internals still say note_session).

MCP tool wrapper: validate the EXACTLY-ONE payload contract (nodes XOR note_file XOR content; loud on both/neither/all; checked FIRST, before any live config read), then delegate to client.add_to_anchor (placement-guarded ETCH). The guard (folder + non-Markdown-file rejection) is the only value-add over workflowy_etch; dialect-neutral capture primitive for anchors. note_file: absolute-path UTF-8 text file -> exactly ONE node (file stem = name, raw text = note). content: raw string with required name= -> exactly ONE node (name = NAME, content = NOTE). name: optional override with note_file (skips stem as name).

F12+4 hygiene: strip a LEADING Cartographer metadata block (MD_PATH: … --- or BEACON (…) … ---) from a node's note before materializing it to a .md. Needed because a Dump-Bay child that was already written back to the primary file via F12+3 carries such a block at the top of its note; without stripping it, that metadata would be written into the new .md as body content (and then split into bogus child nodes). Mirrors markdown_roundtrip._strip_md_path_block / _strip_md_ast_beacon_block but kept local to avoid importing module privates.

Bulk F12+4 helper: classify a node's note as a Cartographer FILE/FOLDER header. Returns ('Root'|'Path', value) or None using the strict first-line-only _extract_path_header_from_note. A folder/path node has a header whose value has no recognized file extension; a file node's value has one (e.g. .md/.py).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a Markdown file (.md/.markdown)? Used by the bulk walk + eligibility classifier to decide whether to recurse INTO a file node (markdown -> yes; any other extension -> skip+prune).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a FILE (has a filename extension) rather than a FOLDER segment? A folder node's Path: is a bare segment (no dot-extension); a file node's Path: ends in an extension. Used to distinguish path/folder nodes (recurse through) from file nodes (skip unless .md). Thin wrapper: the canonical implementation now lives in api_client_nexus (single source of truth, co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note + _classify_node_map_state); imported here via a function-scoped local import to avoid the api_client_nexus->server cycle, mirroring the other unguarded server->client local imports. NO inline fallback copy on purpose: a bool predicate has no safe 'unknown' value (returning False would mislabel a real file node as a folder and misroute the F12 menus), and if api_client_nexus is unimportable the whole server is non-functional anyway -- so we let the import raise loudly rather than keep a divergent second copy of the logic.

Walks UP the nodes-export cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof, unlike the DOM) to classify the hovered node, then combines that with the client-reported visible/hidden child booleans to decide whether the F12+4 entry appears and which bulk sub-options enable. Returns {show, mode, visible_option_enabled, all_option_enabled, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+4 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_materialize). Reads node_id + has_visible_children/has_hidden_children from the payload, runs _classify_bulk_materialize_eligibility, and echoes the verdict back (with node_id for client-side correlation).

Zoom-proof resolver for F12+3: given ANY node_id, walk UP the /nodes-export cache ancestor chain (which never hides anything, unlike the zoomed-in DOM) to find the enclosing Markdown FILE node. If the node itself IS a markdown FILE node, returns it. Crucially IGNORES the md-in-md temp node's SECOND-line Path: (that node is never a reverse-Markdown target); the true primary file is the enclosing markdown FILE ancestor. Returns the FILE node's UUID, or None when no enclosing markdown file exists (e.g. inside a non-markdown file, or no file at all).

Cache-backed (zoom-proof) eligibility classifier for the BULK F12+3 menu entry. Decision tree is SIMPLER than F12+4 (no submenu for availability, no child-visibility input needed to decide SHOW): a markdown FILE node -> single F12+3 (mode='single', no bulk entry); a node INSIDE a mapped file -> no bulk entry (degenerates to standard single F12+3 on the enclosing file, which the server resolves zoom-safely); any node that is NOT a file node and NOT inside a file (a folder/Root: node OR a plain unmapped Workflowy node) -> bulk. Returns {show, mode, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+3 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_f12p3). Reads node_id, runs _classify_bulk_f12p3_eligibility, echoes the verdict {show,mode,reason,classification} back (with node_id for client-side correlation). No child-visibility input is needed (F12+3 bulk has no availability submenu).

Bulk F12+3 collection walk (source-agnostic, mirrors _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves plumbing). DFS over a tree (client visible-DOM payload OR nodes-export cache subtree) gathering MARKDOWN FILE nodes only. Per-node rules: a markdown FILE node QUALIFIES and we do NOT descend into it (F12+3 regenerates the whole file from its Workflowy subtree); a non-markdown FILE node is skipped+pruned; folder/Root: nodes and plain nodes are recursed THROUGH. Uses the universal first-line-only header classifier, so a md-in-md temp node (Path on line 2) is never mistaken for a file node. Returns ordered list of {id,name} file-node descriptors.

Bulk F12+3 execution handler (action=bulk_generate_markdown). Performs ONE gesture-level /nodes-export freshness read (L9 GESTURE) before any cache walk or child launch, builds the tree (walk_mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; 'all' -> cache subtree via _build_cache_subtree_for_bulk_materialize), runs _collect_bulk_f12p3_markdown_file_nodes to gather every Markdown FILE node, then fires ONE INDEPENDENT detached _start_carto_markdown_generate_job per file (N widget status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan). Every child consumes the one shared gesture snapshot and admits/claims its own region independently; this handler does not block.

WebSocket handler for the docked-modal SERVER render (action=render_markdown_modal). Direction-A request_id rail: composes Markdown STRING(s) on the server from a DOM/captured-tree payload: snapshot -> all row option-Y views, rows_only -> server-authored row list only, single -> one focus_leaf row, rows -> frozen-DOM multi-select minimal covering subtree via _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture. Echoes request_id. Never forces a /nodes-export refresh (detect+warn staleness). TASK-DISPATCHED from the reader loop (U4), and the three SYNCHRONOUS compose_markdown_modal_* calls run via asyncio.to_thread so a large compose cannot monopolize the event loop -- the task's S03 operation-boundary snapshot propagates into the thread (contextvars).

WebSocket handler for the slice-group copy button (action=compile_slice_search). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id). TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) so it can do a NESTED Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the ORIGINATING tab without deadlocking the single websocket_handler pump. Reads the live slice-group config from that tab, resolves the requested group_id (or active group), and compiles the Workflowy membership search string via the single Python compiler compile_slice_search_expression (#P -#P--deprecated OR ...). Replies compile_slice_search_result with request_id + expression.

WebSocket handler for the live F8 keypress (action=f8_expansion_plan). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id) carrying the visible DOM subtree. TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab to read the active slice group's prefixes + the live postfix config (one settings reader, no client-side policy). Then runs Phase 0 (validate_subtree_against_cache, fail-closed) and Phase 2 (build_expansion_plan) over the validated visible tree and replies f8_expansion_plan_result (echoing request_id) with {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand, warnings} for the client to execute mechanically. No fallback: on validation failure or no live tab it replies with an error the client surfaces loudly.

Apply-slice Tier-1 handler (action=render_slice_modal): the docked Markdown modal sourced from the CACHE-PROJECTED slice group instead of the live virtualized DOM. Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id); TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_f8_expansion_plan / _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab, which would deadlock the single websocket_handler pump if awaited inline. Resolves the requested slice group (by group_id, else active), then runs the SHARED cache-projection funnel build_stage1_base_tree (Phase 1 build_slice_subtree_from_cache -> Phase 2 build_expansion_plan -> Phase 3 apply_expansion_plan_to_subtree -> Phase 4 prune_collapsed_leaf_zombies) -- the EXACT SAME funnel _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache calls, so the Apply-slice modal and the slice-group GLIMPSE can never diverge on the projection (incl. the Phase-4 render-only zombie prune, the deliberate divergence from the live Workflowy expansion state) -- then _build_markdown_preview_from_tree (the SAME shared composer the live-DOM modal uses) with the _root_in_non_md_file_from_cache seed. Returns ONE Markdown STRING that is complete BY CONSTRUCTION (cache-sourced, not virtualized), so the dock can display it with no scroll/F8/refresh-dance and the client suppresses the scroll-to-bottom warning (cache_sourced=true). Replies render_slice_modal_result echoing request_id so the broker routes it to ONLY the originating tab. | Build the stable STRING key for a tree-view row's (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple, used both to key the Apply-slice SNAPSHOT map server-side and (echoed by the client on a row click) to select the exact occurrence in the SINGLE per-row path. NUL-joined ancestor_path so it cannot collide with a uuid; occurrence suffixed. Deterministic + pure -- the same row produces the same key on the original render and on any re-projection (MATCH = EMIT).

new_result.role: _compose_render_scope(kind, group_id, group_name, root_uuid, sort_by, sort_direction, since, headings_only)
new_result.comment: Build the SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE render_scope echo object for a cache-projected render. This is the ONE object every consumer (client adoptRenderScope -> per-tab render state + ribbon widgets + footer; and the MCP push tool output) treats as the normalized ground truth of what was ACTUALLY rendered, regardless of which SURFACE (ribbon click or MCP glimpse() call) triggered the render. Carries ONLY the normalized structured render-defining fields: scope identity (kind/group_id/group_name/root_uuid) + view params (sort_by/sort_direction/since object-or-null/headings_only). There is no pre-composed display string -- the status footer is the ONE consumer that renders a human string, composing it from THESE fields, so string-composition lives in exactly one place. kind is 'slice' (group at its own root), 'slice_override' (group tags scoped to an override root), 'raw_root' (bare root_uuid raw dump, no group -> the footer labels it 'raw dump of <root8>'), or 'lightning_rod' (a temporary Lightning Rod selection via the `lightning` param, which takes PRECEDENCE). LIGHTNING SELECTION: a lightning render carries ONE opaque `selection` object {mode:'gather'|'render_tags'|'render_search'|'render_symbols', + per-mode fields (tags+postfix_policy | query/query_mode | symbols/root_uuids/favor) + match_scope} that the client round-trips VERBATIM for BEHAVIOR (routing is by selection.mode, never selection_kind). selection_kind ('gather'|'tags'|'search'|'symbols') + workflowy_search_equivalent are DERIVED from selection.mode and are DISPLAY-ONLY (footer/status-bar label). UNMOORED SIGNAL: live_gui_sync_supported is a TOP-LEVEL bool emitted for EVERY kind (+ live_gui_sync_skipped_reason naming why when False) -- False for a raw dump (no membership search), a descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' render (inexpressible as a Workflowy search), a search_too_many_variants refusal, or any lightning selection; the client surfaces the unmoored state on the yellow bar. It is DISPLAY/observability only, never a behavior driver. EVERY kind also carries the explicit CONTENT/TREE CONTRACT fields content_format ('markdown'|'raw_text') + tree_mode ('render_tree'|'root_only') so the client never guesses how to paint the one rendered string or populate the top-half list (only a lightning GATHER is raw_text/root_only today). Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

Phase-E1 SPEC-AWARE BRIDGE to the ONE render_scope composer. Given a RESOLVED RenderProjectionSpec (kind/root/group already canonicalized by the caller's resolution step -- NOT the raw incoming spec), DELEGATE to _compose_render_scope by unpacking exactly the scalar params it already takes (Option A, Dan-decided: delegate, do NOT reimplement from spec.to_render_scope_fields(), so there stays ONE render_scope-assembly implementation and this never becomes a second scope factory / caller-side fabrication site). The is_raw_dump / root_overridden booleans the scalar composer wants are read straight off the spec's kind-derived properties (spec.is_raw_dump / spec.root_overridden), and sort_by is passed via spec.sort_by_internal() (the ONE wire-'none'<->internal-None translation). search_too_many_variants is a POST-RENDER fact (not a spec input field, per invariant 5) so it is threaded as an explicit kwarg here, exactly as the scalar composer already accepts it. This is the E1 seam that lets every downstream server call site (modal handler E3, content-return GLIMPSE paths E4, push frame E5) compose render_scope FROM the same spec it projected from, instead of from a parallel bag of locals -- the two-parallel-assembly-points seam Phase E removes. Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

The ONE inherited slice-group root policy seam shared by MCP/lens renders and every stored-root consumer (APPLY, copy-search, named merge, scoped reprojection, push and group purge). Delegates resolution to resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle with the caller's pinned map; exact UUIDs, clean prefixes including 8 hex, and AP-IDs are adopted with existing archive semantics. Corrective UUID shaves are rejected and only their speculative correction echo is discarded. Transport, scope notes and miss envelopes stay per-origin; explicit input roots keep the standard forgiving boundary.

PURE formatter for the ambiguous/missing error ENVELOPE returned by the cache-projection root_uuid resolution sites (the bare-root RAW-DUMP GLIMPSE, the slice-group override root, the push scope root, and Lightning Rod). Given a resolve_uuid_like_node_handle result that did NOT resolve (candidates present => ambiguous; else => missing), returns the standard {success:False, error, [candidates/matched_prefix_len/truncated], **extra} dict -- so the several sites can't DRIFT on the field set. Deliberately NOT a resolver wrapper: each caller keeps its own resolution and control flow (plain return vs await _reply) and its own error WORDING (via display/label); this only unifies the payload SHAPE. Chain-1 W4 (F5): in the MISSING branch, a refusal-reason operation (a sink, a write, an export, a purge preview) whose root names a visible archived node RAISES ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the exact §5.2/§5.3 text and provenance — before any file/modal/preview work; reads (reason None/flag) and no-context callers keep today's hint-only text. Returns None when the handle actually resolved (caller should not call it then). Pure; no I/O.

ONE handler for every cache-projected docked-modal render + per-row re-render (the 'Apply slice' feature). Resolves the four-cell scope truth table: slice (group_id), slice_override (group_id+root_uuid), raw_root (root_uuid only), lightning_rod (lightning{mode,...}; group-less, Phase-1-only via an injected member_predicate BY DEFAULT -- render_tags + postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) upgrades the cell to the shared build_stage1_base_tree funnel with one nested postfix config read). Lightning modes: gather (short-circuits to the raw-text tag outline), render_tags{tags} (DEFAULT: no config read; 'slice': one nested postfix config read), render_search{query,query_mode} (both scope via one frame root_uuid), and render_symbols{symbols,root_uuids,favor} (the tag-free beacon slice: roots via its own root_uuids -> their LCA, does one nested config read for the global-suppression filter, resolves via the shared _project_render_symbols_from_cache, and appends its unresolved/ambiguous report to the full-document reply), plus render_lens{lens,query?} (the recursive LensSpec cell: one nested config read, the shared immutable Stage-0 snapshot + transport-free _project_render_lens_from_cache, derived-LCA rooting, and explicit empty artifact). All five modes emit one opaque `selection` object into the render_scope. Then runs the shared projection -> prepare_stage2_render_forest -> rows -> snapshot-vs-single machinery and echoes the server-authoritative render_scope.

Bulk F12+4 qualification walk (source-agnostic). The in-set reservation makes prior leaves act as though already on disk so the integer-suffix increment is race-free and deterministic.

Builds the tree (mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; mode='all' -> cache subtree), runs _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves, assigns collision-safe filenames across the whole in-memory set FIRST (single accumulating process, race-free), then for EACH qualifying leaf writes the metadata-stripped note to its .md, sets the node note (Path: header for persist, dummy MD_PATH: block for in-md-file persist, or clears for temp), patches the snapshot, and fires an INDEPENDENT detached F12+1 job per leaf (N status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan).

Browser-initiated UUID Explorer anchor-list convenience endpoint. The ONE module-level coroutine the WS reader loop spawns (via create_isolated_context_task) for the long handlers whose inline failure frame was the generic {action, success:false, node_id, error} shape, instead of awaiting the handler inline: the two F12 refresh actions and (since U4) open_node_in_windsurf / materialize_markdown_file / bulk_materialize_markdown / bulk_generate_markdown. WebSocket handler for the widget's once-a-second CARTO jobs poll (action=carto_list_jobs), spawned by the pump through _carto_list_jobs_poll (single-flight + 0.5 s spacing: the reply is untargeted, so the broker broadcasts it to every tab and a coalesced poll loses nothing). Delegates to the SAME _system_job_cancel_impl the system.job.cancel MCP verb uses; owns its shaped carto_cancel_job_result frames (unchanged wire shape)
Shared FastMCP registration seam for every published tool in both profiles: merge the Claude Code 500000-character result declaration without changing unrelated metadata or execution

Admission footprint derivation for CARTO launches.
