Thin server compatibility wrapper over the dependency-light shared CARTO_REFRESH launch authority; supplies credentials, explicit snapshot freshness, and path/graph footprint resolution while preserving structured governance_cleanup_required launch failures unchanged; S03B Chain-3 (W1): wraps every prepared callback in ONE execution-site cache_operation_boundary (the isolated prepared task's only operation boundary, entered via prepared_runner after obtain_freshness); S04 Remediation Chain 2: the wrapped callback rechecks the shared require_coherence_mutation_admission authority AFTER boundary adoption + freshness, immediately before preparation side effects — refusal persists typed coherence_barrier_active diagnostics, finalizes the exact claim, and never spawns the worker.
Whitens visible-DOM vs cache text for spurious-UPDATE detection in F12 bulk-apply pre-pass; tied to F12+3 timeout investigation

Helper that compares visible Workflowy DOM against /nodes-export cache; deliberately NOT used as bulk-apply pre-filter (see comment in _collect_bulk_visible_apply_groups). Always returned True after refresh and caused F12+2 nothing-happens bug.

new_result.comment: Diagnostic-only residue behind node.edit note search-and-replace. Runs ONLY after exact and 1:1 Unicode-space-fold matching both miss. First probes a space-folded + zero-width-stripped view with an original-index map (never silently mutates through this non-1:1 tier); then a conservative unique visible-token anchor. When a probable region exists, returns the note's ACTUAL substring as suggested_search plus a ready-to-reissue {search,replace} suggested_edit and the first divergent Unicode codepoints. The edit report JSON is ensure_ascii=True, making invisible characters visible/copyable as \\uXXXX. Pure; no I/O.

ONE per-entry note search authority for node.edit single/multi modes. First match by default; replace_all chooses all non-overlapping matches from the pre-entry text without reprocessing replacements. Exact matches anywhere win globally; only an exact miss permits 1:1 Unicode SPACE SEPARATOR folding. Folded matches reuse the original source-context-preserving splicer so unchanged NBSP indentation survives. Returns first index and optional tier/near_miss; replace-all adds a replacement_count. Pure text transformation, no I/O or cache mutation.

THE one note-diff renderer behind every note-edit report (search/replace and whole-note — the public default since [ap:4JSBO5]). Stdlib difflib only; line-oriented. Size-guarded by the ONE shared head+tail clamp (snippet_view.clamp_span_to_head_tail — the same arithmetic the read guard uses) at DEFAULT_NOTE_MAX_LINES: past the threshold the middle is elided behind ONE row naming the omitted diff-line region, the hidden hunk count and the whole-diff totals (+added / -removed); an EMPTY before-note renders the one line 'note was empty; N lines written' instead of a wall of + lines. Pure; no I/O; no second clamp and no second diff renderer exist.

new_result.role: ⚡ edit_node(node_id: str, name, note, note_search, note_replace, note_edits, layout_mode, _completed)
new_result.comment: Public edit surface (legacy workflowy_edit_node + consolidated node.edit). Thin wrapper over _node_edit_core with NO internal channels: every name edit runs the protected-name policy (_compose_protected_name) -- supplied trailing #tags or an added/changed leading [ap:] handle are loud ProtectedNameViolations; existing tags/AP-ID auto-preserve. [ap:4JSBO5]: the whole-note diff default is resolved HERE (return_diff tri-state: omitted + note -> true) so internal narrow channels never build diffs, and the public plain-update ack is converted HERE from the core's redacted WorkFlowyNode into the [ap:PHO4BG] small dict -- node fields minus note/children (and the model_dump mirrors no/ch), plus note_written/note_chars/note_lines when a note was written; never a "note": null.

Shared async core behind workflowy_edit_node / node.edit AND the narrow internal protected-region channels. Every name write is composed from ONE live GET snapshot (memoized _fetch_current_node; note search/replace and opt-in whole-note return_diff reuse the SAME node, so a name+note combo costs one read + one write) via the pure _compose_protected_name policy -- supplied trailing #tags or a new/changed leading [ap:] handle raise ProtectedNameViolation (loud, zero mutation); existing tags/AP-ID auto-preserve, and a rename also preserves the ordinary title's leading emoji run (Z8Q0PF+LITF2F: you need not pass an emoji; a supplied run wins explicitly; _replace_leading_emoji=True hands the run to the supplied title wholesale). Internal callers get exactly ONE narrow channel, never a generic infrastructure bypass: anchor.dock.update passes _tag_transform; anchor.point.assign_id passes _assign_ap_core; anchor.point.remove_id passes _remove_ap_id; the node emoji verbs (update_emoji / prepend_emoji / append_emoji) pass _leading_emoji_mutation; anchor.point.touch passes _touch (a content-preserving modifiedAt advance: echo the live layoutMode with zero text bytes on the wire, or fall back to an identity name recomposition when no echoable layoutMode exists; never composes text itself; returns the UNREDACTED post-write node so the caller can verify preservation); all may inject _current_node to reuse their own live read.

THE ONE substantive implementation behind the three node leading-emoji verbs (update_emoji replace/remove, prepend_emoji before the run, append_emoji after the run). Resolves the node handle, performs one authoritative live read, composes the request through _compose_protected_name's typed narrow LeadingEmojiMutation channel, returns a true zero-write no-op when unchanged (reachable in practice only from update_emoji -- the insert verbs always change the name), and otherwise injects the SAME snapshot into _node_edit_core for one write. Only the leading emoji run of the ordinary name section is affected; AP-ID, legacy decoration before AP, ordinary title, middle/right emojis, trailing tags, and descendants are preserved. The three thin verb delegates below stay beaconless on purpose (curate, don't carpet-bomb) -- they remain Cartographer AST-mapped and symbol-resolvable under this parent.

THE ONE substantive implementation behind the two node note-concat verbs (append_note / prepend_note, [ap:MZOKZ1]): an agent whose note is too big for one tool call writes it in parts -- point.capture the first part, then append/prepend the rest one part per call, no sentinel and no search string. Resolves the mutator handle, performs ONE authoritative live read + wire-to-semantic decode through _read_live_node_note (newline-normalized to pure LF exactly as the note search-and-replace path does), concatenates the non-empty text with the EXPLICIT separator (default '\n'; skipped when the existing note is empty -- there is nothing to separate), and writes once through _node_edit_core(note=..., _current_node=<the same live node>) so the whole verb is one read + one governed write. Byte-exact on the semantic domain; no diff (the point is size); AP-ID, title and trailing tags are untouched (a note-only request composes no name). Empty text is a loud ValueError, never a silent no-op. No mapped-node refusal: parity with node.edit, which refuses none (checked at e5a86ce). The two thin verb delegates below stay one-line re-fronts (curate, don't carpet-bomb).

Thin re-front for node.prepend_note over the ONE _node_note_concat_impl (position='prepend'): the text lands BEFORE the existing note, joined by the explicit separator (default newline).

system.archives.mount (§U3.2 D5, §5.11): set or clear ONE archive's mount_parent_id — the parent its root is planted under when the parent it was exported from is gone. new_result.comment: GLIMPSE `since` Form-A window PARSER. Parses a time-window token into a duration in SECONDS (timestamps are epoch-seconds). Accepts a unit-suffixed integer/float -- s(econds) m(inutes) h(ours) d(ays) w(eeks) -- e.g. '3d','1w','12h','90m','45s'; a BARE number is interpreted as DAYS ('7' == '7d'), the common case. Whitespace-tolerant, case-insensitive. Returns None for a blank/None/garbage/non-positive token so the caller can raise an actionable error. Pure. | GLIMPSE `since` PRUNE -- the shared leaf-branch filter run LAST (after Phase1/2/3 AND after the timestamp reorder), on the already-final sorted forest. Decomposes the forest into root->leaf branches (same DFS the sort uses), keeps a branch iff its branch-date (via the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static -- created=leaf createdAt, modified=branch-max modifiedAt, IDENTICAL to the sort) is beyond the pivot: ascending -> STRICTLY GREATER than pivot (most-recent tail; the pivot node itself excluded, everything newer kept); descending -> STRICTLY LESS than pivot (the commensurate 'oldest tail', a don't-care corner but done right). A branch with no resolvable date is DROPPED (can't prove it's in the window). Then trie-merges the surviving branches back into a tree via the SAME _reorder pass with sort_by carried through, so straddled ancestors re-emit exactly as in the unfiltered render. Returns a NEW forest (inputs untouched); empty list when nothing survives.

GLIMPSE `since` Form-A (time-window) PIVOT. Data-relative leading edge (Dan): the pivot is the branch-date of the MOST RECENT leaf branch in the ALREADY-FINAL forest (ascending) minus the window -- so 'last 1 week' on data whose newest branch is 2 years old means the week ENDING at that 2-year-old edge, NOT wall-clock now. Descending flips to the OLDEST edge plus the window (the don't-care commensurate corner). Uses the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static for every branch date so it matches the sort. Returns the pivot epoch-seconds, or None if no branch has a resolvable date (caller then returns the tree unfiltered rather than erroring on empty data).

GLIMPSE `since="curated"` FORM-B PIVOT (the self-maintaining curation cursor). Walks the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, finds every node that has been CURATED = carries any tag matching an active slice prefix INCLUDING --deprecated variants but EXCLUDING the --suppress/--expand PRESENTATION variants (via node_is_curated_for_prefixes, threaded with the render caller's resolved match_scope -- the SAME SELECTION-stage scope knob Stage-1 membership uses, 'name' = title only so a note-body family tag never moves the cursor, 'name_and_note' = default NAME+NOTE -- deliberately looser than slice MEMBERSHIP on the triage axis, because deprecating a tag is itself a curation act the user must not re-encounter; suppressing/expanding one is a lens carve-out, NOT triage, and must not move the cursor -- Session-019 curated-cursor fix + match_scope plumbing). For each curated node it computes that node's branch-date using the SAME rule the sort uses (_branch_timestamp_key_static over the node's root->leaf cache path: created=the curated node's own createdAt; modified=branch-max modifiedAt down to it), and returns the MAX (ascending; MIN for descending) = the high-water mark. Everything strictly newer than this in the shared-tail prune is the UNCURATED tail. Returns None when NOTHING under root is curated yet (no group tag anywhere) so the tail shows the whole subtree (all of it is 'new since last curated'). Cache-only; pure aside from the cache read.
Count every node in a nested {children:[...]} subtree, inclusive of the root.
Maximum depth of a nested {children:[...]} subtree (a childless root is depth 1).

new_result.role: prepare_stage2_render_forest(final_subtree, cache_by_id, sort_by, sort_direction, since_spec, curated_pivot_ts, recent_by)
new_result.comment: The shared STAGE-2 final-forest preparation: timestamp sort -> since prune -> empty-window detection -> node_count/depth, over a STAGE-1 base tree. Three render sites call it -- render_stage2_filter_sort (the GLIMPSE tail), _handle_render_slice_modal (the Apply-slice modal), and _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture (the frozen-DOM render_spec=modal sibling) -- so all three produce an identical final forest. Returns the final forest as a tree OBJECT (not just a rendered string) because the modal walks it to build its rows / per-row views / last-N label. PURE: no WebSocket, no config read. It does NOT compute the curated pivot -- the caller passes curated_pivot_ts in, because that pivot needs the slice's active_prefixes. recent_by ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a)) is the recency basis of a 'newest' item_count selection, threaded verbatim into apply_since_to_forest (None = resolve at apply: the sort axis when it is a timestamp, else modified -- the ONE resolve_item_count_basis rule). Returns (forest, since_applied, empty_window, node_count, depth, since_err); since_err is surfaced (never swallowed) so each caller shapes its own error reply.

new_result.role: render_stage2_filter_sort(spec, final_subtree, cache_by_id, output_file, source_meta, since_pivot_ts, since_form, body_suppressed_ids, max_nodes, member_predicate)
new_result.comment: STAGE 2 (filter+sort+render): the shared render/sort/write tail for every cache-sourced GLIMPSE (slice-group, bare root_uuid, and Lightning Rod). Runs OVER an already-built STAGE-1 base tree and does PRESENTATION only -- it never re-decides membership. Delegates the sort/since/empty-window/count prep to prepare_stage2_render_forest, then renders through the same composer the live-DOM GLIMPSE uses (_build_markdown_preview_from_tree in markdown mode, _annotate_preview_ids_and_build_tree in full/UUID mode), optionally resolving a row focus to render one node's option-Y view. headings_only renders also carry dock.peek's four-field end-of-line vocabulary ([ap:UH0UOU]): the source_metrics index is built once here (build_render_source_metrics over this render's top-level root) and rides the policy; managed source lines (Cartographer/beacon markers) stay bare. Optionally writes a single compact .md (full-mode disk export is caller-guarded, not here). Merges the caller's source_meta into the payload. NODE LIMIT ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2): the optional max_nodes/member_predicate pair -- passed ONLY by the search surfaces (slice_group.sift / lightning_rod.render_search headings tiers) -- caps the final forest to the first N MATCHING nodes AFTER the sort and the since prune via cap_forest_to_first_node_count, recomputes node_count/depth over what actually renders, and echoes node_limit_applied (the shaper's node-limit line composes from it); every other caller passes neither and stays byte-identical. LENS SCAFFOLD ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g): the optional lens_scaffold_ids set -- passed ONLY by the lens render tails (the caller folds the ancestor_notes opt-out) -- forwards the lens's connective scaffolding above the input roots to BOTH materialize calls' lens-scaffold-ancestor cause, so that ancestor path renders headings-only in Markdown AND full/UUID mode, document order included; every other caller passes nothing and stays byte-identical. Knows NOTHING about slice-group or root_uuid resolution. REPOSITORY VIEW (U1): with spec.repository_view the projection (_repository_view_forest) runs after the prepare/cap steps (a multi-root render refuses), the projected forest materializes with document order / no focus / no chronological suppression, D = composed + one final newline, the payload and the output_file ack carry the repository_view counts (+ document on the in-memory payload), and the file write delivers D exactly -- never the coherence advisory (§6.3).

RAW-DUMP server-side GLIMPSE by BARE root_uuid: the content-return originator of a raw-dump render. NO WebSocket at all (not even the tab-agnostic slice-group config read) -- it needs only the /nodes-export cache. Resolves root_uuid prefix-tolerantly via the SHARED resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle (UUID exact -> unique prefix -> [ap:CORE] AP-ID; multi -> did-you-mean; none -> cache-miss error), builds ONE RenderProjectionSpec (kind raw_root) so STAGE-1 admission (exclude_completed) is read off the spec, projects the COMPLETE subtree via build_slice_subtree_from_cache(..., member_all=True) (every descendant is a member; no slice filtering; NO Phase 2/3/4), then hands the base tree + the SAME spec to the shared STAGE-2 tail render_stage2_filter_sort. An optional boundary_predicate applies the descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' traversal. recursive ([ap:EPR86W] part a) is the depth leg: False walks the root + its DIRECT children only (max_depth=1 through the ONE shared walker; the boundary is moot under the cap, as on dock.peek). This is the pure SCRY-as-Markdown capability: GLIMPSE everything under any UUID server-side, no live Workflowy expansion state required. _source=cache_root_uuid.

new_result.role: async _resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache(cache_by_id, symbols, resolved_roots, suppress_tags, favor, allow_anchor_points)
new_result.comment: Shared per-input symbol resolution core for Lightning Rod. Resolves every requested UUID/symbol exactly once, preserves the original input item beside its resolved UUID, applies root scoping and optional suppression filtering, and returns ordered per-item records plus the classic render_symbols buckets. AP-ID ITEMS (ap:APSYMB): an '[ap:CORE]' / 'ap:CORE' item (any case; a BARE core is NOT accepted -- grammar guard _RENDER_SYMBOLS_AP_ID_ITEM_RE) resolves via the shared resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle BEFORE the UUID-shaped / symbol classification -- but ONLY when allow_anchor_points=True, which is passed ONLY by the render wrapper (_project_render_symbols_from_cache); the beacon-mutation modes call with the default False and are categorically unaffected (anchor points are ephemeral-read-only). Used by render_symbols and the beacon-mutation modes so mutation never re-resolves UUIDs or guesses which operation belongs to which resolved node. BRACKETED-UUID ITEMS (Dan, 2026): an item whose AP-ID-style brackets wrap a pure-hex >=8-char body ('[a2e552e3]' / '[full-uuid]') is unwrapped via the SAME pure normalizer the Layer-1 primitive consumes (unwrap_bracketed_uuid_handle) BEFORE the _uuid_shaped routing classification, so it ROUTES to the UUID leg instead of falling to the symbol leg; '[ap:CORE]' items (colon => non-hex) and bracketed non-hex cores ('[K7M2QF]') are never unwrapped and route exactly as before.

render_symbols PER-ITEM OBJECT ELEMENTS (ap:EXPSWP; D2 input shape Option B; D3 unwrap-only in v1): the ONE shared item normalizer for the render_symbols `symbols` list. An element is either a plain string handle (today's behavior, stripped) or a small object {'uuid': HANDLE | 'symbol': NAME, 'expand'?: bool} -- exactly one of uuid/symbol, non-empty string handle, expand bool if present (absent/false = plain member). Returns {ok, handles (resolution input, strings only), expand_handles (flagged handles, expand-wins on a plain+flagged duplicate per the locked semantics contract), raw (the canonical VERBATIM echo list: stripped strings + shallow-copied objects -- what the spec / wire blob / render_scope selection carries so every re-projection re-runs normalize->resolve->sweep deterministically, D5)}. LOUD structured rejection (success:False-shaped): both keys, neither key, empty/non-string handle, non-bool expand, unrecognized keys, or any element that is neither string nor dict. The uuid/symbol KEY is NOT honored as an explicit-kind resolution hint in v1 (unwrap-only; the handle flows through the existing favor classification) -- a v1.1 nicety. Used by ALL THREE entry surfaces (_lightning_rod_render_symbols, the _handle_render_slice_modal render_symbols branch, and the _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal render_symbols branch), replacing the three hand-rolled [str(s).strip() ...] coercions (a net de-duplication).

DYNAMIC TAG-FREE BEACON SLICE (Lightning Rod mode='render_symbols'). Resolves a mixed list of UUIDs and/or symbols (function/class/beacon names) per-item, UUID-first then symbol-fallback (favor flag), scopes to REQUIRED root_uuids (single or list), applies ABSOLUTE global-suppression filtering (option B) then buckets survivors resolved(1)/ambiguous(N)/unresolved(0)/out-of-scope. PER-ITEM EXPAND (ap:EXPSWP): a `symbols` element may be an object {uuid|symbol, expand:true} -- unwrapped/validated by the ONE shared _normalize_render_symbols_items on ALL THREE entry surfaces (MCP return / docked modal / push). A cleanly-resolved flagged item's whole cache subtree is swept into the Stage-1 member set (member_ids ⊇ resolved_ids) via collect_subtree_ids -- suppression-guarded at sweep time, completed-pruned by Phase 1 at admit time, boundary-free; a flagged-but-not-cleanly-resolved item is INERT (no partial expansion). Still NO Phase 2/3/4 machinery. Builds the render from the member set (resolved ∪ swept) + LCA connective root via build_selected_subtree_from_cache and the SHARED render_stage2_filter_sort tail (Phase-1 SELECTION only; no Phase 2/3/4). Markdown-only (no bracketed mode). Non-fatal: problem items are reported BOTH in-band (appended '## WARNING Unresolved/ambiguous symbols' section) AND out-of-band (resolution_report + warning). ONE WebSocket touch (unlike other Lightning Rod modes): the tab-agnostic get_slice_group_config read to obtain f8_global_never_expand_tags (the wfy-suppress list). Resolution uses ONLY the shared resolvers (resolve_uuid_like_node_handle + client.read_uuid_from_symbol + resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle for GATED [ap:CORE] anchor-point items, ap:APSYMB) -- no bespoke resolution logic. Where the symbol list comes from: a phase-1 architect agent that read a larger slice and passes forward exactly the symbols/UUIDs the phase-2 session should see. | SHARED render-symbols projection core (the anti-seam extraction). The SINGLE resolve->scope->suppress->bucket->LCA implementation, called by BOTH the MCP-return path (_lightning_rod_render_symbols) AND the docked-modal push cell (_handle_render_slice_modal's render_symbols branch), so the two can NEVER drift on resolution semantics. PURE of transport: it takes an already-loaded cache_by_id + an already-resolved suppress_tags list (each caller reads those in its own way -- the MCP path via _resolve_slice_group_config(None), the modal path via its own nested get_slice_group_config read) and returns {ok, error?, lca_root, resolved_ids (explicit-only; NEVER polluted by the sweep), member_ids (resolved ∪ swept -- the Stage-1 member set the callers' predicate tests), expand_ids, resolution_report (+ expand_ids/swept_count), report_markdown, warning}. Uses ONLY the shared resolvers (resolve_uuid_like_node_handle + client.read_uuid_from_symbol + resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle for GATED [ap:CORE] anchor-point items, ap:APSYMB) -- no bespoke resolution logic -- and the shared _symbol_report_row for rich ambiguity rows. No render, no WebSocket, no disk here; the callers own the render tail + reporting placement. NBBW follow-up: the per-item resolution runs in a worker thread on a private loop (cache-only; the pinned snapshot rides the copied context), so a large render never blocks the daemon.

The MCP-return render_symbols cell over the SHARED _project_render_symbols_from_cache resolve->scope->suppress->bucket->LCA core and the ONE render tail. tier (54e8356f(ii), MCP-return ONLY) swaps each rendered member's note for a fenced body via _apply_render_symbols_tier + snippet_view.render_symbol_tier_note: 'slice' (default) unchanged; 'metadata' exactly the snippet size header (the ONE format_snippet_header format); 'context' comment + def + first context_lines lines + a trailer pointing at the rest. The parameter never enters the lightning selection / spec blob, so the docked-modal and push paths cannot see it; headings_only/output_file are refused with a non-slice tier, and a failed disk read keeps the member's original note plus a WARNING section.

render-symbols ambiguity/unresolved REPORT ROW builder -- the anti-seam. It REUSES the rich descriptor the ONE symbol resolver already produced (uuid/name/file_path/ast_qualname/line/via via read_uuid_from_symbol -> _build_candidate_descriptor), looked up from descriptors_by_uuid, rather than rebuilding a poorer row (which was the 5th ambiguity dialect). For a UUID-path candidate (whose descriptor carries no path), it BEST-EFFORT enriches file_path via the EXISTING resolve_cartographer_path_from_node ancestor walk (the same Root:/Path: header logic used everywhere), and fills name from the cache -- tolerating the documented 'no resolvable path' case (a candidate under an unmapped region, or a multi-root call where a given candidate's chain has no Root:/Path: header) by leaving file_path None. Name is DOM-markup-stripped for readability. This is the closest we get to ONE ambiguity descriptor without a broader refactor of the four existing reporters (out of scope now).

render-symbols IN-BAND report: compose the '## WARNING Unresolved / ambiguous symbols' Markdown section appended to the bottom of the render. Lists each problem item (ambiguous / unresolved / out-of-scope / all-suppressed) with its candidate rows. Candidate uuids print SHORT ([ap:0M6VP8]: the paste-backable short form via unique_short_uuid_prefix over uuid_prefix_collisions, lengthened just enough to be unique; the structured resolution_report keeps the full UUIDs). Returns '' when there are no problem items (nothing appended). Deliberately plain Markdown so it renders cleanly in the same pseudo-document.

Phase-C DISK-TARGET UNIQUENESS check (SPEC v5 §5 step 11): no two preflighted items with a RESOLVED TARGET KEY -- actionable OR noop -- may claim the same disk target key. A noop row still asserts an intended end-state for its target; letting it collide with another row's mutation would make its ledger row dishonest. Returns a collisions list (batch preflight failure) or None.

Shared Q3 beacon batch orchestrator for ensure/remove. Ordinary per-item resolution and returned preflight failures are ledger rows, not batch vetoes; valid items continue through the existing JIT/CAS writer. Scope/cache/infrastructure failures and duplicate/disk-target collisions still abort. The ONE all-target lease acquisition, ownership, cancellation, and cleanup paths are unchanged; any lease refusal still blocks all eligible writes. Disk-only with complete partial-success ledger. Policy addendum: docs/BEACON-BATCH-PARTIAL-SUCCESS.md. NON-BLOCKING (NBBW): Phase B resolution runs in a worker thread (private loop, cache-only) and the client preflight/plan/commit bodies run in worker threads -- the commit thread is never abandoned on cancellation, so the lease release in finally still follows the last disk write. GLOBAL SUPPRESSION: symbol resolution honours #wfy-suppress via _beacon_symbol_suppress_tags (fail-loud read); a suppressed-only item is an item-local all_suppressed row, never written. COMMENT CONFLICTS (2R4E1P): a fill-mode conflict is KEPT, never an error -- the labels are still ensured, comment_outcome='kept_existing_conflict' rides every row status (committed/noop alike) with a warning carrying BOTH texts; the batch result gains a top-level warnings list and a summary.comment_conflicts_kept count, which make_mutation_ack lifts to the ack's warnings. ATOMIC OPT-IN ([ap:LPC157] residue): spec.atomic=true (default false) restores the strict preflight veto AFTER Phase C and BEFORE lease acquisition -- any item failure leaves every other row not_run with zero writes and no lease (the failing item keeps its error row); a mid-batch commit failure is still per item (writes are individually CAS-atomic, no rollback exists). ONE-LINE SUMMARY: the result carries a top-level summary_line ('N committed · M noop · K failed (...)' -- the single failure's symbol/kind/reason, else the distinct failure kinds) so an agent can act without reading the ledger.

Q4 Lightning Rod: batch Workflowy #tag mutation (add/remove/rename) on NODES by UUID/[ap:CORE] handle -- the Workflowy-nodes mutation cell of the 2x2 (Q3 = disk beacons). THIN LEDGER WRAPPER over the three client tag primitives (workflowy_add_tag/remove_tag/rename_tag) -- ZERO tag-region surgery of its own (the no-cracks core). Preflight-all-then-commit, mirroring _lightning_rod_mutate_beacons: resolve EVERY handle ONCE via the Layer-3 universal resolver (client.resolve_node_handle; allow_uuid + allow_anchor_point, NO symbols -- symbols are Q3's quadrant) -> ANY unresolved/ambiguous handle ABORTS the batch (complete ledger, zero mutations) -> duplicate-resolved-UUID preflight (batch abort, Q3 parity -- also makes intra-batch substrate drift impossible: each node is read-modify-written exactly once) -> sequential commit in input order delegating to the primitives (per-item failure recorded, batch CONTINUES). Complete ledger: exactly one row per normalized operation, in input order, under EVERY outcome, carrying the primitives' per-op detail (tags_added/tags_already_present, tags_removed/tags_not_present, renamed/old_occurrences_removed/new_tag_already_present, old_name/new_name). CACHE COHERENCE: update_node eagerly patches the /nodes-export cache for THIS server instance (best-effort; other processes refresh separately) -- NO files_changed (no disk touched); disk sync (F12+2) stays the user's standing orthogonal responsibility, same contract as the per-node tag tools. Render knobs (exclude_completed et al.) do NOT apply: mutation may reach suppressed/completed nodes -- Q4 targets NODES by handle (UUID/AP-ID), never by symbol, so global #wfy-suppress (which filters SYMBOL resolution, incl. Q3) does not apply here.

Q4 batch Workflowy tag mutation over the section-9 client wire (action=mutate_node_tags). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id). Deserializes the versioned wire frame {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, operations:[...]} via WorkflowyTagMutationSpec.from_wire -- the SAME _normalize_operations core the MCP tool boundary uses, so the two transports can never drift (STAGE-0 DOCTRINE) -- then runs the SAME _lightning_rod_mutate_tags orchestrator and replies mutate_node_tags_result (echoing request_id) with the full ledger. TASK-DISPATCHED (see websocket_handler) NOT for nested-read deadlock (there are NO nested Direction-A reads -- tag mutation needs NO postfix/config reads; a rename to add --expand is just text) but because a batch runs tens of seconds (~1 op/sec of get_node+update_node API work) and must not block the single websocket_handler pump.

MergeSliceGroups ORCHESTRATOR (Phases A-G of the goal spec + the MRGAMD amendment layer). Mirrors _lightning_rod_mutate_tags in shape (phases, structured returns, complete reporting). Steps: (0) resolve config (postfix words + global-never + groups list) + cache; (1) resolve each group ref to (root_uuid, active_prefixes) -- named via _resolve_slice_group_handle, dynamic via resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle + normalize_slice_group_tags; (2) PHASE A per-group leaf sets via build_stage1_base_tree + collect_effective_slice_leaf_ids; (3) PHASE B combine (union/intersection; empty -> loud error, Ruling 1); (4) PHASE C LCA via compute_lca_from_cache (None -> vault root, Ruling 2); (5) A4 bidirectional safety checks (reverse-prefix against existing prefixes + global-never stem collision); (6) PHASES D+E tag plan via compute_merge_tag_plan; (7) A3.2 congruent-residue pre-mutation check via find_tag_family_collisions against the planned node set; (8) A7 pre-mutation DRY-RUN via build_merge_overlay_cache + simulate_merge_projection (spine reproducibility refusal A6); (9) PHASE F apply via Q4 _lightning_rod_mutate_tags (the SAME asynchronous retry pipeline -- no new transport); (10) A3.4 post-mutation verification via verify_merge_projection; (11) PHASE G persist via create_slice_group (gated on exact completion + verification; idempotent A3.5; non-fatal Ruling 5). target_tab is an ORCHESTRATOR arg (transport routing), NOT a spec field (A10).

MCP tool: merge two or more slice groups into ONE new slice lens via tags applied to Workflowy nodes. Inputs: groups (2+ named or dynamic refs), mode (union|intersection), tag (one base tag). Normalizes via MergeSliceGroupsSpec.normalize_from_tool_args (the ONE MCP-ingress core), then runs the _merge_slice_groups orchestrator. Returns the full report (root, tag counts, Q4 mutation ledger, verification block, persistence record).

MergeSliceGroups over the section-9 client wire (action=merge_slice_groups). Browser-initiated correlated request. Deserializes the versioned wire frame via MergeSliceGroupsSpec.from_wire (the SAME _normalize_group_refs core as the MCP boundary -- the two transports cannot drift, STAGE-0 DOCTRINE), injects config via _read_slice_group_config_nested (browser-initiated nested read, CFGOP1), runs the SAME _merge_slice_groups orchestrator, persists server-side via create_slice_group (A9: the wire handler persists via the SAME server-side path as the MCP origin -- no client-side fire-and-forget), and replies merge_slice_groups_result echoing request_id. TASK-DISPATCHED (see websocket_handler) because a merge runs tens of seconds of ~1 op/sec mutations and must not block the pump.

The FIRST semantic concern on the section-9 client->server mutation channel (action=anchor_dock_update). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id) from the Anchors modal's per-row star toggle. Deserializes the versioned wire frame via AnchorDockUpdateSpec.from_wire (TRANSPORT SHELL ONLY -- K3: it validates object/fields/version/JSON types and "at least one attribute present", and never re-implements the impl's families/attribute semantics) and routes to the ONE canonical seam _anchor_dock_update_impl (K1: target_tab=str(endpoint_id) so the impl's nested Direction-A config read targets the asking tab), whose _attribute_transform -> _node_edit_core(_tag_transform=...) -> _compose_protected_name owns every semantic decision. Replies anchor_dock_update_result echoing request_id with the impl result. The client sends INTENT ONLY (dock_handle + favorite/local + optional families) and composes NO tag. TASK-DISPATCHED (see websocket_handler) because _anchor_dock_update_impl -> _resolve_note_session_config issues a nested Direction-A get_extension_settings read, so an inline await could deadlock the single websocket pump (the _handle_list_anchors_for_widget precedent). Domain errors (ProtectedNameViolation / _AnchorOperationError) reply STRUCTURED with error_code + extra (K2) so the client can render the family chooser from extra.families_present.

LIGHTNING ROD postfix_policy (ap:IMPPTX) -- the ONE shared boundary validator/normalizer for the opt-in postfix-policy knob on Lightning render requests. Returns (normalized, error): 'none' (default -- the original Phase-1-only family/search match, NO expand/suppress/deprecated operations) or 'slice' (render_tags ONLY: the full Stage-1 four-phase funnel via build_stage1_base_tree, with the requested tags as active_prefixes and the live postfix words + real f8_global_never_expand_tags from config). LOUD errors: an unrecognized value, or 'slice' requested for any mode other than render_tags (gather produces a tag set, render_search has no tag-family expansion operand, render_symbols has its own absolute-suppression + per-item expand semantics ap:EXPSWP). Used by EVERY ingress surface -- the lightning_rod tool boundary, _lightning_rod_from_cache, the _handle_render_slice_modal lightning cell, the push cell (_glimpse_push_slice_to_modal), and the Scoped frozen-DOM handler (which then additionally rejects 'slice' itself) -- so the five surfaces can never drift on the contract. Pure; no I/O.

new_result.role: async _lightning_rod_from_cache(mode, root_uuid, tags, query, query_mode, tag_match, postfix_policy, as_markdown, output_file, sort_by, sort_direction, headings_only, since, match_scope)
new_result.comment: LIGHTNING ROD internal orchestrator -- the temporary/in-memory counterpart to _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache, but PURELY cache-only BY DEFAULT (NO WebSocket, NO slice-group config, NO Phase 2/3/4; render_tags postfix_policy='slice' is the ONE exception: ap:IMPPTX routes it through the FULL Stage-1 funnel build_stage1_base_tree with one _resolve_slice_group_config(None) read for the live postfix words + the real f8_global_never_expand_tags list, surfacing Phase-2 warnings / pruned-zombie count / body_suppressed_ids exactly like the persisted slice path). Resolves root_uuid prefix-tolerantly via the shared Layer-1 primitive resolve_uuid_like_node_handle, loads the /nodes-export cache, and dispatches on mode: 'gather' -> gather_tags_in_subtree (returns the sorted tag list; NO render); 'render_tags' -> build_tag_predicate (Option B prefix-family, NO postfix/deprecation semantics BY DEFAULT) -> build_selected_subtree_from_cache -> shared render tail; 'render_search' -> build_search_predicate (shlex 'smart' | 'regex') -> build_selected_subtree_from_cache -> shared render tail. match_scope (SELECTION-stage scope knob: 'name' = title only | 'name_and_note' = default title+body) is validated loudly at this boundary then threaded into ALL THREE modes' harvest/predicate (gather_tags_in_subtree / build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) and echoed in render_scope.lightning.match_scope. This is the THIRD cell of the Stage-1 SELECTION truth table (slice=is_slice_member, raw-dump=lambda True, lightning-rod=custom predicate), running Phase-1-only and skipping presentation policy BY DEFAULT. since='curated' is rejected here (no slice tag set defines 'curated'); live-GUI-sync is never supported. The traversal pair rides the shared selection fragment ([ap:EPR86W] 4b): descend_policy builds the anchor-boundary predicate for all three render modes, and recursive=False is refused LOUDLY here -- a Lightning Rod selection is defined by its predicate over the whole scope, so a depth cap would silently change membership (render_symbols and the mutation modes dispatch above and never carry the flag). Reuses render_stage2_filter_sort verbatim, so Lightning Rod output is structurally identical to every other cache-sourced GLIMPSE.

new_result.role: async _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache(slice_group, as_markdown, output_file, sort_by, sort_direction, target_tab)
new_result.comment: Cache-only GLIMPSE path for a slice group (no DOM/extract_dom): the content-return originator of a slice render. Reads the live slice-group config (tab-agnostic get_slice_group_config -- the ONLY WS touch, for OPTIONS not DOM), resolves the requested slice_group id-OR-name via the SHARED _resolve_slice_group_handle (exact id -> unique 'grp-' prefix -> case-insensitive name fallback -- the SAME resolver the push path uses, so the two can't drift), derives its root_uuid + active prefixes + effective sort, optionally resolves a root_uuid_override (the slice_override scope) or a stop-at-child-anchors boundary predicate, and builds ONE RenderProjectionSpec BEFORE projecting so STAGE-1 admission (exclude_completed/match_scope) is read off the spec. Runs STAGE 1 via the shared funnel build_stage1_base_tree (Phase 1 membership -> Phase 2 plan -> Phase 3 collapse/expand -> Phase 4 zombie prune), computes the curated pivot when since='curated', then hands the base tree + the SAME spec to the shared STAGE-2 tail render_stage2_filter_sort. active_prefixes / postfix words / global_never / cache_by_id are live-config OPERANDS, deliberately NOT spec fields. Output is structurally identical to a live-DOM GLIMPSE of the same expanded slice, so a session can be initialized with no human at the Workflowy GUI. Chain-1 r2 (F5): a sink aimed at a stored root that names a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal before any render/file work. Chain-2 r1 (F1): with NO override, the EFFECTIVE STORED root itself resolves through the SAME shared composite resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle the override root gets (live legs first, then the archive legs — the fallback gate and record_archive_served ride inside it), so an exported-and-deleted stored root is served by the automatic fallback re-run (banner + provenance via the finalizer) and an include-mode run records the archive answer; a live stored root resolves to itself unchanged, and an unknown one stays unresolved for the Stage-1 absent-root branch (today's error, sink refusal intact). Chain-2 r2 (R1): a SHAVED corrective match of the stored root is REJECTED, never adopted — the stored identity and the pre-r1 miss policy are preserved (uuid_resolution_was_shave classifies the outcome; the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded; the raw root falls to the absent-root branch) — while an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2) and keeps the archive repair. No second resolver and no per-carrier banner copy: the lens group atom's inherited root shares this exact seam via lens_engine._resolve_root.

PUSH-TO-MODAL path for glimpse(push_to_modal=True): instead of RETURNING the rendered content to the agent, it COMMANDS the target Workflowy tab to render the requested SERVER-SIDE SCOPE into its docked Markdown modal -- the server-push twin of a human clicking APPLY. Chain-1 W4 (F5): the funnel's resolve-HERE-before-the-round-trip doctrine now covers the render_lens cell's atom roots too -- a root naming a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal (the docked modal never serves archives), so a push can never ack success and then fail tab-side. Chain-1 r2 (R2-W2): the resolve-HERE doctrine now covers every indirect selection as well -- a render_lens GROUP atom pre-flights its group's STORED root (an explicit root_handle override is the target and wins; a bare group atom rides the stored default, so a recursive merged lens cannot hide an archived effective root), the render_symbols cell resolves its roots and runs its items through the SHARED _resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache router (live legs first; an archived root or item refuses before any command; items still ride verbatim per D5), and the direct slice-group cell resolves the chosen group's STORED root when no override root is present. Handles the full (slice_group, root_uuid) truth table: slice_group only (resolve id-or-name -> canonical group_id via the SHARED Layer-1 _resolve_slice_group_handle -- the SAME id/prefix/case-insensitive-name resolver _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache uses), root_uuid only (resolve prefix-tolerantly via the SHARED resolve_uuid_like_node_handle -> a RAW-DUMP push, the zero-token 'show me this anchor' command), or BOTH (slice lens scoped to an override root). All resolution happens HERE (before the round-trip) so a bad group name / missing UUID fails loudly early. Sends a Direction-A 'apply_slice_in_dock' frame carrying whichever of {group_id, root_uuid} are present + the AGENT-SUPPLIED sort/since as an EXPLICIT override (never the tab's global dock sort) via the generic _ws_request_response rail; returns the tab's ack. The tab-side dispatch invokes the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock (same fn the APPLY button uses), so the dock render + (for a slice) live-GUI-sync watcher are identical to a manual Apply; a raw-dump push installs NO watcher (no search/plan). The caller (glimpse) guards a bare live-DOM push (neither scope) as the only error.

UUID-hallucination HARDENING for a render_spec-driven GLIMPSE (the render_spec="modal"/blob path). Given a deserialized RenderProjectionSpec + the /nodes-export cache map, canonicalize EVERY UUID the spec carries -- root_uuid, focus.uuid, and EVERY focus.ancestor_path entry -- through the SHARED prefix-tolerant Layer-1 resolver resolve_uuid_like_node_handle (the exact machine SCRY / anchor / snippet callers use). Grace runs BEFORE the exact (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) focus match downstream, so it only CANONICALIZES a possibly-drifted string to its cache UUID; it NEVER loosens the occurrence-exact match itself (a canonicalized triple still resolves to exactly one occurrence via _resolve_focus_index_path). On the render_spec="modal" path the UUIDs are already server-canonical (near-no-op belt-and-suspenders); on the pasted-blob fallback path this is the real net against an agent-drifted UUID in the chain. A UUID that stays unresolved (no exact hit, no unique prefix) or is ambiguous is LEFT AS-IS (best-effort): a bad focus already fails safe to the whole document downstream, and a bad root_uuid surfaces its own cache-miss error in the dispatch that follows. Returns a NEW spec via with_overrides; the input spec (frozen) is never mutated. Pure; no I/O beyond reading the passed cache map.

Dispatch a resolved RenderProjectionSpec to the right cache-render helper by spec.kind -- the shared tail for BOTH render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (the "modal" WS query and the pasted-blob fallback). It routes the (slice|slice_override) cells to _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache (passing spec.group_id as slice_group, the resolved root as root_uuid_override for slice_override, and spec.focus) and the raw_root cell to _glimpse_root_uuid_from_cache (passing spec.root_uuid + spec.focus). The lightning_rod cell (ap:GLMPMODAL) re-projects the FOURTH scope by reading spec.lightning['mode'] and calling the SAME projector a fresh lightning_rod() call uses (_lightning_rod_from_cache for gather/render_tags/render_search; _lightning_rod_render_symbols for render_symbols): the opaque lightning selection is passed through verbatim, so no new render path is introduced. Each mode keeps its own constraints (render_symbols Markdown-only + roots via its own selection.root_uuids; gather raw-text/root_only; since='curated' rejected inside the projector). FOCUS on a lightning modal read is now SUPPORTED for the node-tree modes (render_tags/render_search/render_symbols): spec.focus is threaded into the projector and resolved occurrence-exactly by the shared render_stage2_filter_sort focus authority -- the ONLY residual rejection is gather+focus (a gather is a tag outline with one synthetic root row, so a real row focus is a category error). Every view knob (as_markdown / sort / since / headings_only / match_scope / descend_policy) is read off the spec, so the render is byte-identical to the equivalent explicit-arg GLIMPSE -- the whole point of routing through the ONE spec object. descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' is honored for the raw_root cell by building the anchor-boundary predicate here (the one config-read WS touch), exactly as the explicit-arg root_uuid path does.

The AGENT-OVERRIDE seam for the render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (render_spec="modal" AND the pasted-blob fallback). Given the RESOLVED, tab-sourced (or pasted) RenderProjectionSpec and the agent's TRI-STATE view overrides (as_markdown / headings_only / sort_by / sort_direction / since; None = inherit what the modal is showing, a value = explicit override), it (1) merges the non-None overrides onto the spec via the SINGLE normalized mutator spec.with_view_overrides (which re-runs the ONE normalizer and preserves the resolved kind via kind_hint -- NOT raw with_overrides), then (2) runs the LOUD combination guards ONCE on the FINAL merged spec, where spec.focus and spec.kind are known. The two guards (Dan-decided): (A) a sort override (sort_by/sort_direction supplied) is REJECTED when spec.focus is present -- sorting a single focused option-Y row is ill-defined; the user re-roots the modal at that subtree instead; (B) a since override is REJECTED when spec.focus is present (a tail/window over the whole underlying scope intersected with a focused row is meaningless). Beyond focus, the standard since preconditions are enforced by reading the FINAL SinceSpec object fields; curated requires a slice/slice_override scope. Returns (spec, None) on success or (spec, error_dict) on a rejected combination. This is the ONLY place agent view overrides are applied to a render_spec spec, so both render_spec sub-paths share ONE override+guard implementation.

Pure pre-order DFS that returns the FIRST node in a forest whose id/uuid matches -- the CANONICAL (unsorted) node lookup for the Scoped Lightning Rod occurrence-exact re-root pre-step in _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture. After the sorted forest is pruned to a clicked occurrence and that occurrence's LEAF UUIDs are collected, this locates the clicked node's canonical node in the UNSORTED captured forest so its subtree can be rebuilt DE-MIRRORED (filtered to those leaf UUIDs via build_selected_subtree_from_forest). Relies on the v1 invariant that a Workflowy UUID appears AT MOST ONCE in the raw (unsorted) tree -- Workflowy 'mirrors' are explicitly UNSUPPORTED in v1 -- so 'the first match' IS 'the only match'. Returns None if not found. The UUID (not object identity) is the ONLY valid bridge between the sorted shadow-copy tree and the canonical tree.

SLICE-BASE projection for a SLICE-FROZEN Scoped Lightning Rod. Deserializes the client's durable base_render_spec (RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob) and RE-PROJECTS that scope from the /nodes-export cache into a single render TREE, so _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture can then treat it EXACTLY like a DOM captured_tree (same re-root pre-step, same build_selected_subtree_from_forest filter, same _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture compose). It REUSES the canonical funnels -- build_stage1_base_tree for a slice / slice_override scope (via the SAME nested get_slice_group_config Direction-A read the sibling _handle_render_slice_modal uses), and build_slice_subtree_from_cache(member_all=True) for a raw_root scope -- and NEVER inlines a new projection. Returns (tree, None) on success or (None, error_dict) on any failure (no tab, no group, empty group, cache miss), so the caller replies verbatim. A lightning_rod base is rejected (a prior Lightning render is already ephemeral and arrives as captured_tree, never as a durable base spec). The projected tree is a first-class EPHEMERAL dom_capture from the caller onward -- the one-way collapse of the slice, NEVER re-laundered into a durable spec. STAGE-1 POLICY THREADING (post-Sol-audit Finding 3): spec.exclude_completed and spec.descend_policy's shared anchor boundary now reach the projection -- they were silently dropped before, so a frozen scope's Scoped re-projection could surface completed nodes and descend through child anchors the original render excluded.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD over a FROZEN DOM view (action=render_lightning_dom_capture). The DOM-frozen half of the Scoped toggle: the dock is showing an EPHEMERAL captured DOM forest and the user fired a Lightning Rod with [Scoped] ON, so the search is confined to that on-screen forest rather than walking the whole cache root. Reads the frame's captured_tree + opaque lightning selection {mode, tags?, query?, query_mode?, match_scope, postfix_policy?}; builds the SAME singular predicate the cache path uses (build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) and filters the forest via build_selected_subtree_from_forest; then composes through the EXISTING _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture machinery via its pre_filter seam, so the artifact stays a first-class kind='dom_capture' (EPHEMERAL -- the client provenance adapter must never launder it into a durable RenderProjectionSpec). gather short-circuits to gather_tags_in_forest -> render_tags_outline (raw_text/root_only), the forest sibling of the cache gather seam. No cache walk, no slice config; render_symbols is NOT supported here (it is inherently a cache-resolution mode). postfix_policy='slice' is LOUD-REJECTED in v1 (ap:IMPPTX): the full Stage-1 funnel hydrates expansions from the raw /nodes-export cache, which would silently graft nodes from OUTSIDE the ephemeral frozen domain (a source-correct forest hydrator is a separate future feature). The rejection now runs BEFORE any source-fork projection (post-Sol-audit Finding 4), so an unsupported request fails with its own actionable error -- never masked by a config/projection failure and never after wasted projection work. Task-dispatched like the sibling modal handlers. A malformed query fails LOUD (lightning_rod_query_error); an empty match renders an empty dom_capture document (valid 'no matches'), never an error.

The DOM-FROZEN sibling of _glimpse_dispatch_spec for render_spec="modal". It does NOT use the cache-projection path, because a frozen DOM view is a DIFFERENT SOURCE AXIS: an EPHEMERAL captured tree the tab pinned at freeze, not a durable /nodes-export scope. It composes that captured tree through the SAME composer + row-identity + focus primitives the cache path uses: normalize the {root,children} payload to one forest; prepare_stage2_render_forest for sort/since/counts (curated since is rejected -- no slice tags); then the shared materializer. TWO deliberate departures from the cache tail: (1) focus is EXACT-OR-ERROR -- an unresolvable focus triple returns a loud stale error, not the lenient whole-document fallback; (2) full/UUID mode is supported ONLY with headings_only=True (the {UUID<->title} harvest; a full body dump is rejected). The render_scope echo is honest kind='dom_capture' (durable_scope=False, live_gui_sync_supported=False) -- it never masquerades as raw_root/slice. GUARDRAIL: the captured tree is never folded into a RenderProjectionSpec. ADVISORY PROVENANCE (S04 Remediation Chain 4): the hard-barrier read advisory is a cache-provenance claim applied ONLY when the composed content is /nodes-export-derived -- the cache_sourced kwarg (default False, this function composes browser-captured trees) is carried explicitly to the ONE advisory authority; the render_spec="modal" dom_captured_tree read and genuinely DOM-frozen Scoped Lightning are unadvised, while a slice-frozen Scoped run passes cache_sourced=True and stays advised.

THE render_spec="modal" path -- the primary 'GLIMPSE what I'm looking at in the docked modal' capability. Issues ONE Direction-A get_current_modal_render_spec WS query to the target tab via the generic _ws_request_response rail (request_id correlation; the tab answers from its OWN dockedSliceContext.render_spec + selected-row triple -- a LEAF query, NO nested back-to-tab round trip, so NO deadlock-note applies). Deserializes the reply's render_spec blob into a RenderProjectionSpec via from_render_spec_blob (the SAME normalizer every entry point uses), applies UUID prefix-grace to every UUID in the spec (root + focus triple) via _grace_resolve_spec_uuids against the /nodes-export cache, then dispatches by kind through _glimpse_dispatch_spec -> the existing focused-projection helpers. DETERMINISTIC end-to-end: the agent types ZERO UUIDs (the blob comes from the tab's own server-adopted scope), and SERVER code (not the agent) deserializes + re-projects, so this is the (b)-variant architecture Dan chose -- the Python composer stays the sole renderer, no client-string round-trips through the server. Fails loudly if the tab has no cache-sourced render to report (success:false + a clear message telling the human to Apply a slice / push a scope first).

THE ONE agent-facing output-contract finalizer for the GLIMPSE FAMILY of MCP tools -- its consumers are the glimpse family (workflowy_glimpse), lightning_rod, anchor.dock.render, and slice_group render/sift/merge.render. Given the rich internal result dict every render helper builds, it delivers to the AGENT exactly what the human wants to see -- and nothing redundant. Rule: (1) output_file set -> pass the file-write summary through unchanged (the disk write is the deliverable, not the string). (2) result is not a dict -> already a bare value, pass through. (3) MARKDOWN / RAW-TEXT mode -- a RENDERED TEXT STRING is present -> return it RAW (real newlines, like read_text_file), NOTHING ELSE: preview_markdown (every Markdown-mode render across GLIMPSE live-DOM / slice_group / raw root_uuid / render_spec modal+blob / dom_capture, AND Lightning Rod render_tags/render_search/render_symbols) OR preview_text (the Lightning Rod gather raw-text tag outline, byte-identical to the modal's Gather). The rendered string IS the whole semantic payload in this mode, so no envelope is wanted. This is the single future-proof seam: ANY future raw-text mode just fills preview_text (or preview_markdown) and is delivered raw with ZERO further change here. (4) FULL / UUID mode -- a preview_tree is present -> return the STRUCTURED DICT, preserving preview_tree AND all the genuinely-useful metadata (node_count, depth, _source, render_scope, since_applied, ...), but STRIPPING ONLY the redundant CONTENT twins: `rows` (modal tree-view metadata that duplicates preview_tree) and any stray preview_markdown/preview_text; additionally, when headings_only=True (the compact UUID-harvest pass), strip bulky live-DOM raw `root`/`children` to keep the payload small. Full mode is for structural / UUID work, so the stats ARE wanted here -- only the duplicative rows/markdown clutter is dropped. (5) everything else (errors success:false, push_to_modal acks, gather's structured tag list when preview_text is somehow absent, empty payloads with neither field) -> pass the structured dict through unchanged so failures/acks still signal correctly. The rich internal payloads (rows, render_scope, since_applied, node_count) are LEFT INTACT on the helper returns -- they still flow to the browser/modal WS reply handlers that need them; this finalizer only shapes the AGENT-facing tool return. preview_markdown is checked before preview_text before preview_tree: at most one is ever populated on a given result, so order is belt-and-suspenders. STALE-FOCUS GUARD [ap:XDVDRG]: a Markdown/raw-text result that carries focus_unresolved is NEVER delivered raw -- its always-empty string would read as a legitimately empty view; the structured stale payload is returned instead (success flipped to false, the empty preview twins and modal rows dropped, error + focus_unresolved kept) so the shared family error boundary surfaces the loud stale-focus error. F3/F2 ancestor-chain WS handler: virtual-UUID (mirror) parsing, /nodes-export cache fetch + dirty-ID advisory, shaped error frames — but the walk and the WHOLE Markdown grammar are delegated to ancestor_path.build_ancestor_path_document, the ONE shared core the node.ancestors MCP verb also calls, so the hotkey and the verb can never drift. The document carries dock.peek-vocabulary right-side markers (⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓ + ▸N/desc/self/tree metrics) plus the 🗺️ mapped-folder / 📄 mapped-file markers with the key at the top, so this handler reads the configured Dock vocabulary via a nested get_extension_settings Direction-A read — which is why websocket_handler TASK-dispatches it (an inline await would deadlock the pump, the list_anchors_for_widget reason).

Derive a safe .md filename from a Workflowy node name for F12+4 materialize. Strips leading decoration/emoji, trailing #tags, illegal filename chars; collapses whitespace to underscores; guarantees a non-empty stem and a .md extension.

F12+4 leading-text fix: if the note's body (after optional YAML frontmatter) starts with prose BEFORE the first Markdown heading, synthesize a leading '# Leading text' H1 above that prose so the pre-heading text is not lost when the note is split into a heading subtree. No-op when the body already opens with a heading or is empty.

F12+4 hygiene: strip a LEADING Cartographer metadata block (MD_PATH: … --- or BEACON (…) … ---) from a node's note before materializing it to a .md. Needed because a Dump-Bay child that was already written back to the primary file via F12+3 carries such a block at the top of its note; without stripping it, that metadata would be written into the new .md as body content (and then split into bogus child nodes). Mirrors markdown_roundtrip._strip_md_path_block / _strip_md_ast_beacon_block but kept local to avoid importing module privates.

Bulk F12+4 helper: classify a node's note as a Cartographer FILE/FOLDER header. Returns ('Root'|'Path', value) or None using the strict first-line-only _extract_path_header_from_note. A folder/path node has a header whose value has no recognized file extension; a file node's value has one (e.g. .md/.py).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a Markdown file (.md/.markdown)? Used by the bulk walk + eligibility classifier to decide whether to recurse INTO a file node (markdown -> yes; any other extension -> skip+prune).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a FILE (has a filename extension) rather than a FOLDER segment? A folder node's Path: is a bare segment (no dot-extension); a file node's Path: ends in an extension. Used to distinguish path/folder nodes (recurse through) from file nodes (skip unless .md). Thin wrapper: the canonical implementation now lives in api_client_nexus (single source of truth, co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note + _classify_node_map_state); imported here via a function-scoped local import to avoid the api_client_nexus->server cycle, mirroring the other unguarded server->client local imports. NO inline fallback copy on purpose: a bool predicate has no safe 'unknown' value (returning False would mislabel a real file node as a folder and misroute the F12 menus), and if api_client_nexus is unimportable the whole server is non-functional anyway -- so we let the import raise loudly rather than keep a divergent second copy of the logic.

FIRST server-queried F12 menu-visibility check. Walks UP the nodes-export cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof, unlike the DOM) to classify the hovered node, then combines that with the client-reported visible/hidden child booleans to decide whether the F12+4 entry appears and which bulk sub-options enable. Returns {show, mode, visible_option_enabled, all_option_enabled, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+4 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_materialize). Reads node_id + has_visible_children/has_hidden_children from the payload, runs _classify_bulk_materialize_eligibility, and echoes the verdict back (with node_id for client-side correlation).

Zoom-proof resolver for F12+3: given ANY node_id, walk UP the /nodes-export cache ancestor chain (which never hides anything, unlike the zoomed-in DOM) to find the enclosing Markdown FILE node. If the node itself IS a markdown FILE node, returns it. Crucially IGNORES the md-in-md temp node's SECOND-line Path: (that node is never a reverse-Markdown target); the true primary file is the enclosing markdown FILE ancestor. Returns the FILE node's UUID, or None when no enclosing markdown file exists (e.g. inside a non-markdown file, or no file at all).

Cache-backed (zoom-proof) eligibility classifier for the BULK F12+3 menu entry. Decision tree is SIMPLER than F12+4 (no submenu for availability, no child-visibility input needed to decide SHOW): a markdown FILE node -> single F12+3 (mode='single', no bulk entry); a node INSIDE a mapped file -> no bulk entry (degenerates to standard single F12+3 on the enclosing file, which the server resolves zoom-safely); any node that is NOT a file node and NOT inside a file (a folder/Root: node OR a plain unmapped Workflowy node) -> bulk. Returns {show, mode, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+3 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_f12p3). Reads node_id, runs _classify_bulk_f12p3_eligibility, echoes the verdict {show,mode,reason,classification} back (with node_id for client-side correlation). No child-visibility input is needed (F12+3 bulk has no availability submenu).

Bulk F12+3 collection walk (source-agnostic, mirrors _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves plumbing). DFS over a tree (client visible-DOM payload OR nodes-export cache subtree) gathering MARKDOWN FILE nodes only. Per-node rules: a markdown FILE node QUALIFIES and we do NOT descend into it (F12+3 regenerates the whole file from its Workflowy subtree); a non-markdown FILE node is skipped+pruned; folder/Root: nodes and plain nodes are recursed THROUGH. Uses the universal first-line-only header classifier, so a md-in-md temp node (Path on line 2) is never mistaken for a file node. Returns ordered list of {id,name} file-node descriptors.

Bulk F12+3 execution handler (action=bulk_generate_markdown). Performs ONE gesture-level /nodes-export freshness read (L9 GESTURE) before any cache walk or child launch, builds the tree (walk_mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; 'all' -> cache subtree via _build_cache_subtree_for_bulk_materialize), runs _collect_bulk_f12p3_markdown_file_nodes to gather every Markdown FILE node, then fires ONE INDEPENDENT detached _start_carto_markdown_generate_job per file (N widget status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan). Every child consumes the one shared gesture snapshot and admits/claims its own region independently; this handler does not block.

WebSocket handler for the docked-modal SERVER render (action=render_markdown_modal). Direction-A request_id rail: composes Markdown STRING(s) on the server from a DOM/captured-tree payload: snapshot -> all row option-Y views, rows_only -> server-authored row list only, single -> one focus_leaf row, rows -> frozen-DOM multi-select minimal covering subtree via _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture. Echoes request_id. Never forces a /nodes-export refresh (detect+warn staleness). TASK-DISPATCHED from the reader loop (U4), and the three SYNCHRONOUS compose_markdown_modal_* calls run via asyncio.to_thread so a large compose cannot monopolize the event loop -- the task's S03 operation-boundary snapshot propagates into the thread (contextvars).

WebSocket handler for the slice-group copy button (action=compile_slice_search). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id). TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) so it can do a NESTED Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the ORIGINATING tab without deadlocking the single websocket_handler pump. Reads the live slice-group config from that tab, resolves the requested group_id (or active group), and compiles the Workflowy membership search string via the single Python compiler compile_slice_search_expression (#P -#P--deprecated OR ...). Replies compile_slice_search_result with request_id + expression.

WebSocket handler for the live F8 keypress (action=f8_expansion_plan). Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id) carrying the visible DOM subtree. TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab to read the active slice group's prefixes + the live postfix config (one settings reader, no client-side policy). Then runs Phase 0 (validate_subtree_against_cache, fail-closed) and Phase 2 (build_expansion_plan) over the validated visible tree and replies f8_expansion_plan_result (echoing request_id) with {collapse_suppressed, collapse_deprecated, expand, warnings} for the client to execute mechanically. No fallback: on validation failure or no live tab it replies with an error the client surfaces loudly.

Apply-slice Tier-1 handler (action=render_slice_modal): the docked Markdown modal sourced from the CACHE-PROJECTED slice group instead of the live virtualized DOM. Browser-initiated correlated request (client-minted request_id); TASK-DISPATCHED (NOT inline) -- twin of _handle_f8_expansion_plan / _handle_compile_slice_search -- because it does the SAME nested Direction-A get_slice_group_config round-trip back to the originating tab, which would deadlock the single websocket_handler pump if awaited inline. Resolves the requested slice group (by group_id, else active), then runs the SHARED cache-projection funnel build_stage1_base_tree (Phase 1 build_slice_subtree_from_cache -> Phase 2 build_expansion_plan -> Phase 3 apply_expansion_plan_to_subtree -> Phase 4 prune_collapsed_leaf_zombies) -- the EXACT SAME funnel _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache calls, so the Apply-slice modal and the slice-group GLIMPSE can never diverge on the projection (incl. the Phase-4 render-only zombie prune, the deliberate divergence from the live Workflowy expansion state) -- then _build_markdown_preview_from_tree (the SAME shared composer the live-DOM modal uses) with the _root_in_non_md_file_from_cache seed. Returns ONE Markdown STRING that is complete BY CONSTRUCTION (cache-sourced, not virtualized), so the dock can display it with no scroll/F8/refresh-dance and the client suppresses the scroll-to-bottom warning (cache_sourced=true). Replies render_slice_modal_result echoing request_id so the broker routes it to ONLY the originating tab. | Build the stable STRING key for a tree-view row's (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple, used both to key the Apply-slice SNAPSHOT map server-side and (echoed by the client on a row click) to select the exact occurrence in the SINGLE per-row path. NUL-joined ancestor_path so it cannot collide with a uuid; occurrence suffixed. Deterministic + pure -- the same row produces the same key on the original render and on any re-projection (MATCH = EMIT).

Build the SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE render_scope echo object for a cache-projected render. This is the ONE object every consumer (client adoptRenderScope -> per-tab render state + ribbon widgets + footer; and the MCP push tool output) treats as the normalized ground truth of what was ACTUALLY rendered, regardless of which SURFACE (ribbon click or MCP glimpse() call) triggered the render. Carries ONLY the normalized structured render-defining fields: scope identity (kind/group_id/group_name/root_uuid) + view params (sort_by/sort_direction/since object-or-null/headings_only). There is no pre-composed display string -- the status footer is the ONE consumer that renders a human string, composing it from THESE fields, so string-composition lives in exactly one place. kind is 'slice' (group at its own root), 'slice_override' (group tags scoped to an override root), 'raw_root' (bare root_uuid raw dump, no group -> the footer labels it 'raw dump of <root8>'), or 'lightning_rod' (a temporary Lightning Rod selection via the `lightning` param, which takes PRECEDENCE). LIGHTNING SELECTION: a lightning render carries ONE opaque `selection` object {mode:'gather'|'render_tags'|'render_search'|'render_symbols', + per-mode fields (tags+postfix_policy | query/query_mode | symbols/root_uuids/favor) + match_scope} that the client round-trips VERBATIM for BEHAVIOR (routing is by selection.mode, never selection_kind). selection_kind ('gather'|'tags'|'search'|'symbols') + workflowy_search_equivalent are DERIVED from selection.mode and are DISPLAY-ONLY (footer/status-bar label). UNMOORED SIGNAL: live_gui_sync_supported is a TOP-LEVEL bool emitted for EVERY kind (+ live_gui_sync_skipped_reason naming why when False) -- False for a raw dump (no membership search), a descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' render (inexpressible as a Workflowy search), a search_too_many_variants refusal, or any lightning selection; the client surfaces the unmoored state on the yellow bar. It is DISPLAY/observability only, never a behavior driver. EVERY kind also carries the explicit CONTENT/TREE CONTRACT fields content_format ('markdown'|'raw_text') + tree_mode ('render_tree'|'root_only') so the client never guesses how to paint the one rendered string or populate the top-half list (only a lightning GATHER is raw_text/root_only today). Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

old_result.comment: Phase-E1 SPEC-AWARE BRIDGE to the ONE render_scope composer. Given a RESOLVED RenderProjectionSpec (kind/root/group already canonicalized by the caller's resolution step -- NOT the raw incoming spec), DELEGATE to _compose_render_scope by unpacking exactly the scalar params it already takes (Option A, Dan-decided: delegate, do NOT reimplement from spec.to_render_scope_fields(), so there stays ONE render_scope-assembly implementation and this never becomes a second scope factory / caller-side fabrication site). The is_raw_dump / root_overridden booleans the scalar composer wants are read straight off the spec's kind-derived properties (spec.is_raw_dump / spec.root_overridden), and sort_by is passed via spec.sort_by_internal() (the ONE wire-'none'<->internal-None translation). search_too_many_variants is a POST-RENDER fact (not a spec input field, per invariant 5) so it is threaded as an explicit kwarg here, exactly as the scalar composer already accepts it. This is the E1 seam that lets every downstream server call site (modal handler E3, content-return GLIMPSE paths E4, push frame E5) compose render_scope FROM the same spec it projected from, instead of from a parallel bag of locals -- the two-parallel-assembly-points seam Phase E removes. Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

The ONE inherited slice-group root policy seam shared by MCP/lens renders and every stored-root consumer (APPLY, copy-search, named merge, scoped reprojection, push and group purge). Delegates resolution to resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle with the caller's pinned map; exact UUIDs, clean prefixes including 8 hex, and AP-IDs are adopted with existing archive semantics. Corrective UUID shaves are rejected and only their speculative correction echo is discarded. Transport, scope notes and miss envelopes stay per-origin; explicit input roots keep the standard forgiving boundary.

PURE formatter for the ambiguous/missing error ENVELOPE returned by the cache-projection root_uuid resolution sites (the bare-root RAW-DUMP GLIMPSE, the slice-group override root, the push scope root, and Lightning Rod). Given a resolve_uuid_like_node_handle result that did NOT resolve (candidates present => ambiguous; else => missing), returns the standard {success:False, error, [candidates/matched_prefix_len/truncated], **extra} dict -- so the several sites can't DRIFT on the field set. Deliberately NOT a resolver wrapper: each caller keeps its own resolution and control flow (plain return vs await _reply) and its own error WORDING (via display/label); this only unifies the payload SHAPE. Chain-1 W4 (F5): in the MISSING branch, a refusal-reason operation (a sink, a write, an export, a purge preview) whose root names a visible archived node RAISES ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the exact §5.2/§5.3 text and provenance — before any file/modal/preview work; reads (reason None/flag) and no-context callers keep today's hint-only text. Returns None when the handle actually resolved (caller should not call it then). Pure; no I/O.

ONE handler for every cache-projected docked-modal render + per-row re-render (the 'Apply slice' feature). Resolves the four-cell scope truth table: slice (group_id), slice_override (group_id+root_uuid), raw_root (root_uuid only), lightning_rod (lightning{mode,...}; group-less, Phase-1-only via an injected member_predicate BY DEFAULT -- render_tags + postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) upgrades the cell to the shared build_stage1_base_tree funnel with one nested postfix config read). Lightning modes: gather (short-circuits to the raw-text tag outline), render_tags{tags} (DEFAULT: no config read; 'slice': one nested postfix config read), render_search{query,query_mode} (both scope via one frame root_uuid), and render_symbols{symbols,root_uuids,favor} (the tag-free beacon slice: roots via its own root_uuids -> their LCA, does one nested config read for the global-suppression filter, resolves via the shared _project_render_symbols_from_cache, and appends its unresolved/ambiguous report to the full-document reply), plus render_lens{lens,query?} (the recursive LensSpec cell: one nested config read, the shared immutable Stage-0 snapshot + transport-free _project_render_lens_from_cache, derived-LCA rooting, and explicit empty artifact). All five modes emit one opaque `selection` object into the render_scope. Then runs the shared projection -> prepare_stage2_render_forest -> rows -> snapshot-vs-single machinery and echoes the server-authoritative render_scope.

Bulk F12+4 qualification walk (source-agnostic). DFS over a tree (fed EITHER by the client visible-DOM payload OR the nodes-export cache subtree) applying the rules: recurse THROUGH folder/path nodes; into .md file nodes; SKIP+prune non-md file nodes; never qualify a node with children; qualify a childless non-path/non-file node iff its note (leading metadata block stripped) parses to >=1 markdown heading via _note_body_has_heading. Returns the ordered list of qualifying leaf descriptors.

Bulk F12+4 (mode B, recurse-all-incl-hidden) tree source: build a nested {id,name,note,children[]} subtree rooted at root_uuid directly from the /nodes-export cache, ignoring Workflowy expansion state entirely (like F12+3's synthetic-tree path). Returns the root node dict, or None if root not in cache.

Bulk F12+4 filename assignment. ONE accumulating pass over the full qualifying-leaf set: derive each leaf's stem (FILEBASE-ancestor prefix + sanitized node name, same logic as single-node F12+4) and resolve collisions against BOTH on-disk files AND already-assigned in-set names (siblings can share identical markdown headings). The in-set reservation makes prior leaves act as though already on disk so the integer-suffix increment is race-free and deterministic.

Bulk F12+4 execution handler (action=bulk_materialize_markdown). Builds the tree (mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; mode='all' -> cache subtree), runs _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves, assigns collision-safe filenames across the whole in-memory set FIRST (single accumulating process, race-free), then for EACH qualifying leaf writes the metadata-stripped note to its .md, sets the node note (Path: header for persist, dummy MD_PATH: block for in-md-file persist, or clears for temp), patches the snapshot, and fires an INDEPENDENT detached F12+1 job per leaf (N status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan).

Browser-initiated UUID Explorer anchor-list convenience endpoint. TASK-DISPATCHED because it delegates to the SAME list_anchors MCP tool wrapper, which performs a nested Direction-A get_extension_settings read; awaiting inline would deadlock the websocket pump. Replies list_anchors_for_widget_result with the exact list_anchors payload (global anchors only; local anchors suppressed by the shared server path) plus request_id for broker/tab correlation. Client formats it as UUID/name text and copies/displays it; no client-side anchor enumeration logic.

The ONE module-level coroutine the WS reader loop spawns (via create_isolated_context_task) for the long handlers whose inline failure frame was the generic {action, success:false, node_id, error} shape, instead of awaiting the handler inline: the two F12 refresh actions and (since U4) open_node_in_windsurf / materialize_markdown_file / bulk_materialize_markdown / bulk_generate_markdown. Awaits handler(data, websocket) inside the same try/except the inline clauses carried (log_event error line, then the best-effort failure frame), so the pump keeps servicing frames while a handler runs and a failed spawned handler still reports exactly as before.
